jobs.description:
Who We Are

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.

The Opportunity

Oportun is currently seeking qualified candidates with customer service, cashier, sales, or hospitality experience to work Full-Time. At Oportun, we consider our customers to be our members, and the primary focus of our store-based teams is to create and generate a rewarding and unique member service experience.

As a Store Team Lead, you will be responsible for overseeing the daily operations of a single store and ensuring consistent, high-quality member service and sales. You will supervise and coach a team of Member Loyalty Representatives (MLRs) to meet and exceed sales goals and ensure that everyone on the team is complying with company processes and procedures, including Oportun sales practices.

In this role, you will also be responsible for listening, helping, and connecting with people at all touchpoints, such as in our stores and in the communities around our stores through personal outreach activities. As a key member of our team, you will make the mission of Oportun come to life by educating our members and communities about our inclusive, affordable financial services that empower them to build a better future.

What You'll Do

Your day-to-day

• Welcome members with a warm greeting and provide quality member service

• Seamlessly process all transactions, while following company policies & procedures and protecting our members’ information.

• Respond to member inquiries or complaints with empathy, escalating issues as needed, involving store personnel or member experience to the appropriate senior leadership or HR personnel

• Work as a team or independently, including time alone in the store without direct supervision or with coworkers, while exceeding daily goals in our lending and servicing activities

• Enjoy informing and educating potential members about Oportun’s services by engaging in outreach efforts more than 50% of the time at Oportun locations, partner locations, and/or community events. Activities include: Plan and execute targeted outreach and promotional activities, including researching locations and venues to promote our products and services. Schedule and manage in-store promotional activities Building relationships with local businesses (e.g., mechanic shops, dental offices, furniture stores) and speaking with local business owners and their employees about how Oportun’s services can help their customers. Conducting outreach efforts at local flea markets, community events, and at our Lending As A Service (LAAS) partner locations to increase awareness capture leads, and assist with starting applications; Actively engaging with people at and around Oportun’s retail locations, encouraging store visits, and assisting with applications. Supporting community outreach and marketing events, by passing out flyers and educating the local community about Oportun and its products and services; and Using iPads or assisting potential members with scanning QR codes during outreach efforts to start new applications.

• Proactively identify opportunities to improve store performance

• Inspire team to take responsibility for achieving store objectives

• Light housekeeping to keep the work area and store location inviting and presentable to all who visit, including daily collection of trash, sweeping, mopping, and window cleaning as needed.

• Use a computer intermittently (approx. 3-6 hours per day) for administrative tasks and for servicing members.

• Stand while assisting members, sitting is allowed during non-member-facing tasks

• Occasionally unpack and store office or cleaning supplies.

• Must have the ability to travel between designated work locations (including outreach activities) within a reasonable commuting distance as part of standard job duties. Travel will be limited to sites considered part of an ordinary commute.

• Be a role model for Oportun's Core Values: On a Mission, As One, to Make It Better, Now

Who You Are

The right fit looks like this

You're comfortable navigating complexity and don't wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, and expect the same in return.

• Must be outgoing, sales-focused, and enjoy speaking with people.

• Must love to help members, including prospective members through outreach and educational activities.

What You Bring

Skills & experience

Required

• Must be bilingual (English/Spanish).

• Proficient in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint)

• 2+ years of sales experience and 1+ year of proven retail leadership experience as a team lead or supervisor, with a focus on people management, sales, and operations

• Must be available to work weekends and be flexible with a rotating work schedule of hours based on store needs. Schedules are set every two weeks.

• Must have regular, reliable, and predictable attendance to support store operations.

• Ability to lift and/or move objects up to 25 pounds, as needed

• Basic computer skills and ability to operate office equipment such as phones, scanners, and iPads.

• Ability to organize and file paper documents.

Nice to Have

• banking experience is a plus

Compensation

The base hourly rate for this full-time position is $24.00- $28.00.

Our hourly rates are determined by role, location and experience. The hourly range displayed on each job posting reflects a minimum and maximum for new hire rates for this position, specific to the location of this job posting.

Please note that the compensation details listed in this posting reflects only the hourly rate for this position and does not include other compensation elements or benefits.

Why Oportun

What's in it for you

Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. Benefits vary by country of employment.

As a Valuable Member of Our Team, You’ll Receive

• Opportunity to positively impact your community

This is a summary of select benefits and does not represent the full benefits package. Eligibility and plan details vary by location and employment status. To learn more about Oportun and our benefits, visit oportun.com/careers

Our AI Mindset

We build with AI. We lead with judgment.

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work.

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting, willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle.

In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together.

jobs.title: Summer Travel Camp Director, Chicago Region (2027)
jobs.description:
Galileo is looking for an experienced leader to join our team as a Travel Camp Director. Travel Camp Directors support multiple summer camps for K–8th grade across region, stepping in for Camp Directors or Assistant Camp Directors during absences or when extra support is needed. Reporting to your Field Program Manager, you'll keep operations running smoothly, mentor staff, and create joyful, safe, and inspiring camp experience.

You’ll bring Galileo’s mission to life—fostering creativity, innovation, and fun—while managing daily logistics, camper behavior, and team culture. You may be assigned a home camp or rotate between sites as needed. Responsibilities also include family communication, staff onboarding, timecard approval, compliance, and upholding camp policies.

Why This Role Matters

Galileo started in 2002 with a single summer camp in Palo Alto, named for Galileo Galilei, one of history’s great innovators. Today we run 90+ sites across eight states, and Camp Directors are still the people who give each camp its own traditions and magic. Our mission is to develop innovators who envision and create a better world, and at camp, you’re the one who makes that real for campers, families, and staff every day.

You will be Accountable for

Bringing Galileo’s Spirit to Life

• Infuse camp with joy, tradition, and creativity

• Build an inclusive environment where every camper, staff member, and family feels seen, supported, and inspired

Leading with Ownership and Vision

• Own every aspect of your camp’s launch, from preseason planning through end-of-summer wrap-up

• As both operational lead and culture builder, oversee every detail from daily camp operations to parent communication while delivering an exceptional program

Keeping Camp Safe and Running Smoothly

• Prioritize camper safety, family trust, and program fidelity at all times

• Anticipate needs, adapt quickly, and problem-solve on the fly so camp runs seamlessly, even when things don’t go as planned

Developing and Managing Your Team

• Train and mentor a staff of 7 to 40 (depending on site size), including educators and entry-level staff, while actively building your team culture

• Provide clear expectations for instructional and program standards, ongoing feedback, and professional development

• Own core management responsibilities such as training support, scheduling, payroll, and ongoing performance management

Embracing Challenge and Innovation

• Use the Galileo Innovation Approach (GIA) to encourage curiosity and problem-solving

• Lead your team in turning challenges into opportunities, keeping both spirit and operations aligned to Galileo’s mission

• Communicate openly with your Field Program Manager, seek out feedback, and turn it into action

• Take ownership of your own professional development, staying self-motivated to learn, grow, and improve throughout the summer

Building Strong Partnerships

• Serve as the primary face of camp within the community

• Communicate proactively with families, facilities partners, and cross-functional teams

• Collaborate with your Field Program Manager and cultivate trust with community partners, staff, and campers

Location & Work Schedule:

This is a seasonal role running March–September 2027, with a schedule divided into three phases. Exact dates will vary based on hire date and specific site operating dates:

• Phase One: Training & Prep (March–June): 5 to 15 hours per week, depending on tenure and start date — mostly flexible and remote, with some required scheduled and in-person commitments. This phase includes in-person training(s), a Bay Area retreat, scheduled virtual training(s), marketing events, and on-site prep at your camp location during the week leading up to camp. Some events may take place during evenings and weekends.

• Phase Two: On-Site (June–August): On-site hours typically range from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM (M-F), up to 50 hours per week over 5–8 weeks, depending on camp placement.

• Phase Three: Wrap-Up (Aug–Sept): Up to 5 hrs total, remote, for final admin tasks and staff reviews.

Compensation:

(Year 1 estimate):

• Preseason (Feb–June): Earn hourly pay ($22-24/hour) for flexible, part-time prep and training

• Camp Season (June–Aug): Transition to a weekly salary ($1,400/week plus an additional $50/week for each year of returning tenure in this role) as a full-time, exempt Camp Director during summer operations

• Postseason (Aug–Sept): Wrap up with light part-time work, paid hourly ($22-24/hour)

• Bonus/Commission: Earn an additional $1 per camper-week enrollment, plus potential commission for add-on weeks

Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and Galileo camp director tenure. Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Perks:

• Free camp for your child(ren) or two giftable weeks (incl. extended care)

• 15% Friends & Family discount

• Priority nomination for financial assistance for someone you know

• 3+ years of experience working directly with students in an education setting (out-of-school time, teaching, education administration, camps/recreation, etc.) is required

• Minimum 1 year of experience managing or supervising adult staff is required

• Proven experience creating safe, inclusive environments for children and building trust with families

• Proven experience setting clear expectations, giving ongoing feedback, and coaching staff to improve

• Demonstrated ability to manage operational details like scheduling, staffing, and payroll

• Track record of staying calm and making sound decisions in fast-paced situations, including safety issues and challenging conversations with families

• Strong written and verbal communication with families, partners, and supervisors

• Experience with hands-on, project-based learning (STEAM, art, design, maker programs) is a plus

• Availability for part-time remote work starting March 2027, and full-time on-site work starting June 2027 (dates vary by location)

• Willingness to travel in the region to up to 3 in person marketing events, in the preseason

• Ability to complete all required training before camp begins

• Ability to meet state requirements to work with children, including mandated screenings and Adult & Child First Aid/CPR/AED certification

The base hourly rate for this full-time position is $24.00- $28.00.

Why Oportun

What's in it for you

Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. Benefits vary by country of employment.

What You'll Do

• Support the development and execution of integrated media plans across digital, social, search, programmatic, endemic, and other healthcare media channels.

• Track campaign pacing, delivery, and key milestones, escalating risks or discrepancies when identified.

• Support client and publisher billing processes, budget reconciliations, invoice tracking, and financial documentation in partnership with Business Operations.

• Build campaigns and maintain records within Mediaocean Prisma and other planning and campaign management platforms.

• Coordinate meetings, capture notes, track action items, and ensure timely follow-up across internal and external teams.

• Learn the client's business, brand objectives, customer audiences, and therapeutic area landscape to support increasingly strategic contributions.

This Position is a Perfect Fit for You If

• Our values of Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I" align with how you work.

• You are highly organized and thrive when juggling multiple projects and deadlines.

• You are curious about media, marketing, customer engagement, and how healthcare brands reach and influence audiences.

• You proactively ask questions, seek feedback, and continuously look for opportunities to learn and grow.

• You enjoy collaborating across disciplines and building strong relationships with teammates and partners.

• You embrace new technologies, including AI-powered tools, and are excited by innovation within media and marketing.

What You Should Have

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 0-2 years of experience in media, advertising, marketing, communications, or an agency environment.

• Understanding of digital media, campaign planning, or marketing fundamentals.

• Pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences experience is a plus.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

• Excellent written, verbal, and organizational communication skills.

• Proficiency with Excel, PowerPoint, and Google Slides.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong problem-solving skills and willingness to take ownership of assigned work.

• Desire to build a career in media planning, customer engagement, and healthcare marketing.

Pay Range: $50,000-$63,000 + overtime

jobs.title: IT Technician
jobs.description:
About Us

Fashion Nova is one of the fastest-growing e-commerce brands in the world. In 2018, we were named the #1 most-searched fashion brand on Google. Since then, we have continued to grow, launching Fashion Nova CARES, NovaKIDS, Nova Beauty, and Maven Beauty. Even more amazing launches are in the works as we speak!

At Fashion Nova, we are dedicated to bringing the customer the latest trends to make them look and feel their best without the high price point. We deliver the hottest styles at lightning-fast speed, ensuring that all are included with FashionNovaCURVE and NovaMEN. Wherever our customer is, we are committed to bringing them the trends they love at the prices they love.

About the Role

Fashion Nova is seeking a hands-on IT Technician to deliver exceptional white-glove technical support to our corporate teams. You'll troubleshoot hardware, software, and enterprise applications, collaborate with IT teams to resolve issues, and support technology deployments and company-wide initiatives.

We're looking for a proactive, solutions-driven professional who can hit the ground running, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and help continuously improve our IT support experience.

Responsibilities

• Support Apple and Windows end users across the enterprise using Jira Service Desk ticketing system.

• Support Zoom Communication services including: Zoom phone, Zoom Rooms, Zoom Softphone and all related presentation AV services.

• Support the entire Fashion Nova user community with their mobility devices including iPhones and tablets.

• Create documentation for the Service Desk staff for planning, implementing, testing, rolling out upgrades, updates and replacement hardware to the enterprise.

• System imaging process to replicate Windows hardware configurations.

• Hardware refreshes for multiple platforms.

• Assist in the evaluation and selection process for all Service Desk tools during end-of-life agreements for each tool and the renewal or replacement of such services.

• Perform ongoing support operations and continuously refine end user documentation.

• Tend to the incoming requests via the ticketing system to address problems and resolve issues in a timely manner with limited disruption.

• Achieve support SLA’s “Mean Time to Resolve” (MTTR).

• Help cross train staff and increase productivity through positive reinforcement and hands on teachings.

• Document key application functions, admin processes and report on service status.

• Escalate support issues to vendors, follow up and resolve them in a timely manner.

• Proficient in scripting and performing mass deployments (updates and security patching).

• Partner with other business functions to evaluate, prioritize and resolve new issues & problem scenarios.

• Collaborate with other technical and functional teams to document and support business rules, system operating procedures.

Required Skills

• Preferred degree in Computer Science, Engineering or related discipline or equivalent education and experience.

• Must have knowledge of at least 80% of the following applications from day one: One Log In, Gmail, Zoom, Jira, Slack, Mosyle, Mobility Knowledge, Mas360, AD, JAMF, Intune, & Trend Micro

• 5+ years of experience supporting Windows and Apple operating systems.

• 3+ years related experience in imaging Windows systems.

• Strong understanding of best practice IT Service Management including the ITIL framework.

• Experience with scripting and automation tools (a Plus)

• Must be able to create effective documents, systems operating procedures & FAQs

• Must be able to diligently work under short deadlines and be able to keep composure at all times.

• Must be a self-starter with great initiative and drive which requires minimal supervision.

• Strong speaking and presentation skills to deliver end user training along with white glove style support.

• System administration and IT certifications in Linux, Microsoft, or other network related fields are a plus.

• Working knowledge of virtualization, VMWare, or equivalent.

• Strong knowledge of systems and networking software, hardware, and networking protocols.

• Audio Video skills – projection, audio, recording and editing a plus.

Benefits

• Employee Discount

• Medical, Dental and Vision Coverage

• 401k Match

• Kitchen stocked with snacks and drinks

• Weekly catered food, fun events, raffles and free FN swag

• Summer Fridays at HQ

• Company Sponsored Parties

• Team bonding events and programs to strengthen relationships with co-workers

Fashion Nova, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse workplace environment.

jobs.description:
Are you driven to grow, lead, and make a meaningful impact? At Apex, we’re building more than a consulting and engineering firm—we’re creating a place where your career accelerates, your contributions matter, and your potential is fully realized. We believe your growth is our growth, which is why we invest in your development at every stage of your career. Here, you’ll work on projects that shape communities, protect the environment, and create lasting impact, all while being empowered with the autonomy and flexibility to do your best work.

Fueled by high-quality delivery, exceptional client retention, and strategic acquisitions, Apex Companies continues to rank among the fastest-growing firms in the AEC industry, recently recognized by the Zweig Group for our industry-leading growth. Our success is grounded in strong leadership, a collaborative culture, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional outcomes.

As we continue to expand, we're looking for high-performing professionals who are ready to lead, collaborate, innovate, and create impact. At Apex, you help shape what's next. When we succeed together, we share in that success. All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

Position Summary: The Collection Analyst is responsible for supporting the timely collection of outstanding client invoices, maintaining accurate collection records, and partnering with internal teams and clients to resolve payment issues. This role supports cash flow management by proactively monitoring receivables, communicating with clients and project teams, and ensuring follow-up activities are completed in accordance with established collection processes. This position will support the East Business Units and must be willing to work Eastern Time Zone hours.

Your Responsibilities as a Collection Analyst:

• Manage the collections for one of the four business units within Apex.

• Monitor assigned accounts receivable balances and identify past-due invoices requiring follow-up, per the client payment terms.

• Contact clients regarding outstanding balances, payment status, remittance details, and invoice questions.

• Collaborate with project managers, project accountants, and other internal teams to resolve collection matters.

• Record and review collection activity, client responses, payment commitments, and follow-up actions in the appropriate tracking tool.

• Identify, track and maintain payment portal access for applicable client accounts within the business unit.

• Review aging reports and prioritize collection efforts based on balance, age, risk, and business needs.

• Prepare collection updates, reports, and status summaries for management review.

• Support recurring collection meetings by providing account updates, recommended next steps, and follow-up status.

• Escalate high-risk accounts, delinquent balances, or unresolved disputes to management in a timely manner.

• Maintain professional client relationships while supporting timely payment and adherence to agreed payment terms.

• Support demand letter preparation, collection agency submissions, and other escalation procedures as directed.

• Support process improvements related to collections tracking, reporting, and client communication.

What we're looking for:

• An associate’s or bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field is preferred.

• Three or more years of experience in accounts receivable, collections, and customer service.

• Strong communication skills with the ability to interact professionally with clients and internal teams.

• Strong attention to detail when updating and maintaining customer account records.

• Ability to resolve complex payment issues.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a timely manner.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and accounting or ERP systems; experience with Deltek Vantagepoint is an advantage.

Core Competencies

• Committed to delivering exceptional customer service and building positive client relationships.

• Problem-solving skills to resolve issues effectively.

• Maintains a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.

• Handles financial information responsibly while maintaining confidentiality.

• Collaborates effectively with internal teams.

Success Measures

• Reduction in past-due accounts receivable for the assigned business unit.

• Timely and consistent follow-up on assigned past-due accounts.

• Accurate and complete documentation of collection activity.

• Effective coordination with internal teams to resolve payment issues.

• Professional communication with clients that supports relationships and timely payment.

Why you'll love working for us:

• Company-subsidized medical and dental.

• Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.

• 401k match, tuition assistance, and more.

• Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.

• Performance-based bonuses or other incentives.

• Working with the best and brightest in the industry.

• 2,000+ employee national firm with 50+ locations across the US.

jobs.title: Director of Growth
jobs.description:
ABOUT DARKROOM

Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.

At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.

Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a senior growth marketer to own acquisition and lifecycle for Shadow, the most advanced marketing agent in the world, and Darkroom, our tech-enabled growth firm. Ad Age recently described us as “if Omnicom was rebuilt on AI.” Your job is to turn the attention we create into sign-ups, paying users and qualified leads. Shadow comes first.

This is a media and lifecycle role. You run paid acquisition, own the funnel from first click to paying user, and keep testing until the numbers move. Paid media and lifecycle sit under you. You work closely with our SEO and creator teams, the Director of Content, sales and the Shadow product team, and you run the work in Shadow from day one.

This is a New York-based role operating in the EST Time Zone, on-site at our NYC office, and all business is conducted 100% in English.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 1. Paid Acquisition: Meta, Google, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, TikTok, and new platforms. The budget split, audiences, bidding, and testing priorities.

 2. Creative Testing: A standing testing system for messages, use cases, audiences and formats. Brief the creative team, scale what works, and kill what doesn’t.

 3. Content Distribution: Turn our weekly long-form and short-form video content into paid distribution that brings people to Shadow.

 4. Sign-up & Activation: The Shadow sign-up and onboarding flow, with Product: activation milestones, in-app prompts, and the path to the first useful result. Landing pages and conversion tests.

 5. Lifecycle: Email and HubSpot. Onboarding, engagement, win-back, and upgrade for Shadow, and lead nurture for Darkroom.

 6. Darkroom Inbound: Qualified leads, cost per lead, and routing with sales so leads turn into meetings.

 7. Measurement: From spend to sign-up to paid to retention for Shadow, and from spend to lead to pipeline for Darkroom. Attribution, incrementality tests, clean CRM data, a weekly growth review, and a monthly report to leadership.

 8. Team: Lead the lifecycle manager and paid media specialists day-to-day, and work tightly with the SEO and creator team so everything feeds the same funnel.
    
    


YOU SHOULD APPLY IF THIS SOUNDS LIKE YOU

 1. 4+ years in growth or performance marketing, with paid budgets you managed yourself. You have scaled acquisition on Meta and Google and at least one of LinkedIn, TikTok or YouTube, and you can show what happened to CAC, conversion and revenue.

 2. You have grown a self-serve product: a SaaS, subscription or app where people sign up, activate and pay without talking to sales. You have moved activation and retention, not only the top of the funnel, and you have run lifecycle yourself: onboarding, nurture, segmentation and re-engagement, ideally in HubSpot.

 3. You know our world. DTC, e-commerce, performance marketing, AI tooling. Shadow’s users are marketers, so you can tell a strong ad from a weak one and explain why. B2B lead generation for an agency or services business is a strong plus.

 4. You are AI forward and already work with Claude, ChatGPT, or similar daily for analysis and execution, and have shipped real work with them. We are a Claude-first company.
    
    


HARD DISQUALIFIERS

 1. Less than 4 years of experience in growth or performance marketing.

 2. Never managed paid budgets yourself, only through agencies.

 3. No experience growing a self-serve product (SaaS, subscription or app).

 4. No ownership of acquisition targets like CAC, conversion, sign-ups or qualified leads.

 5. Experience mainly in events, partnerships or brand marketing.

 6. No experience using AI tools.




WHAT IT'S LIKE TO WORK AT DARKROOM

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We're looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect everyone to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity and ownership, and we support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape.

We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.

 - Unlimited PTO + US holidays: Rebooting is part of the work.

 - In person in NYC: You'll work from our New York office at 40 Wall St, side by side with the CEO.

 - Health & Wellness: Company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision coverage.

 - Finances and retirement: A 401(k) with company match and profit-sharing opportunities.

 - Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave for new parents.

 - Growth: A direct path to running a line of the business.

 - Compensation: The base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $180,000 per year. This range represents the anticipated minimum and maximum for this position and applies to candidates based in New York City, in compliance with the New York State Pay Transparency Law and the New York City Salary Transparency Law. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

 


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace. We are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

jobs.title: Instructional Assistant (Advanced Manufacturing Technician)
jobs.description:
ABOUT PER SCHOLAS:

For 30 years, Per Scholas has been on a mission to drive mobility and opportunity in the ever-advancing technology landscape by unlocking the untapped potential of individuals, uplifting communities, and meeting the needs of employers through rigorous tech training. By teaming up with dynamic employer partners, ranging from Fortune 500 companies to innovative startups, we're forging inclusive tech talent pipelines, fulfilling an ever-increasing need for skilled talent. With national remote training and campuses in 20+ cities and counting, Per Scholas offers no-cost training programs in the most sought-after tech skills, spanning Cloud, Cybersecurity, Data Engineering, IT Support, Software Engineering, and more. To date, 30,000+ individuals have been trained through Per Scholas, propelling their professional trajectories into high-growth tech careers with salaries three times higher than their pre-training earnings. Learn more by visiting PerScholas.org and follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.

Per Scholas candidates must reside in one of the following states, provided the position does not carry a specific office location requirement: AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IL, IN, KS, MD, MA, MI, MO, NC, NJ, NY, OH, PA, TX, WA, WI.

POSITION TITLE: Advanced Manufacturing Technician Instructional Assistant

LOCATION: Milwaukee, WI

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Per Scholas is seeking an Advanced Manufacturing Technician Instructional Assistant to join our Training Team and work with the Advanced Manufacturing Technician Instructor. The ideal candidate is a safety-minded, detail-oriented problem solver with strong technical and instructional skills, who adapts quickly to a dynamic environment and keeps a strong sense of accountability. The Instructional Assistant helps adult learners understand electrical and mechanical systems and build the operational discipline and risk awareness that highly automated plants require.

To succeed in this role, candidates must be business-minded within our mission focus and excel in instructional delivery that meets clients’ and learners’ high expectations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Assist the Advanced Manufacturing Technician Instructor in delivering instructor-led training that prepares students for entry-level to mid-level careers as Advanced Manufacturing Technicians in highly automated manufacturing environments. Responsibilities include daily instruction, assessment administration, attendance tracking, one-on-one tutoring, daily evaluation and monitoring of individual student progress, and consistent enforcement of classroom and lab standards.

• Assist in teaching foundational and intermediate technical concepts, including:

• Safety (OSHA/NFPA 70E)

• Basic Technical Skills (Hand Tools, P&ID reading)

• Electrical Fundamentals

• Sensors and Actuators

• Pumps, Motors, Motor Controllers, and VFDs

• Automation Equipment (PLC/SCADA)

• Conveyors/Robotics

• Assist in facilitating hands-on lab exercises on electrical panels, monitoring simulations, and mechanical systems, and enforce OSHA- and NFPA 70E-aligned safety practices in every lab.

• Assist in evaluating student troubleshooting performance using scenario-based diagnostics (e.g., P&ID reading, motor and VFD faults, sensor and actuator checks) and structured performance checklists.

• Lead study groups based on the instructor’s evaluations, and be ready to cover a lesson for a short time if the instructor needs to step out of the classroom.

• Plan each day’s activities with the instructor, prepare the tools and equipment for lectures and hands-on labs, and confirm that all equipment used by learners is returned.

• Provide students with relevant supplemental resources for deeper learning on technical systems, industry certifications, and best practices.

• Work closely with the instructor, career coaches, and the wider team to identify student needs, give ongoing feedback, implement individualized study plans for learners who are struggling, and participate in regular student-status meetings.

• Monitor and enforce learner attendance, dress code, and other program policies.

• Maintain and update Salesforce and/or our LMS (Canvas) in real time with student grades, certification scores, attendance, and performance notes.

• Support and maintain training curricula, syllabi, lesson plans, and classroom materials, identifying areas for improvement based on delivery experience.

• Dedicate capacity (e.g., 10% of non-instructional time) to professional development, technical upskilling, curriculum modernization, and contributing to the product’s retrospective/evaluation cycle.

• Work closely with the instructional and curriculum development teams to provide feedback on lab effectiveness, learner pain points, and content clarity.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO US

Instructional Skill Sets

• 2-4 years of experience working in manufacturing environments or power generation fields.

• 1-3 years of experience teaching technical subjects to technicians and operators.

• Strong technical background; able to grasp and convey highly technical subject matter clearly.

• Ability to respond clearly to live digital conversations via Zoom or in-person training environments.

• Strong communication and facilitation skills.

Required Skill Sets

• Technical proficiency in the course’s technical areas: safety (OSHA/NFPA 70E); basic technical skills (hand tools, P&ID reading); electrical fundamentals; sensors and actuators; pumps, motors, motor controllers, and VFDs; automation equipment (PLC/SCADA); and conveyors/robotics.

• Demonstrated understanding of industrial or mission-critical safety standards (OSHA, NFPA 70E, LOTO procedures).

• Ability to guide learners through troubleshooting scenarios in a structured and safety-conscious manner.

• Demonstrated fluency in using generative AI tools (e.g., Google Gemini) for instructional prep and assessment, and to model real-world professional use in the technical domain.

• Commitment to ongoing professional development, applicable certifications, and coursework to stay current with evolving manufacturing and automation technologies.

Preferred Skill Sets

• Prior experience in industrial maintenance, manufacturing, or critical facilities environments.

• Experience with SCADA or other industrial monitoring and control systems.

• Industry certifications such as OSHA 10 or 30 (General Industry), NFPA 70E training, or electrical, HVAC, or maintenance certifications.

• Experience teaching adult learners in competency-based or hands-on technical training programs.

Professional Qualifications

• Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline (or equivalent industry experience)

• Strong technical aptitude (Google Workspace, LMS platforms, Zoom, project management tools)

• Excellent written communication, presentation, and classroom management skills

• Strong evaluation and data management skills

• Ability to interpret technical documentation including schematics, P&IDs, and single-line diagrams

Personal Characteristics

• You thrive in a creative, inventive, fast-paced startup environment with people who are passionate about their work and mission.

• You are data-driven, result-oriented, and a forward-looking catalyst for social change.

• You have a collaborative and flexible work style. You’re excited to work cross-functionally with other departments and independently.

• You are a life-long learner.

• You are an effective communicator with strong oral and written skills.

• You are tech-savvy and learn new tools quickly.

• You are detail-oriented, with exceptional organizational management skills.

• You have strong public speaking and interpersonal skills. You are a motivator who is personable, approachable, and socially engaging. You can cultivate relationships and build rapport quickly and authentically with people from various professional and cultural backgrounds.

• You are adept at managing your time and balancing multiple projects and tasks.

• You stand behind our mission, believing that individuals from any community should have access to well-paying career positions and that talent should be recognized and recruited from diverse sources.

LI - #Onsite

For this role specifically, we are targeting a hourly rate of $28.

Benefits & Perks

Per Scholas offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and overall quality of life!

Holidays & PTO: Full-Time Per Scholas team members enjoy over 40 days of paid time off each year through a mix of holidays, vacation, and sick/personal time! All employees are eligible for Holiday pay upon hire (a total of 22 holidays annually, including a week off for Independence day and a week before the New Year). Full-Time Benefits Eligible employees also receive 80 Wellness Hours to use for Sick, Safe, or Personal reasons and accrue Vacation at a rate of 8 hours at the beginning of every month, supporting rest, recharge, and work-life balance. Vacation accruals increase with tenure. Part-time employees are afforded time off on a prorated basis and in accordance with local requirements.

jobs.title: Senior Growth & Business Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

Our Global Markets Growth & Business Operations team is growing. Our goal is to accelerate growth in our managed countries and to turn each country's ambition into a plan that gets delivered. We work closely with Brand Marketing, Growth Marketing, Product, Communications, Supply, Policy and Finance teams, both central and local, to develop growth levers, streamline operations, and drive impact for countries.

The Difference You Will Make

We are looking for someone to own and scale the growth operations capability for our global markets. You will set the direction for how we identify, pilot and scale new levers that capture growth country by country, and you will hold the organization accountable to deliver. This is a high-visibility role where your influence comes from the quality of your thinking and your ability to mobilize teams across a global matrix.

You will partner with Growth Marketing, Brand Marketing, Finance, Product and country leadership to build playbooks that can be implemented across markets, and you will shape the annual country plans and the central Global Markets strategy, including executive presentations to senior leadership.

This role requires expertise in business operations, marketplace dynamics, marketing channels and implementation, and a strong understanding of supply dynamics.

A Typical Day

Growth strategy and programs

• Own the strategy for the growth levers we run across global markets: decide where to invest, what to scale, and what to stop.

• Identify, pilot and scale new local demand levers, such as guest incentives and promotions, dynamic merchandising, local partnerships and local marketing, piloting new approaches before building the infrastructure to operate them at scale.

• Turn successful pilots into playbooks that countries can adopt, adapting them to local market realities.

• Build the investment case for new programs: sizing, business case, and the alignment needed to win resources in global planning cycles.

Country plans and operating rhythm

• Lead the development of annual and quarterly country plans and the central Global Markets strategy, setting and pressure-testing targets with country and functional leaders.

• Own the operating cadence: business reviews and OKR tracking that give leadership a single, trusted view of performance and the story behind it.

• Convert strategy into sequenced execution plans with named owners, milestones and success measures; surface risks early and drive them to resolution.

• Track business performance by country and the impact of the current playbook of levers, and act on what you find.

Cross-functional leadership

• Act as the connective tissue between country teams and central functions including Growth Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product, Communications, Supply, Policy and Finance.

• Broker trade-offs between global consistency and local market needs, and build alignment on priority projects, launches and product tests.

• Represent the team in senior forums, and mentor and raise the bar for others on the team through your example and feedback.

Insights and storytelling

• Turn complex data into clear narratives and recommendations that help leadership decide.

• Establish the metrics that matter and hold teams to a shared definition of success.

• Champion data-driven decision-making and use AI tooling to shorten the time from question to insight, automating recurring analysis and reporting so the team spends its time on judgment.

Your Expertise

• 12+ years in business operations, strategy, consulting or commercial leadership, scaling a business through demand, operations and supply, with a track record of owning outcomes across markets or a business unit

• Demonstrated ability to set strategy and drive it through to execution, and to prioritize quickly and go deep on new initiatives

• Deep experience influencing without authority across a global matrixed organization, including with senior and executive stakeholders

• Strong analytical toolkit: comfortable interrogating the numbers yourself and proposing a clear path to implementation

• Exceptional written and verbal communication, with executive presence

• Comfort with ambiguity, and a strong bias toward action and ownership

• Practical fluency with AI tools and a view on where they change how a team operates

• Travel up to 20%, including internationally

Additional

• Experience in a two-sided marketplace, travel/hospitality or consumer tech a plus

• Experience launching or scaling new programs or lines of business across multiple markets

• Experience with marketing channels and growth levers such as promotions, incentives, partnerships and merchandising

Your Location:

Due to the nature of this position, the successful applicant will need to be based in the San Francisco Bay Area to be able to conduct their work.

Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: reasonableaccommodations@airbnb.com. Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process.

We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Airbnb values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Airbnb are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, gender, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

How We'll Take Care of You:

Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits.

Pay Range

$204,000—$249,000 USD

Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @airbnb.com or @ext.airbnb.com email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing.  We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. We encourage candidates to remain vigilant of these recruiting scams and not share sensitive information if you do not believe an individual is actually affiliated with Airbnb.

Role Purpose

The Manager, Village Medical Operations turns the medical strategy for the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games into a working Polyclinic and Village medical service. Reporting to the Director, Village Medical Operations, this role plans operational workflows, coordinates facility setup and testing, and integrates multidisciplinary services from primary care and sports medicine to pharmacy and dental care. Working with medical providers, Village Management and international stakeholders, the Manager helps build a compliant, accessible and athlete-centered medical operation that serves athletes throughout the Games.

Key Responsibilities

· Translate medical strategy into Polyclinic operating plans, service schedules, layouts, patient flows and clinical documentation.

· Coordinate setup, test event validation, bump-in and bump-out of Village Polyclinic, satellite medical and athlete recovery facilities.

· Support delivery of sports medicine, physiotherapy, radiology, dental and pharmacy services, including WADA-compliant medication protocols.

· Collaborate with medical providers to recruit, credential and train Polyclinic clinicians, technicians and volunteers.

· Liaise with IOC/IPC commissions, NOC/NPC teams, hospitals, EMS and Village Management to integrate services and emergency transfers.

· Direct operational experience coordinating multidisciplinary medical delivery within ambulatory centers, clinics, sports medicine settings, or major multi-sport events.

· Demonstrated experience in facility planning, workforce management, and health system integration in complex, multi-stakeholder clinical settings.

· Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, PowerPoint and Teams, and project management tools such as Smartsheet or Asana.

Valued Experience

· Prior Olympic, Paralympic or elite international event operations experience.

· Familiarity with WADA and IOC/IPC medical standards.

· Collaborate in an inclusive, accessible workplace that helps create the Games.

What This Role Means for the Games

Athletes arrive in Los Angeles trusting that expert care is close at hand. This role helps the Village Polyclinic deliver safe, accessible and responsive medical services, so every Olympic and Paralympic athlete can recover and perform at their best.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

jobs.title: Senior Relationship Manager
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Imprint is on a mission to make every customer a regular.

You know how it feels when you walk into your favorite coffee shop and they know your name and start prepping your usual? Imprint makes it possible for the largest brands to create that experience at scale.

We bring payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence together in one platform, so brands can recognize and reward customers as individuals and keep them coming back. With the power of our technology and data, brands create financial products that their customers’ use everyday, earning more of their spend and increasing loyalty. Customers are rewarded with money and time saved, and surprised and delighted with a more unique, tailored experience.

We first proved our business in co-brand credit cards. For decades, the same few banks dominated the industry, building brands’ programs on mainframes older than the internet. We took a different approach, rebuilding the technology from the ground up. Today, Imprint has more than two million members, with partners like Shell, Kroger, H-E-B, and Booking.com http://Booking.com representing half a trillion dollars in total US consumer spend. Now, we’re growing our partnerships, bringing on more members, and expanding beyond credit cards so that brands offer more ways to pay and be rewarded to recognize their customers as individuals no matter their income or preferences.

Better yet, we’re doing it differently with a lean team of the most talented people on earth. Historically, companies scaled by adding people. Imprint is taking on our opportunity with a small team of exceptional people, with the best AI and technology dramatically amplifying what each person can accomplish. That means you’ll learn faster here than you could anywhere else. You’ll be one of the few people building an entirely new technology with the ownership and trust to shape what Imprint becomes. You’ll work alongside people who make you sharper everyday, armed with tools that turn your best ideas into reality faster than you thought possible. This is a rare chance to do the most important work of your career and to help prove that a small team can build what’s never been done before, inside industries that haven’t changed in decades.



Role Summary 

As Senior Relationship Manager, you will run Imprint's day-to-day work with our two sponsor banks. Sitting in Regulatory Affairs, you will own bank deliverables for live programs: submission packages, approvals, bank testing follow-ups, recurring oversight and contractual reporting, and the standing relationship with each bank's working teams.

You will act as the single point of contact for the banks' working teams: keeping recurring obligations on schedule, tracked in one place, and delivered to the bank on time. Commercial's launch team owns the program and the partner; you own what the bank needs to review, approve and receive. Product, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance and Operations produce the underlying work, and you are accountable for the deadline and the delivery. This is a senior relationship manager role that runs bank work across both new launches and business as usual.

Responsibilities

 - Own day-to-day contact with both sponsor banks, including standing calls, follow-ups and ad hoc data requests; own the oversight and contractual reporting calendar for live programs so every report and SLA is delivered on time, owned, and tracked in one place

 - Run oversight materials, launch letters and post-launch follow-ups with the banks

 - Support senior leadership on the bank work they own: executive relationships with bank leadership, quarterly business reviews and escalations

 - Hold functional teams to bank deadlines: each team produces its own reports and artifacts, and you are accountable for on-time delivery to the bank

 - Improve and automate bank workflows to reduce manual work and turnaround time

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

 - Taken over day-to-day contact and standing calls with both sponsor banks, and built trust with each bank's working teams through reliable execution and clear communication

 - Built a single tracker of every recurring oversight, contractual and SLA obligation to the banks, each with a named owner and due date

 - Delivered every bank report and data request due in the period on time

 - Run at least one new program or product submission through bank review, approval and launch follow-ups

 - Established working relationships with Commercial's launch team, Product, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance and Operations

 - Identified and implemented 2–3 process improvements that reduce turnaround time on bank submissions or reporting

Qualifications

Required

 - 8+ years of experience in fintech bank partnerships, sponsor bank operations, or program or project management in regulated financial services

 - Senior project manager who can run several launches and a full reporting calendar at once and keep each on schedule

 - Deep understanding of fintech and sponsor bank dynamics, bank oversight expectations and regulatory requirements

 - Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and external partners without direct authority

 - Strong problem-solving skills: ability to identify issues, propose solutions, and execute independently

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with high emotional intelligence and stakeholder management capability

 - Highly organized and process-oriented, with a track record of improving workflows and driving operational efficiency

 - Grit, initiative, and ownership mindset—proactively driving outcomes rather than waiting for direction

Nice to Have

 - Experience with credit card issuance, co-branded card programs or lending at a fintech with active sponsor bank relationships

 - Familiarity with standard productivity tools: Google Workspace, Notion, Jira, Asana, Microsoft

 - Track record of centralizing knowledge, automating workflows, or scaling operational processes

 - Experience managing metrics-driven programs with clear success criteria and accountability

 - Experience preparing materials for bank oversight committees, business reviews or regulatory exams




PERKS & BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation and equity

 - Medical plan options fully paid by Imprint, including coverage for your dependents 

 - 100% company-paid dental and vision plan options

 - Mental health support through Spring Health, plus a confidential Employee Assistance Program

 - Healthcare navigation through Rightway, plus HSA, FSA and commuter benefits

 - Flexible paid time off

 - 20 weeks of paid parental leave for primary caregivers and 8 weeks for all new parents

 - The latest tools and technology, including AI, so you can do your best work
   
   

Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

The Temporary Senior Producer, Podcast Subscriptions will play a critical role in producing standout audio and video content designed to drive audience revenue for NPR and Member stations, delight existing NPR+ subscribers, and convert listeners into paying supporters.

Rather than solely acting as a traditional producer, this role requires a self-contained content scavenger and editor. You will delve into raw recordings, unreleased tape, and deep archives across major NPR properties to surface hidden gems, assemble compelling bonus edits, and produce short-form video highlights.

Working closely with show runners, content teams, marketing, and editorial leadership, you will lead the hands-on execution of supporter-only perks—ranging from uncut vault interviews and host banter reels to digital articles, blog features, and special pilot projects.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.

Responsibilities

• Mine raw show files, unedited interviews, and archive vaults to discover, edit, and publish high-value bonus audio and video content.

• Produce specialized archival projects for flagship programming, including retrospectives, unedited guest material, and custom audio or video features.

• Edit audio and video deliverables using industry-standard production software for promotional teasers, subscriber feeds, and multi-platform distribution.

• Pilot new supporter-only podcast benefits

• Develop, write, and manage subscriber-only digital and community features, including donor updates, direct audience engagement experiments, and digital articles.

• Collaborate with show runners and production teams to ensure bonus content aligns with overall vision and host expectations.

• Partner with Marketing and Development teams to write and produce promotional spots highlighting subscriber benefits.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

• 8+ years of audio production and editing experience in radio or podcasting.

• Demonstrated proficiency in both audio editing and video production/motion design using tools like Adobe Premiere, Descript, After Effects, and Riverside.

• Proven journalist's or curator's eye for identifying narrative-rich, entertaining moments in raw files without needing line-by-line editorial direction.

• Ability to write and produce recordings of clean, professional voiceover or narration bridges independently.

• Experience working diplomatically and cross-functionally with high-profile hosts, showrunners, and editorial leadership in a matrixed organization.

• Demonstrated capability to self-manage multiple complex work streams and deliver high-quality cuts on tight deadlines.

• Commitment to fostering diversity, equity, and inclusion in editorial framing and workplace culture.

Preferred Qualifications

• Demonstrated proficiency in both audio editing and video production/motion design using tools like Adobe Premiere, Descript, After Effects, and Riverside.

jobs.title: Head of Construction Operations
jobs.description:
ABOUT CHARGE ROBOTICS

Charge Robotics is a Series A startup building robots that build solar farms.

Demand for new solar projects is booming (one-fifth of all the solar that exists in the US was installed last year!), but today’s construction companies can’t keep up due to limited labor resources.

We thought this was insane, so we developed robots to directly address this bottleneck and speed up the world’s transition to renewables. We’ve shipped our first commercial system already, and are in the process of scaling up our operations to meet our massive demand.

Charge is a fast-moving company, which means constant opportunities for learning and growth. You’ll have a large impact on the direction of our company and our product, which will be reflected in significant equity compensation. And you get to work with 🤖 giant robots 🤖.

If you are excited to work on interesting technical & operational problems with direct climate impact, you’re going to fit right in at Charge Robotics.

Read more about Charge in recent press:

 - YouTube - Introducing Sunrise, the assembly line for solar https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ix0oMgqTfko

 - Fast Company - Solar Building Robots to Solve One of Climate's Biggest Problems https://www.fastcompany.com/91108331/these-solar-assembling-robotic-arms-could-solve-one-of-the-industrys-biggest-problems

 - MIT News - Making solar projects cheaper and faster with portable factories https://news.mit.edu/2025/charge-robotics-makes-solar-projects-cheaper-faster-portable-factories-0312

We’re MIT-founded and backed by Silicon Valley’s top investors, including Founders Fund, Energy Impact Partners, Lux Capital, YC (S21), and more.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As Head of Construction Operations, you’ll own how Sunrise gets solar farms built in the field. You’ll run our deployments on utility-scale solar sites end to end, from site readiness and mobilization through daily production to demobilization, and build the team, playbooks and systems that take us from a handful of systems in the field to a fleet.

You’ll report directly to our CEO and work closely with our engineering, manufacturing and commercial teams. You’ll also be the main point of contact for our EPC customers’ field teams.

This is a rare chance to bring deep construction experience to a new way of building solar, and to define what a construction operation built around robots looks like.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Run our field deployments. Own every Charge project from site readiness and mobilization through production and demobilization, and deliver each one on schedule, on budget and to our quality and safety standards.

 - Scale from a few systems to a fleet. Build the playbooks, staffing plans and field-to-HQ communication protocols that let us run multiple systems across multiple sites at once as our manufacturing ramps.

 - Build and lead the field organization. Hire, train and lead site superintendents, operators, field engineers, technicians and local crews, and build a culture of ownership, safety, accountability and continuous improvement.

 - Own production performance and cost. Track install rate, system uptime and cost per MW on every site, find what’s slowing us down, and drive the fixes in the field and back at HQ.

 - Be the voice of the field. Turn what you learn on site into clear requirements, design feedback and acceptance standards for engineering and manufacturing, so every system arrives ready to build.

 - Lead customer relationships on site. Serve as the primary point of contact for our customers’ field teams, give regular project updates, and resolve issues before they slow the job.

 - Shape what projects we take on. Partner with our commercial team to assess site readiness, schedules and labor models for new projects, and bring operational input to pricing and contracts.

 - Own field safety and compliance. Set and enforce our field safety program, and make sure every site meets OSHA, customer and environmental requirements.


YOU BRING

 - 10+ years in construction management, including 5+ in utility-scale solar. You’ve led field operations on large solar projects, ideally tracker and module installation at an EPC or self-perform contractor.

 - A track record of running multiple sites at once. You’ve managed several concurrent projects and owned their schedules, budgets and results.

 - Leadership that others follow. You’ve built and led field teams of superintendents, foremen and crews, developed leaders under you, and worked with both union and non-union labor.

 - A strong safety and quality record. OSHA 30 or equivalent, and a history of safe, high-quality installation on large sites.

 - Command of the numbers. You’re fluent in project controls, cost tracking, production reporting and the tools that go with them.

 - A builder’s mindset. You’re excited to run a construction operation built around new technology and can quickly turn lessons from the field into better processes for the company. Our HQ team that you'll work closely with is a ~30 person startup, which brings high growth and ownership but requires comfort with ambiguity, decisiveness, and operating speed.

 - Ability to travel 50–75% of the time. Most travel is to active solar construction sites where we deploy Sunrise, with occasional trips to our HQ in San Leandro, CA.

 - A degree in construction management, engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience leading field work.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Tracker installation expertise, especially on Nextpower (formerly Nextracker) systems.

 - New technology in the field. Experience deploying automation, robotics or other first-of-a-kind equipment on construction sites.

 - Startup or scale-up experience. You’ve built a field operation early on and know when to formalize a process and when to keep moving fast.

 - International projects. Experience mobilizing equipment and crews for projects outside the US.

 - Industry presence. Strong relationships across EPCs, developers and tracker OEMs, and comfort representing Charge at conferences and industry events.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

jobs.description:
What Impact You'll Have

We are seeking an Aeronautical Production Specialist to support the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency's (NGA) Airfield Foundation Data (AFD) program. In this role, you will contribute to the creation and maintenance of foundational airfield intelligence by extracting, analyzing, validating, and producing geospatial data in accordance with NGA standards and specifications. Your work will directly support mission-critical aviation, intelligence, and operational planning requirements by ensuring the accuracy and completeness of airfield feature data.

What You'll be Owning

• Extract, analyze, and maintain Airfield Foundation Data (AFD) features from imagery and other geospatial sources in accordance with NGA product specifications.

• Identify, collect, validate, and update airfield features including runways, taxiways, navigational aids, air traffic control towers, hangars, and other aviation-related infrastructure.

• Perform data acquisition, evaluation, analysis, entry, application, and maintenance activities within NGA-defined collection areas.

• Conduct mensuration activities to support accurate feature extraction and geospatial positioning.

• Execute quality control and quality assurance reviews to ensure compliance with established NGA standards and accuracy requirements.

• Support product finishing activities and assist with database updates as required.

• Create, maintain, and update technical documentation supporting production processes and mission requirements.

• Collaborate with team members and stakeholders to resolve data discrepancies and improve production workflows.

• Ensure production milestones and deliverables are completed accurately and on schedule.

What You Must Have

• Active TS/SCI clearance.

• Candidates must either possess an active CI Polygraph at the time of hire or be willing and eligible to obtain and maintain one.

• 1–3 years of experience performing geospatial feature collection, feature validation, and finishing activities involving points, lines, and polygons.

• Basic knowledge of airfield infrastructure, including runways, taxiways, navigational aids, air traffic control towers, hangars, and related aviation features.

• Experience performing imagery analysis and mensuration activities.

• Ability to understand, update, and develop technical documentation supporting production requirements and mission objectives.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to data quality and accuracy.

• Ability to work independently while effectively collaborating within a team environment.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

What Would be Nice to Have

• Understanding of geospatial principles including horizontal and vertical coordinate systems, elevation models, and positional accuracy standards.

• Knowledge of imagery sources, geospatial products, collection processes, and sensor capabilities.

• Experience reading, interpreting, and writing XML.

• Familiarity with NGA production workflows, specifications, and quality standards.

• Experience using GIS, imagery exploitation, or geospatial production tools.

• Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Geography, Geospatial Intelligence, GIS, Remote Sensing, Aviation, or a related field.

Why Choose GRVTY

The toughest national security challenges demand vision and ingenuity, not just resources. We deliver mission and technical expertise to outpace our adversaries. We’re purpose-built to tackle the most entrenched, systemic national security issues around the world.

We partner with our customers to help them overcome challenges in every corner of technology and defense—including the ones still being explored.
