About the Team

Manufacturing Engineering, part of CoreWeave’s Data Center Infrastructure Supply Chain, connects design intent with supplier capability so manufacturing capacity keeps pace with CoreWeave’s growth. The team evaluates both the equipment suppliers produce and the processes used to build it, supporting owner-furnished, contractor-installed (OFCI) equipment across electrical distribution, power generation, cooling, and fit-out. The goal is predictable quality: equipment that arrives at site to the correct specification, with complete records, in good condition.

As the Data Center Manufacturing Engineering Manager, you will help CoreWeave determine whether suppliers can deliver, building confidence through evidence from supplier evaluation through equipment delivery. Day to day, you will assess factories, review production plans, troubleshoot manufacturing failures, coordinate factory testing, and drive supplier improvements. You will work with Design, Strategic Sourcing, Procurement Operations, Supply Planning, Construction, Commissioning, and Facility Engineering. Your job is to connect how equipment is built with how it is deployed, set clear actions, and escalate risks early to protect quality, cost, and deployment schedules.

This role requires 40–60% travel to supplier sites, manufacturing facilities, and active construction sites across US hubs.

Key Responsibilities:

• Manufacturing Engineering Practices: Develop and implement Manufacturing Engineering practices covering supplier validation, production readiness, factory testing, issue escalation, and lessons learned.

• Design for Manufacturability: Work with Design and suppliers to evaluate manufacturability, assembly methods, material selection, and testability. Recommend improvements that preserve approved performance and safety requirements.

• Manufacturing Controls: Work with the responsible technical teams to turn specifications and deployment needs into manufacturing controls, inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and documentation requirements.

• Contract Requirements: Work with Strategic Sourcing and Procurement Operations to build manufacturing, quality, testing, and traceability requirements into RFPs, contracts, and supplier agreements.

• Supplier Qualification: Lead supplier quality onboarding, qualification, and ongoing performance management for critical infrastructure vendors.

• Factory Assessments & Testing: Lead supplier factory assessments and audits before award or production ramp, validating technical capability, production capacity, workforce readiness, tooling, critical processes, and quality controls. Conduct factory acceptance tests (FATs) and manufacturing readiness reviews to confirm conformance before shipment.

• Corrective Action: Drive supplier corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) through measurable closure and sustained improvement.

• Installation Readiness: Work with construction and commissioning teams to make sure equipment arrives complete, compliant, and ready to install.

• Field Quality Issues: Own investigation and resolution of major field quality issues, including defects, non-conformances, installation deviations, and missing documentation. Feed lessons learned systematically back into supplier requirements and RFPs.

• Supplier Performance Measures: Establish supplier performance measures for throughput, first-pass yield, defects, rework, corrective-action closure, and delivery readiness. Use verified data to expose gaps and prioritize improvement.

• Risk Tracking: Maintain traceable records of supplier assessments, manufacturing risks, test results, deviations, and action logs, with clear owners, due dates, and escalation paths.

• Supplier Improvement: Lead supplier improvement initiatives that reduce variation, improve safety and efficiency, and address recurring quality, cost, and schedule risks. Verify results through sustained performance.

• Reporting: Build dashboards and run regular supplier reviews that communicate evidence, risks, decisions, and recovery progress to project teams and leadership, using analytics and digital tools to improve visibility.

Qualifications:

• 8+ years of experience in manufacturing, supplier engineering, supplier quality, or production operations for complex mechanical or electrical equipment.

• Hands-on experience evaluating factory capability, production flow, capacity, tooling, assembly processes, and process controls, with documented manufacturing improvements.

• Proven track record conducting supplier audits and FATs/SATs and driving CAPA programs with documented outcomes.

• Strong experience applying structured problem-solving methods (8D, FMEA, RCA) and statistical process control (SPC) to resolve manufacturing failures.

• Experience managing quality for complex mechanical and electrical systems (e.g., generators, switchgear, cooling equipment, power distribution).

• Ability to define, track, and report quality metrics tied to operational and financial impact.

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, or a related technical discipline.

Preferred Skills:

• Certifications such as ASQ CQE, CQA, Six Sigma Black Belt, or equivalent.

• Experience supporting hyperscale or AI-focused data center deployments.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Technical Operations
jobs.description:
Profound is the fastest-growing AI marketing platform, used by 15% of the Fortune 500 including Comcast, Estée Lauder, and Walmart, and innovators like Ramp, MongoDB, and Figma. It is where marketing teams do the work: research, briefs, content, campaigns, reporting, all in one place, alongside agents that carry the load with them.  

Built on 2B+ real user prompts and growing, Profound’s data shows you what people ask AI and what the models say back. Profound's AI Marketer joins that data with deep context about our customers to find the opportunities worth acting on, and then puts agents to work: automating reporting, drafting content, auditing pages for readability, running competitive research. It measures what works and gets better every day.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a Technology Operations Engineer to own the reliability, security, and scalability of our identity, endpoint, and IT infrastructure systems. You'll work directly with our Engineering and Operations team to transform reactive IT support into proactive, automated systems that scale with our rapid growth. This role is perfect for someone who sees IT operations as a strategic enabler of engineering velocity, not just a support function.

You'll be based in our Union Square office, collaborating closely with your colleagues in person and remotely in San Francisco.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Day-to-Day Operations & Incident Response

 - Triage and resolve technical issues with a focus on automation and continuous improvement

 - Manage and troubleshoot macOS devices and development environments at scale

 - Trace root causes across complex, multi-system failures (Google Workspace → MDM → AWS)

 - Build runbooks, troubleshooting guides, and documentation that elevate team capabilities

Strategic Systems Thinking

 - Identify patterns in recurring issues and implement systematic fixes

 - Analyze downstream impacts before making changes; understand the blast radius of identity and access management decisions

 - Lead projects that address operational pain points (device provisioning, access control, compliance automation)

 - Design self-service solutions that empower engineers to move faster

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Translate technical issues for stakeholders across Engineering, People Ops, and Finance

 - Partner with security to implement and maintain compliance controls

 - Support our rapid hiring by streamlining onboarding and provisioning processes

 - Mentor future IT team members on troubleshooting methodology and systems thinking


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

Required Experience:

 - 5+ years in IT Operations or Technical Support, ideally supporting engineering teams in high-growth SaaS/AI companies

 - Systems thinker who naturally traces dependencies and asks "why did this break?" not just "how do I fix it?"

 - Strong incident management skills: triage, root-cause analysis, and pattern recognition

 - Experience with identity management, SSO, and access control systems

 - Clear communicator who can explain complex technical issues to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders

 - Self-directed with strong judgment on when to escalate versus resolve independently

Technical Skills:

 - Expert troubleshooting across the Apple ecosystem, including MDM (Kandji, Jamf, or similar)

 - Advanced Google Workspace administration (SAML/OIDC, lifecycle automation, SCIM)

 - Multi-cloud support experience (AWS primary, familiarity with GCP/Azure)

 - Network troubleshooting (DNS, VPNs, routing)

 - Scripting and automation (Python, Bash) for repetitive tasks and integrations

 - Experience with infrastructure as code and configuration management

 - Good taste with technology, both software and hardware


WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE UNIQUE

You're not just fixing problems—you're building the operational foundation for a company that's defining a new category. Every system you implement, every process you automate, directly accelerates our ability to ship products that help companies navigate the AI revolution.

As our first dedicated Technology Operations hire, you'll have significant autonomy to shape how we scale our technical operations. You'll work alongside engineers who are building billion-scale event processing systems, and your work will directly impact their velocity and effectiveness.


COMP 

 - Base salary: $120,000 - $170,000



Note: All official communication from Profound will come from a @tryprofound.com email address. If you're contacted by anyone using a different domain, please disregard and report it as spam.

jobs.title: Manager, Marketing Operations
jobs.description:
The Manager, Marketing Operations leads the people, priorities, platforms, and operating practices that enable Marketing to execute reliably and at scale. Reporting to the Vice President, Growth Marketing, this role translates Marketing strategy into a prioritized operational roadmap and is accountable for team performance, marketing technology reliability, lead-lifecycle effectiveness, campaign governance, data quality, and measurable continuous improvement.

The Manager maintains sufficient technical depth to guide decisions and evaluate trade-offs while enabling senior individual contributors and technical partners to own complex solution design and execution. The role partners closely with Revenue Operations, Revenue Technology, Sales, IT, Data, Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, Legal, and Marketing leaders to deliver scalable, governed, and increasingly automated ways of working.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

Marketing Operations Leadership & People Management

• Leading, coaching, developing, and managing the Marketing Operations team, establishing clear goals, role expectations, performance standards, and development plans.
• Owning intake, prioritization, capacity planning, and work allocation across campaign operations, platform administration, lead management, reporting, data quality, automation, and operational support.
• Establishing team operating rhythms, service expectations, escalation paths, and performance measures; addressing delivery or capability gaps promptly.
• Developing team capability in marketing technology, data literacy, automation, systems thinking, troubleshooting, documentation, and responsible AI-enabled work.

Marketing Technology & Platform Operations

• Owning the Marketing Operations roadmap and business administration of the marketing technology ecosystem, aligned with Marketing and revenue priorities.
• Ensuring Salesforce-connected marketing capabilities and related audience, journey, campaign, personalization, analytics, and activation platforms remain reliable, scalable, secure, and appropriately governed.
• Establishing platform ownership, access, release, QA, documentation, change management, and lifecycle practices in partnership with technical owners.
• Evaluating platform capabilities and recommending whether to build, buy, integrate, consolidate, or retire technology; senior technical contributors may lead detailed design and implementation.

Data, Lead Lifecycle & GTM Integration

• Owning Marketing requirements and outcomes for lead and contact capture, enrichment, normalization, deduplication, segmentation, scoring, routing, suppression, consent, lifecycle progression, attribution, and Sales handoff.
• Establishing data-quality standards, monitoring, and corrective mechanisms that identify incomplete, stale, duplicate, conflicting, or incorrectly routed records.
• Partnering with Revenue Operations and Revenue Technology to maintain clear decision rights and ownership boundaries across Marketing, CRM, and revenue systems.
• Guiding the governed use of first-party, intent, engagement, enrichment, product, campaign, conversational, and customer signals in marketing audiences and workflows.

Campaign & Operational Governance

• Establishing scalable standards for campaign intake, taxonomy, naming conventions, UTMs, audience definitions, consent and suppression, lifecycle triggers, attribution, QA, documentation, and launch readiness.
• Ensuring reusable processes, templates, and service models enable channel and lifecycle marketers to execute quickly without avoidable manual handoffs.
• Defining and monitoring SLAs for recurring operational work; investigating exceptions, failures, and bottlenecks and holding owners accountable for resolution.
• Anticipating operational needs for campaigns, product launches, customer journeys, segmentation strategies, and new go-to-market motions.

Automation, AI & Continuous Improvement

• Prioritizing high-value automation and approved AI-enabled use cases that reduce repetitive work and improve quality, speed, consistency, and decision support.
• Establishing human accountability, permissions, testing, monitoring, escalation, documentation, and change controls for automated and AI-supported workflows.
• Partnering with technical teams and senior individual contributors on secure implementation across approved systems, APIs, data sources, and knowledge repositories.
• Measuring productivity and quality gains and redirecting capacity toward analysis, optimization, experimentation, and higher-value systems work.

Operational Performance & Cross-Functional Partnership

• Establishing dashboards and operating metrics for lead-flow health, platform reliability, campaign quality, SLA attainment, data quality, throughput, cycle time, automation adoption, and stakeholder outcomes.
• Using operational evidence to identify root causes, clarify trade-offs, prioritize investment, and quantify the impact of improvements.
• Serving as the primary Marketing Operations partner across Marketing, Revenue Operations, Revenue Technology, Sales, IT, Data, Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, Legal, and vendors.
• Communicating roadmap priorities, capacity, dependencies, risks, decisions, and expected outcomes clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

YOU’VE GOT WHAT IT TAKES IF YOU HAVE:

• 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in Marketing Operations, marketing automation, marketing technology, Revenue Operations, lifecycle operations, CRM operations, or a closely related field.
• 2+ years of demonstrated leadership experience, which may include formal or informal team leadership, coordinating work and priorities, guiding others, providing feedback, and addressing team challenges.
• Demonstrated experience operating enterprise CRM and marketing automation capabilities in a B2B environment.
• Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional system, integration, data, automation, or process-improvement initiatives from requirements through implementation and sustained operation.
• Experience establishing operational standards, governance, documentation, measurement, and quality controls across complex marketing processes.
• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Information Systems, Analytics, Computer Information Systems, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and practical experience.

IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAD:

• Experience working in B2B SaaS, healthcare technology, education technology, or another complex or regulated technology environment.
• Experience implementing or operating Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Marketing Cloud Account Engagement, Data Cloud, or comparable enterprise lifecycle and automation platforms.
• Hands-on experience with enrichment, audience-building, intent, conversation-intelligence, or GTM orchestration technologies such as Gong or 6sense.
• Experience designing or operating production AI-enabled or multi-system automated workflows with defined governance and human oversight.
• Relevant certifications such as Salesforce Administrator, Salesforce Marketing Cloud Administrator or Consultant, Salesforce Data Cloud Consultant, or comparable marketing automation credentials.

We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world.

Team Description:

As part of the Surgery & Robot Hardware Department, the Surgical Consumables Team is responsible for producing a wide range of critical mechanical devices that enable our life-changing surgical procedures. Balancing immediate needs with long-term scalability, we drive innovation with precisely-engineered tools that ensure safety, reliability, and high-quality surgical execution.

Job Description and Responsibilities:

As a Manufacturing Technician at Neuralink, you will be responsible for manufacturing our surgical robot’s consumables, including the needle cartridge, which is a critical component used to insert the electrodes of our brain-computer interface device. Manufacturing the needle cartridge involves working with lasers, digital optics, lenses, sonication machines, welding machines, and pressurized air/gasses. You will work alongside the robotics mechanical engineering team to tackle mission-critical projects, by assembling production devices as well as prototypes for research and development. You'll also drive efforts like troubleshooting, data analysis, process improvement, and designing/building new fixtures. Your projects will immediately impact quality and rate of progress. • Assemble a range of high-precision medical devices for both testing and clinical use

• Manage inventory, stockpiles, and order requests to facilitate studies and tests across the organization

• Develop processes and procedures to improve quality, efficiency, and traceability

• Work closely with hardware engineers to support testing and issue resolution

jobs.description:
The Patient Care Technician reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Memorial, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Patient Care Technician’s primary function is to assist and support the Professional Registered Nurse in all aspects of direct and indirect patient care activities.  The Patient Care Technician functions as a member of the unit staff under the direction and supervision of the professional Registered Nurse.

Responsibilities:

• Direct Patient Care Activities Assists with admission, transfer, and discharge process.Takes and records temperature, pulse, respirations, weight for adults and/or neonates, height, and blood pressure.Measures and records intake and output including output from drains.Applies cardiac monitor/oximetry.Obtains EKG.Adheres to the infant security protocol (accurate assessment of band placement).Performs normal newborn hearing screening.Obtains capillary blood glucose for adults and/or neonates.Performs phlebotomy.Applies Fetal Monitor equipment on pregnant patients.Discontinues heplocks and foley catheters. Administers enemas.Collects specimens (urine, stool, blood and sputum) on adults and/or neonates. Makes rounds of patients and anticipates their needs and observes newborns in the nursery.Responds to patient call lights in a timely manner, especially emergency lights.Distributes fresh drinking water and nourishments to patients. Prepares patients for meals; assists or feeds patients as necessary. Feeds normal newborns as assigned.Provides morning care, bed baths and evening care according to established Nursing Care Procedures. Provides peri-care to appropriate patients.Provides newborn care to the infant including bath, dressing, obtaining foot prints, assistance with feeding (bottle and breast), glucose checks.Makes occupied and unoccupied beds.Ambulates patients and instructs on walker, cane and crutch walking as appropriate for assigned unit. Assists with pre-and post-operative care; positions patients as ordered; applies special equipment for safety; lifts and turns patients with proper and safe body mechanics and available resources.Applies comfort and safety measures (side rails and call lights). Sets up oxygen and suction equipment and other respiratory equipment for adults and/or neonates.Applies dressings to Stage I and Stage II skin breakdown. Prepares patient room for MD or RN assessment, evaluation, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Assists with procedures in the normal newborn nursery as directed.Transports patients, equipment and/or supplies during urgent and emergent situations and to front door on discharge.Responds to emergency situations, secures assistance and initiates basic life support.Reports observations and documents appropriately. Promptly notifies RN of any change in patient condition.Performs post-mortem care and transports bodies to the morgue when necessary.Assumes responsibility for the care of patient’s prosthetic devices, hearing aides, dentures, eye glasses, etc.Follows established policies, procedures and standards of care in all areas of practice.

• Indirect Patient CareMaintains a safe and clean environment. Duties may include: maintaining temperature logs on, defrosting, and cleaning refrigerator, straightening linen, cleaning utility rooms, cleaning IV poles, cleaning scale, cleaning and returning equipment to SPD, replacing and disposing of soiled linen bags.Performs duties delegated by the RN to facilitate patient care and the efficient operations of the assigned patient care unit.Collects and inventories patient belongings on admission, transfer and discharge.Completes charges using appropriate documentation.Orders supplies on-line or appropriate requisitions and stocks in appropriate location.Obtains necessary equipment and supplies to facilitate patient care.Assures room readiness for incoming patients.Checks designated equipment for proper functioning.Counts instruments and sterile trays sent and received from SEP as appropriate for assigned unit.Stocks and removes linen from patient rooms.Sets up and breaks down delivery table.Participates in staff meetings.Demonstrates cost effective approach to patient care in terms of equipment, supplies and other resource use.Participates in quality improvement activities.Participates in daily/weekly/monthly QC’s.Participates in orientation of new staff.Performs related duties as assigned.Uses established communication channels to resolve work related problems.Understands and consistently demonstrates principles of “Patient’s First” philosophy.Carries out assigned tasks and activities on a shift basis, as delegated by the RN.Assumes responsibility for meeting mandatory requirements.

Required:

• CNA Certification or currently enrolled in School of Nursing who has successfully completed basic clinical rotations.
• CPR recognition by the American Heart Association (BLS for Healthcare Providers).
• Minimum of 90% correct on annual mandatory Health and Safety Training quizzes.
• Unit based recognition for Capillary Blood Glucose Monitoring.

• Previous experience in a health care setting preferred with a demonstrated ability to relate to patients, family, nursing and medical staff.

Preferred:

jobs.description:
At InStride, people are our purpose.

We believe that investing in people is the most powerful way to drive success—for individuals and organizations alike.

Our mission goes beyond skill-building; we're here to empower our partners’ employees to advance their careers, elevate their expertise, and achieve meaningful personal and professional growth.

No matter the team you’re on, our dedication to the success of our partners and their employees is what drives us. If you're passionate about making a difference and driving educational and professional advancement, InStride is the place for you.

To get a better feel for our culture, watch more here.

Candidates must be located in one of the following states to be considered eligible for employment: AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, IL, IN, KS, LA, MA, MD, MI, MN, MO, NC, NH, NJ, NV, NY, OH, OR, PA, TX, VA, WA, WI.

What we're looking for:

InStride is seeking experienced Data Analysts to join our growing Data Analytics team. As a Senior Data Analyst reporting to the Director of Data Analytics, you will play a crucial role in transforming data into actionable insights and recommendations that drive strategic decisions across the business. You’ll collaborate closely with stakeholders across the company, providing them with data-driven insights to support growth and operational efficiency. Your work will contribute to building a strong data culture, enabling key business partners to self-serve data through dynamic dashboards and make informed decisions using company-wide metrics.

Skills we’d love to see you show off:

• Data Analysis & Reporting: Analyze complex datasets from Databricks to provide actionable insights across internal teams such as sales, marketing, finance, and product. Build and maintain dynamic Tableau dashboards that empower stakeholders to self-serve and track key metrics.

• Stakeholder Collaboration: Work closely with business partners to understand needs and provide data-driven insights for strategic decisions. Serve as a trusted advisor to business stakeholders, helping them interpret data and apply it effectively.

• Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Metrics: Identify, define, and track company-wide key performance indicators (KPIs) aligned with business goals. Continuously monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of KPIs, suggesting new metrics to support organizational consistency.

• Data Validation & Integrity: Ensure accuracy and consistency in data reporting, collaborating with analytics engineers to maintain data quality. Validate data models, ensuring alignment with business requirements and optimization for reporting.

• Data Visualization & Presentation: Create clear and compelling visualizations to communicate complex data to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Present insights and recommendations in a concise, actionable format to business leaders and teams.

• Documentation & Best Practices: Maintain thorough documentation of data models, analysis processes, dashboards, and business rules. Ensure stakeholders understand key metrics and methodologies through clear and accessible documentation.

Who you are:

• 5+ years of experience in a data analysis or business intelligence role.

• Strong expertise in SQL and visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI.

• Excellent business acumen with the ability to quickly understand complex business processes and relationships between data.

• Proficient in statistics and comfortable applying statistical methods to analyze data.

• Experience identifying, defining, and tracking KPIs that support strategic business initiatives.

• Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with a knack for making data insights easy to understand for non-technical stakeholders.

• Experience working in a collaborative environment with technical teams and non-technical stakeholders.

• Experience in the edtech or education sector is a plus.

How you will create impact:

• Enable key business partners to make data-driven decisions by providing timely and insightful analysis.

• Collaborate with engineers to ensure the reporting infrastructure supports efficient and accurate business insights.

• Identify and track key performance indicators (KPIs) that drive business success and continuously evaluate their effectiveness.

• Improve data visualization and storytelling capabilities across the organization, increasing trust in and reliance on data.

• Help drive business performance by uncovering trends and opportunities.

Compensation

We encourage you to talk with your recruiter to learn more about the total compensation and benefits available for this role.

$100,000—$125,000 USD

We are looking for someone who is not only technically skilled, but also enthusiastic about making a meaningful impact. At InStride, we foster a culture of belonging, we support authenticity and intersectionality, and we embrace and appreciate our differences. jobs.description:

Position Summary

The Inventory Control Manager is responsible for implementing and overseeing robust processes related to inventory accuracy, reporting and cycle counting.  The candidate chosen for this position will lead an on-site inventory team within their home campus, and may support a remote team in another campus, collaborating regularly with operations and administrative leaders to build meaningful relationships that help to fuel the continued growth strategy of ITS Logistics.

Principle Accountabilities

• Create and implement processes and procedures that improve the client experience related to inventory accuracy and reporting, including standard operating procedures (SOPs)

• Oversee and improve various existing daily/weekly/monthly cycle counting programs, implement new programs, as required

• Partner with the Operations and Administrative teams to proactively identify and remove roadblocks that affect inventory accuracy

• Acquire a strong understanding of internal WMS and reporting systems, leveraging them regularly to drive continuous improvement in inventory accuracy

Position Requirements

Requirements for this position include, but are not limited to:

• Bachelor’s Degree preferred, but not required

• Five + years of experience in a distribution environment with a strong understanding of WMS/ERP systems and inventory control/management practices is required

• Excellent leadership and organizational skills, advanced problem resolution skills

• Strong verbal and written communication skills

• Solid understanding of MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

• Positive, team-first attitude and strong work ethic

• Demonstrated ability to multi-task and prioritize assignments

Physical Demands

• Alternates between a quiet, climate-controlled office and an active, fast-paced industrial environment subject to variable temperatures, machinery noise, and dust. Adherence to all local safety and PPE protocols is required on the operations floor.

• Required to be onsite at the Sparks, NV Facility Monday thru Friday

jobs.title: Director, Buying & Planning
jobs.description:
Join one of the fastest growing, most dynamic companies in the furniture industry. For over 25 years, Four Hands has been a leading designer and wholesaler of furniture and décor, helping people create spaces that feel like home.

Recognized on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing companies and named one of Austin’s Top Workplaces year after year. We invest in exceptional people — with a team of over 800 and growing — fostering our employees’ careers and celebrating them at every step of the way. Four Hands is where passion meets purpose and where your next chapter begins.

The Director, Buying & Planning leads demand planning, buying, and inventory management across the business, translating the Vice President’s strategic direction into disciplined execution. This role is accountable for the quality of forecasts, inventory investments, product availability, and inventory health across categories.

As a leader within Demand and Supply Planning, you will lead the planning team and serve as a key partner to Merchandising, Sales, Product Development, Finance, and Supply Chain. You will own the planning operating rhythm, resolve complex inventory trade-offs, strengthen systems and processes, and provide the Vice President with clear insights, recommendations, and execution plans.

In This Role

• Direct demand forecasting, buying, and inventory strategies across categories, translating departmental and financial priorities into measurable plans and results

• Own the execution of demand planning, inventory optimization, and replenishment policies to achieve service-level, inventory productivity, and excess reduction targets

• Lead Open-to-Buy (OTB) management and recommend inventory investment trade-offs against revenue, margin, cash flow, and working capital objectives

• Own the planning team’s contributions to Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP), connecting category forecasts, supply constraints, financial plans, and required decisions

• Establish forecasting standards, review demand assumptions and exceptions, and direct corrective actions to improve forecast quality and product availability

• Own planning performance reviews and action plans across forecast accuracy, inventory turns, weeks of supply, service levels, aging, excess, and product availability

• Direct lifecycle and inventory investment plans with Merchandising and Product Development, including introductions, growth, replenishment, and product exits

• Influence pricing, promotional, and markdown decisions with Merchandising, Sales, and Marketing through inventory exposure and profitability analysis

• Ensure customer forecasts, sales pipeline insights, and major account needs are incorporated into demand plans, with clear validation and accountability

• Direct inventory balancing for kits, components, complete sets, and assortments to reduce stockouts and avoid stranded inventory

• Partner with international teams, sourcing teams, and suppliers to elevate lead-time reliability, production alignment, vendor performance, and supply continuity

• Lead mitigation plans for supply disruption, demand volatility, stockouts, excess inventory, and obsolescence; escalate material risks with options and recommendations

• Translate financial and inventory targets into category-level plans and monitor performance against budget, forecast, service, and working capital commitments

• Set priorities for process improvement, standardization, automation, and data quality to improve planning effectiveness, accuracy, and scalability

• Lead business requirements, testing, implementation, and adoption of planning and inventory management tools in partnership with Technology and Analytics

• Execute the planning technology roadmap established with the Vice President, ensuring processes, decision frameworks, and team capabilities evolve together

• Present business performance, scenarios, exceptions, and recommended actions to the Vice President and senior cross-functional stakeholders

• Lead cross-functional working sessions to resolve planning conflicts, establish decision ownership, and ensure timely follow-through on commitments

• Own the monthly and quarterly planning calendar, forecast and buy approvals, operating reviews, and execution controls across the planning organization

• Develop and evaluate scenarios for demand shifts, supply constraints, lead-time changes, and financial pressure; recommend fact-based actions and trade-offs

• Other duties as assigned, in accordance with training and qualifications

• Uphold the Core Values and be a valuable member of the Four Hands Team Be open and honest Reach for excellence Act with responsibility Value the whole person Enjoy the journey

Leadership and Team Management

• Lead day-to-day operations of the Buying & Planning function, setting priorities, resource plans, decision rights, and consistent execution standards

• Establish measurable team and individual objectives linked to forecast performance, availability, inventory health, and business results

• Build effective collaboration across planners, merchants, sales partners, and supply teams; ensure decisions and actions are clearly communicated

• Manage, coach, and develop planning talent through performance feedback, technical training, succession planning, and growth opportunities

• Create a culture of analytical rigor, ownership, continuous improvement, and disciplined follow-through on identified performance gaps

• Lead the team through system and process change, ensuring adoption, clarity of expectations, and sustained improvements in performance

• Allocate work and resources to deliver departmental operating plans, resolve escalated issues, and support the Vice President on priority initiatives

• Use market, business, and team performance data to identify emerging risks, capability gaps, and opportunities to improve results

The Ideal Person

• 10+ years of experience in demand planning, inventory management, merchandise planning, or buying within a complex, multi-category business

• Experience leading managers and/or experienced planners, build high-performing teams, establish accountability, and develop future leaders

• Expertise in demand forecasting, inventory flow, replenishment, and Open-to-Buy (OTB), with demonstrated ownership of planning results across multiple categories

• Proven accountability for inventory investments and financial trade-offs involving revenue, margin, service levels, cash flow, and working capital

• Experience leading S&OP or equivalent cross-functional planning cycles, translating demand and supply inputs into executable decisions

• Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience using large datasets, planning systems, and scenario analysis to guide decisions

• Demonstrated success influencing senior leaders across Merchandising, Product Development, Sales, Supply Chain, Finance, and Technology

• Strong commercial and financial acumen, including the ability to make and communicate difficult inventory and service-level trade-offs

• Deep knowledge of product lifecycle planning, assortment complexity, launches, exits, obsolescence, and inventory risk management

• Experience with global suppliers and extended supply chains, including manufacturing lead times, supplier performance, and supply constraints

• Track record of leading measurable improvements in planning performance, operating discipline, process design, and organizational scalability

• Hands-on leadership in planning technology implementations, data governance, system adoption, and analytics-driven process improvement

About Four Hands

Headquartered in Austin, Texas, since 1996, Four Hands crafts furniture, art and décor — pieces that are all about creating space. Timeless, thoughtful designs with endless possibilities. Pieces meant to be experienced and form a whole that feels like home.

Our trade customers range from interior designers to large retailers who rely on our expertise to grow and guide their business to success. We treat our partners as part of the Four Hands family, championing them and rooting for their every win.

And, we are constantly pursuing better — from sourcing the finest materials and finishes to seeking fresh inspiration to elevate our designs — we are never settled, never done.

Four Hands is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Four Hands recruits qualified applicants and advances in employment its employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, disability, genetic information, ethnic or national origin, marital status, veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Visit www.FourHands.com for more information.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, US Quality Operations
jobs.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.



With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.

As production grows, we need clear evidence that each spacecraft meets its requirements and a quality system that helps teams find and resolve risks early.

We are looking for a Senior Manager, Quality Operations to lead US quality for satellite buses and payloads from incoming material through building, test and acceptance. You will build a pragmatic system and lead engineers and inspectors close to the floor. You have independent authority to hold work or withhold readiness concurrence and to escalate unresolved mission risk. This is a hands-on leadership role in a fast-moving, dynamic environment.


WHAT YOU WILL DO:

 - Lead US quality engineers and inspectors across supplier, receiving, production and test coverage. Set training, inspection points and delegated authority.

jobs.description:

• Support the development, configuration, testing, and ongoing improvement of LogicGate workflows and applications supporting compliance and business continuity programs.
• Research and evaluate technologies and automation opportunities that improve compliance monitoring, evidence collection, data analysis, reporting, and program execution.
• Analyze program data to identify trends, discrepancies, risks, and improvement opportunities and develop dashboards and reports that provide actionable insights.
• Independently manage assigned initiatives and deliverables, establish and track milestones, resolve issues, and communicate risks, dependencies, or delays.
• Develop clear documentation, standard operating procedures, process guidance, FAQs, and other materials supporting compliance and continuity programs.
• Support the Compliance Compass communications program by researching technology and compliance topics and translating requirements into clear, practical guidance for technology teams.
• Prepare presentations, reports, and communications for technical teams, business stakeholders, and leadership.

• Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, cybersecurity, information systems, engineering, business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
• 2+ years of relevant experience in technology, IT operations, software development, cybersecurity, technology compliance, risk management, operational resilience, or a related discipline.
• Demonstrated technical aptitude and foundational knowledge of software applications, infrastructure, cloud technologies, software development, cybersecurity, or IT operations.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated ability to investigate issues, evaluate information, identify inconsistencies, and develop practical recommendations.
• Demonstrated ability to independently manage assignments, organize priorities, and follow through on deliverables.
• Experience using Excel, Power BI, or comparable analytical and reporting tools to organize, reconcile, analyze, and present data.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical concepts, findings, and requirements to technical and nontechnical audiences.
• Ability to learn unfamiliar technologies, business processes, compliance requirements, and software tools quickly.

Skills & Experience We Are Looking For

• Hands-on experience or demonstrated familiarity with cloud platforms, software development environments, source code management, CI/CD pipelines, or infrastructure technologies such as AWS, GCP, GitHub, Jenkins, or Kubernetes.
• Experience assessing or implementing technical controls associated with SOX, SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, or comparable control frameworks.
• Experience supporting business continuity planning, business impact analyses, disaster recovery, technology recovery, or operational resilience programs.
• Experience with workflow automation, scripting, data analysis, reporting, or visualization using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or Excel.
• Experience with governance, risk, and compliance platforms such as LogicGate or comparable workflow and GRC technologies.
• Graduate coursework or an advanced degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information systems, engineering, or a related discipline.
• Relevant professional certifications such as CISA, Security+, CISSP, CBCP, or comparable technology, security, audit, or resilience certifications.
• Experience working in digital media, streaming, direct-to-consumer, or other technology-intensive environments.
• Intellectual curiosity and a strong interest in understanding how technologies, systems, and processes work.
• An analytical and investigative approach, including the ability to assess the quality of information, recognize discrepancies, identify underlying issues, and reach well-supported conclusions.
• A self-directed and accountable working style, with the initiative to take ownership of assignments and drive them through completion.
• Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, well-organized work.
• Adaptability and resourcefulness when learning new tools or working across unfamiliar technical or business subject matter.
• Strong collaboration skills and the ability to build productive relationships across technical and business teams.
• A practical, improvement-focused mindset that balances compliance and control objectives with operational efficiency.

Eligibility Requirements

jobs.title: Sr. Threat Researcher
jobs.description:
Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Threat Hunter to join our Threat Hunting team in a hybrid capacity based out of our Santa Clara, CA office (3 days per week in-office) or Remote in the US reporting to the Threat Hunting Manager. In this role, you will conduct proactive and retroactive hunting operations across Zscaler and third-party telemetry—including endpoint, cloud, network, and identity data sources—to detect emerging threats and adversarial activity across customer environments. Threat hunting is the core focus of this role, empowering you to analyze large, complex datasets, execute independent investigations, translate findings into actionable detection logic, and mentor team members.

What you'll do

• Conduct proactive and retroactive threat hunting across Zscaler telemetry (ZIA, network) and third-party sources (EDR, cloud, identity) to identify threats and adversarial activity in customer environments

• Query, analyze, and correlate large, complex datasets using proprietary data platforms and SQL-based tools to surface high-fidelity security signals

• Research and analyze adversarial tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) aligned with the MITRE ATT&CK framework to formulate and test hunting hypotheses

• Translate hunting findings into actionable detection hypotheses and logic in close partnership with Detection Engineering, Threat Intelligence, and Research teams

• Document findings with technical precision for internal and customer stakeholders, while refining hunting methodologies and mentoring junior team members

Who You Are

• An analytical and inquisitive investigator with a deep passion for dissecting attacker methodologies and uncovering stealthy adversary behaviors.

• A collaborative technical partner who thrives in an in-office and hybrid environment, translating complex investigative data into actionable detection logic.

• A self-directed problem solver capable of managing high-volume, multi-source telemetry investigations independently and efficiently.

• A clear and articulate communicator who can convey intricate threat findings seamlessly to both deeply technical teams and executive customer stakeholders.

• A dedicated mentor and continuous learner eager to elevate team tradecraft, share knowledge, and foster an inclusive, high-performing culture.

What We're Looking for

• Demonstrated experience leveraging modern AI tools and workflows to enhance analytical efficiency, accelerate research, and optimize daily threat investigations

• 3+years of hands-on cybersecurity experience focused on threat hunting, incident response, security operations, or malware analysis

• Proven track record of conducting hunting across multi-source telemetry, including endpoint (EDR), network, cloud, and identity data

• Solid working knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework with demonstrated ability to analyze adversary TTPs and build hunting hypotheses

• Proficiency querying and analyzing large, complex datasets using SQL or comparable query languages

What Will Make You Stand Out

• Experience utilizing AI, LLMs, or machine learning models to accelerate threat hypothesis generation, anomaly detection, or hunting automation

• Experience working with Zscaler telemetry (ZIA, ZPA) or comparable enterprise network security platforms

• Experience developing behavioral detection rules or detection logic within SIEM environments such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or Elastic

• Scripting and automation skills in Python, paired with hands-on experience hunting across cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP)

jobs.title: Head of Retail
jobs.description:
The Role

As Head of Retail, you’ll own Triumph’s retail presence. Every card pulled in Rips is a real card, but the rip itself was built for the phone. Now we’re taking it to the places collectors already go.

Over the next few years, that means our own stores and mall kiosks, vending machines, partnerships with local card shops, and a line of physical repacks. You’ll pick the formats and markets, prove them out in pilots, scale what works, and run the network day to day.

This is a builder role. You’ll be modeling unit economics, walking malls, negotiating with landlords and card shop owners, sourcing machines and fixtures, launching repacks with our collectibles team, and on the floor when the doors open. You’ll lead retail for Triumph with the full support of the operations team, and you’ll write the playbook every future location follows. This role reports to our Senior Director of Operations.

This role is based out of Fremont, with one day a week at Triumph’s headquarters in San Francisco.

What You’ll Do

 - Set Triumph’s retail strategy: which formats, which markets, in what order, and the unit economics behind each. Own the retail P&L.

 - Open and run our own stores and mall kiosks. Select sites with our real estate team, negotiate with landlords and mall operators, and manage buildouts through opening day.

 - Build and run a fleet of vending machines, from hardware vendors and placement deals to restocking routes and uptime.

 - Build a network of partner card shops, putting Triumph product and experiences in their stores on terms that work for both sides.

 - Work with our partnerships team to land product placement and shelf space with national retailers.

 - Bring Triumph’s physical repack line to market with our collectibles team, owning pricing, production, packaging, and distribution.

 - Coordinate with operations, security, and IT so every location opens with inventory, point of sale, payments, and loss prevention ready on day one.

 - Partner with legal and compliance to clear each format and market before launch.

 - Hire, train, and lead the retail team, from store staff to field operators.

 - Build the playbook: site criteria, format standards, partner terms, vendor bench, and opening checklists.

 - Travel regularly to markets, locations, and partner shops.

Qualifications

 - 7+ years in retail operations, with direct experience launching stores, kiosks, or vending fleets.

 - Track record of taking a retail concept from pilot to multiple locations while owning the P&L.

 - Financial rigor. You can model the unit economics of a store, a kiosk, or a single machine, and defend the numbers.

 - Experience managing high-value inventory, with loss prevention built into how you operate.

 - Experience hiring and leading teams spread across multiple locations.

 - Experience opening locations under real time pressure.

 - Comfort working directly with counsel on leases and partner agreements.

 - Comfort owning a function end to end and driving work to completion without a playbook handed to you.

 - Fluency with AI tooling as a daily working habit.

 - Bonus if you’ve run both staffed retail and vending, or have existing relationships with mall operators and retail landlords.

Why Triumph?

 - High growth. Build the real-world front door to a high-scale consumer platform that touches gaming and collectibles.

 - High agency. Small, high-impact operations team with significant opportunity for leadership and growth.

 - Competitive salary and benefits. $400/mo lunch credit, healthcare, vision, dental, 401k, etc.

Founded in 2009, RTR has disrupted the $2.4 trillion fashion industry by inspiring women with a more joyful, sustainable and financially-savvy way to feel their best every day. As the ultimate destination for circular fashion, the brand now offers infinite points of access to its shared closet via a fully customizable subscription to fashion, one-time rental or ownership. You'll own the full sales cycle for this segment, from strategy and outreach through demos, proposals, and close, working closely with our CSMs, product specialists, and business development team to bring the right solutions to schools that need them.

jobs.title: Vice President, Global Commercial Partnerships
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Authentic Brands Group (Authentic) is a global brand and entertainment platform that owns and invests in iconic intellectual property and cultural assets. It accelerates brands through a set of specialized businesses that combine powerful storytelling, premium content, unforgettable live experiences and global commerce. Through a network of more than 1,700 best-in-class licensees and strategic partners across 150 countries and expansive distribution, Authentic’s brands drive more than $38 billion in annual systemwide retail sales worldwide.

Authentic’s diversified portfolio spans more than 50 brands and reaches nearly one billion social media followers. Its roster includes Reebok, Champion, Shaquille O’Neal, David Beckham, Kevin Hart, Sports Illustrated, Elvis Presley, Muhammad Ali, Marilyn Monroe, GUESS, Aéropostale, Nautica, Eddie Bauer, Lucky Brand, Nine West, Brooks Brothers, Juicy Couture, Vince Camuto, Izod, Van Heusen, Dockers, Ted Baker, Hart Schaffner Marx, Vince, Barneys New York, Judith Leiber, Quiksilver, Spyder, Billabong, Volcom, Roxy, RVCA, DC Shoes, Prince, Sperry and Hunter.

For more information, visit corporate.authentic.com. Follow Authentic on LinkedIn, Instagram and WeChat.

Why Authentic

You’ll be able to access the resources and scale, while leveraging innovative technology and nimble environment. What we’re saying is, this isn’t your average day job. If you’re hungry to drive ideas into action and own your career, let’s chat. Our team is rapidly innovating to evolve and define the future of our brands. With the help of some of the brightest minds in retail, marketing, licensing, legal and more, we are building the intersection of digital and experiential marketing to help achieve that mission. We reimagine, evolve and transform brands! At Authentic, we foster an inclusive workplace where diversity of thought and expertise drive competitive advantage. Our global teams are built by go-getters who contribute unique perspectives and push the boundaries of creativity and innovation. Headquartered in New York City, Authentic has offices in major metropolitan cities including Los Angeles and Miami, as well as Toronto, Mexico City, London, and Shanghai.

What You’ll Do

Authentic Live creates and delivers premium, turnkey branded experiences at the intersection of sports, music, fashion, lifestyle, entertainment, and culture. Through a portfolio of distinctive live events, cultural platforms, and experiential properties, we connect the world’s most influential brands with passionate audiences at some of the most prominent moments in culture.

The Vice President, Global Commercial Partnerships is a senior individual contributor responsible for driving significant new revenue across the Authentic Live portfolio. This entrepreneurial seller will leverage a strong network of brand and agency decision-makers to originate, structure, negotiate, and close high-value, multi-platform partnerships. Working closely with the EVP, Authentic Live, and cross-functional stakeholders, the VP will own the full sales cycle from prospecting and pipeline development through contracting and close, shape commercial strategy for the portfolio, and own revenue and profitability outcomes end to end.

What You’ll Be Working On

Commercial Strategy & Revenue Ownership

• Develop and execute a global commercial partnerships strategy designed to accelerate revenue growth, expand market penetration, and maximize the commercial potential of the Authentic Live portfolio.

• Own and deliver against defined annual and quarterly new-business revenue targets, with accountability for pipeline development, deal conversion, and overall sales performance.

• Set portfolio-wide commercial priorities, determining where Authentic Live focuses its partnership efforts across existing properties, new platforms, and emerging cultural moments.

• Serve as a principal commercial advisor to the EVP, Authentic Live, and executive leadership, shaping revenue priorities, sales forecasts, commercial objectives, and go-to-market strategy.

• Translate company growth objectives into the global partnerships commercial plan and target-account strategy, and own results against that plan end to end.

New Business Development & Strategic Deal Origination

• Proactively identify, prospect, and pursue high-value brand partners, with an emphasis on large-scale, multi-property, multi-year, and multi-market partnership opportunities.

• Originate and close significant commercial partnerships across Authentic Live’s portfolio, including Coachella, DUNKMAN, OVO Fest, and other large scale sports, music, lifestyle, and entertainment properties.

• Build and maintain a robust, qualified pipeline of prospective partners, leveraging existing relationships, personal networks, strategic introductions, industry intelligence, and proactive outbound sales efforts.

• Develop relationships with senior brand executives, including CMOs, chief brand officers, global marketing leaders, and agency decision-makers, to uncover business needs and position Authentic Live as a strategic commercial partner.

• Pursue opportunities that extend beyond traditional event sponsorship, including integrated brand platforms, experiential marketing, hospitality, content, talent, cultural partnerships, and year-round brand engagement.

• Own every opportunity end to end, from initial outreach through close, renewal, and expansion.

Complex Negotiation & Deal Structuring

• Lead high-stakes commercial negotiations, developing partnership structures that maximize revenue, protect margins, and deliver sustainable long-term value.

• Shape the commercial narrative for Authentic Live’s largest and most strategic pursuits, connecting Authentic Live’s assets and capabilities to prospective partners’ marketing, business, and brand objectives.

• Structure integrated partnership packages that leverage multiple properties, rights, experiences, markets, and activation opportunities to increase deal size and commercial value.

• Navigate complex deal cycles involving multiple decision-makers, procurement teams, legal counsel, agencies, and internal stakeholders.

• Drive negotiations to timely and successful close while balancing partner needs, inventory availability, contractual obligations, delivery costs, and business priorities.

• Identify opportunities to expand initial deals into broader portfolio relationships, renewals, extensions, and incremental revenue streams.

Financial Accountability & P&L Management

• Own the financial performance of the global partnerships book of business, with end-to-end accountability for revenue targets, deal economics, and contribution to overall portfolio profitability.

• Develop and manage sales forecasts, pipeline reporting, revenue projections, and close plans, providing the EVP and executive leadership with clear visibility into expected performance, risks, and opportunities.

• Evaluate deal structures, pricing, rights packages, and partnership economics to ensure proposed agreements align with approved financial objectives.

• Work cross-functionally with finance and event operations to assess fulfillment costs, activation requirements, resource commitments, and anticipated margins.

• Define and uphold pricing and margin guardrails for partnership deals, in partnership with Finance, so revenue growth is profitable and deliverable.

• Monitor performance against targets and proactively implement strategies to address pipeline gaps, conversion challenges, or revenue shortfalls.

Market Intelligence & Commercial Innovation

• Serve as Authentic Live’s authority on the global brand marketing, sponsorship, experiential, entertainment, and live events landscape, bringing an outside-in perspective that informs executive decisions on portfolio, pricing, and growth.

• Identify emerging categories, high-growth brands, new spending opportunities, and shifts in marketing investment that can create commercial advantages for Authentic Live.

• Monitor competitor activity and partnership trends to inform pricing, positioning, sales strategy, and product development.

• Drive the development of new partnership products and commercial models with internal teams, that respond to market demand and unlock new revenue opportunities.

• Bring an entrepreneurial mindset to the business, challenging conventional sponsorship models and developing creative commercial solutions that distinguish Authentic Live in the marketplace.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Deal Delivery

• Work closely with the EVP, Authentic Live, and internal stakeholders across event operations, marketing, talent, creative, legal, finance, and production to develop commercially viable partnership solutions.

• Ensure proposed partnerships are aligned with the capabilities, rights, inventory, and operational realities of each property.

• Facilitate a seamless transition from signed agreement to fulfillment, ensuring commercial commitments are clearly documented and communicated to the teams responsible for delivery.

• Hold accountability for partnership outcomes from sale through delivery, surfacing material risks, resource requirements, or contractual considerations to executive leadership and resolving issues across teams.

• Serve as a senior face of Authentic Live to the market, representing the company in C-suite client meetings, industry events, partner presentations, and commercial negotiations.

Must Haves

• Experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in global partnerships, sponsorship sales, business development, experiential marketing, or commercial sales within sports, music, entertainment, media, lifestyle, or related industries.

• Proven Sales Performance: Demonstrated success originating and closing multi-million-dollar commercial partnerships, with a track record of consistently meeting or exceeding significant revenue targets.

• New Business Hunter: A proactive, entrepreneurial sales mentality with the ability to build a pipeline from the ground up, generate new opportunities, and convert senior-level relationships into meaningful commercial outcomes.

• Executive-Level Network: Established relationships with senior brand marketers, global marketing executives, agency leaders, and commercial decision-makers across relevant industries.

• Commercial Acumen: Strong understanding of sponsorship valuation, partnership economics, pricing strategy, deal structuring, revenue forecasting, and profit-margin considerations.

• Strategic Negotiation: Proven ability to lead complex, high-value negotiations and navigate sophisticated deal cycles involving multiple stakeholders.

• Financial Fluency: Experience evaluating deal profitability, managing commercial forecasts, assessing financial trade-offs, and making decisions informed by revenue and margin objectives.

• Strategic Thinking & Execution: Ability to develop a compelling commercial strategy while remaining highly hands-on in prospecting, pitching, negotiating, and closing business.

• Communication & Presentation: Exceptional verbal, written, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence senior executives and communicate sophisticated partnership propositions clearly and persuasively.

• Analytical Capabilities: Ability to leverage market intelligence, pipeline analytics, financial data, and performance metrics to prioritize opportunities and improve commercial outcomes.

• Autonomy & Accountability: Comfortable operating as a senior individual contributor in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment, taking ownership of results and working independently while collaborating across the organization.

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Sports Management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

• Travel: Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required for client meetings, property visits, events, and industry conferences.

Core Competencies

• Hunter Mentality: Relentless focus on prospecting, building relationships, and closing new business.

• Commercial Ownership: Owns revenue outcomes, pipeline health, and deal economics end to end for the global partnerships business.

• Strategic Deal-Making: Identifies ways to grow partnership value for both the brand and Authentic Live.

• Executive Presence: Builds trust with senior decision-makers and represents Authentic Live confidently in high-stakes settings.

• Results Orientation: Moves opportunities forward with urgency and a focus on measurable outcomes.

• Entrepreneurial Thinking: Identifies new markets, categories, and partnership models that expand the business and create competitive differentiation.

• Financial Discipline: Balances aggressive growth objectives with thoughtful pricing, sound deal structures, margin protection, and commercial sustainability.

• Collaboration & Influence: Aligns stakeholders and resolves issues across teams to move complex deals forward.

jobs.title: Medical Affairs Director
jobs.description:
About Equip 

Equip is the leading virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment program on a mission to ensure that everyone with an eating disorder can access treatment that works. Created by clinical experts in the field and people with lived experience, Equip builds upon evidence-based treatments to empower individuals to reach lasting recovery. All Equip patients receive a dedicated care team, including a therapist, dietitian, physician, and peer and family mentor. The company operates in all 50 states and is partnered with most major health insurance plans. Learn more about our strong outcomes https://equip.health/outcomes and treatment approach at www.equip.health. http://www.equip.health

Founded in 2019, Equip has been a fully virtual company since its inception and is proud of the highly-engaged, passionate, and diverse Equipsters that have created Equip’s culture.  Recognized by Time https://time.com/collection/time100-companies-2023/6285207/equip/ as one of the most influential companies of 2023, along with awards from Linkedin https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-top-startups-2022-50-us-companies-rise-linkedin-news/ and Lattice https://lattice.com/blog/announcing-the-2023-finalists-for-lattices-people-success-awards, we are grateful to Equipsters for building a sustainable treatment program that has served thousands of patients and families.

About the role

Equip is seeking a distinguished Medical Affairs Director to serve as a key clinical expert, strategic partner, and brand ambassador as we scale our evidence-based eating disorder care. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Clinical Affairs, this leader will play a dual role: serving as an internal clinical escalation resource for complex cases while actively driving external engagement, provider outreach, and thought leadership.

In this high-visibility role, you will collaborate closely with Patient Acquisition, Marketing, and Clinical Training teams to amplify Equip’s mission through medical advocacy, peer-to-peer education, and strategic partnership development. Whether hosting virtual provider roundtables, speaking at national conferences, or consulting on strategic pilot programs, you will serve as the medical voice connecting Equip’s clinical excellence with the broader healthcare community.


Responsibilities

 - Serve as a consulted clinical expert for multidisciplinary treatment teams on complex, high-acuity adolescent cases, offering medical guidance and documenting recommendations in the EMR per Equip policies.

 - Communicate and collaborate with outside physicians, external providers, payors, and strategic partners to answer questions about Equip’s evidence-based treatment model and facilitate care coordination.

 - Collaborate with the VP of Clinical Affairs and commercial teams on growth initiatives, including pilot program development, transition track introductions, and clinical advocacy projects.

 - Provide expert input on emerging trends, clinical guidelines, and innovations in adolescent medicine and eating disorder treatment to inform internal policies, training curriculum, and external marketing/educational content.

 - Participate in clinical leadership syncs, supervision, and interdisciplinary discussions to ensure seamless alignment across Clinical Affairs, Care Ops, and Commercial teams.

 - Support external education and relationship-building with referring providers, collaborating organizations, and payors.

 - Offer clinical insight to support internal policies and external messaging, educational content, and communications.

 - Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

 - MD or DO degree with board certification in Family Medicine, Pediatrics,  Internal Medicine, or Adolescent Medicine.

 - Active, unrestricted medical license, with willingness to obtain additional licenses as needed (Equip fully covers licensing fees).

 - 10+ years of active clinical practice, with deep expertise in eating disorder medical management, high-acuity telehealth care, and interdisciplinary care coordination.

 - Proven experience as a clinical spokesperson with a track record of building external strategic partnerships (e.g., payors, health systems, referral networks).

 - Exceptional communication skills with demonstrated comfort presenting, advising, and articulating clinical value to both clinical and executive audiences.

Compensation & Benefits Package

Compensation: 

 - Earning Potential Range: $195,000 - $245,000 + 15% Annual Performance Bonus Potential

Time Off:

 - Flex PTO policy (3-5 wks/year recommended) + 11 paid company holidays.

 - Generous parental leave.

Core Benefits:

 - Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and AD&D insurance.
   
   - Equip pays for a significant percentage of benefits premiums for individuals and families.

 - Spring Health, a 100% employer-paid mental health benefit through Guardian.
   
   - You can receive 5 free therapy sessions and 5 free coaching sessions per year for you and each of your dependents.

 - Employee Assistance Program (EAP), a company paid resource for mental health, legal services, financial support, and more!

 - HealthJoy, a 100% employer-paid platform connecting you to a healthcare concierge who can help you navigate your benefits.

 - 401K Option!

Work From Home Additional Perks:

 - $50/month stipend to cover home internet expenses.

 - $250/month stipend to use a co-working space.

 - Initial work-from-home stipend of up to $500.
   
   - Reload of $200 on the home office stipend at the 3-year mark and then every other year after that (year 5, year 7, etc.).

 - Company Laptop.

Physical Demands

Work is performed 100% from home with limited travel required. This is a stationary position that requires the ability to operate standard office equipment and keyboards as well as to talk or hear by telephone. Sit or stand as needed.

At Equip, Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) are woven into everything we do. At the heart of Equip’s mission is a relentless dedication to making sure that everyone with an eating disorder has access to care that works regardless of race, gender, sexuality, ability, weight, socio-economic status, and any marginalized identity. We also strive toward our providers and corporate team reflecting that same dedication both in bringing in and retaining talented employees from all backgrounds and identities. We have an Equip DEIB council, Equip For All; also referred to as EFA. EFA at Equip aims to be a space driven by mutual respect, and thoughtful, effective communication strategy - enabling full participation of  members who identify as marginalized or under-represented and allies, amplifying diverse voices, creating opportunities for advocacy and contributing to the advancement of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging at Equip.

As an equal opportunity employer, we provide equal opportunity in all aspects of employment, including recruiting, hiring, compensation, training and promotion, termination, and any other terms and conditions of employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, familial status, age, disability, weight, and/or any other legally protected classification protected by federal, state, or local law. 

Our dedication to equitable access, which is core to our mission, extends to how we build our "village." In line with our commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB), we are dedicated to an accessible hiring process where all candidates feel a true sense of belonging. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete your application, interview, or perform the essential functions of a role, we invite you to reach out to our People team at accommodations@equip.health.
