jobs.description:
About Wing:

Wing offers drone delivery as a safe, fast, and sustainable solution for last mile logistics. Consumer appetites for on-demand services are increasing, but current delivery methods are inefficient, costly, and contribute to road accidents and air pollution. Wing’s fleet of highly automated delivery drones can transport small packages directly from businesses to homes on-demand, in minutes. We design, build, and operate our aircraft, and offer drone delivery services on two continents. Our technology is designed to be easy to integrate into existing delivery and logistics networks, offering a scalable drone delivery solution for a broad range of businesses. Wing is a part of Google's parent company, Alphabet, and our mission is to create the preferred means of delivery for the planet. If you're ready to do the greatest work of your life, come join us.

About the Role:

Wing is looking for a Senior Counsel, Employment to join our Legal team. This role is based remotely in the United States. As Senior Counsel, Employment, you will serve as Wing’s lead employment attorney and strategic legal partner to Human Resources, People Operations, and operational leadership across our rapidly scaling global business. In this role, you will provide comprehensive legal counseling across the entire employee lifecycle, including multi-state remote workforce compliance, recruiting, wage and hour, performance management, leaves of absence, accommodations, and employee relations. You will also spearhead Wing's contingent workforce and TVC (Temporary, Vendor, Contractor) governance strategy, partnering with Operations and Sourcing to mitigate co-employment risk across ground operations and technical staffing vendors, and advising on FAA/DOT Part 135/107 safety-sensitive workforce compliance and OSHA safety standards.

The ideal candidate brings deep employment counseling expertise, high emotional intelligence, practical business judgment, and experience navigating both corporate tech and field operations labor models in a high-growth environment.

What You’ll Do:

• Serve as the primary legal advisor to Wing People Ops team and business leaders on recruiting, performance management, employee relations, discipline, reorganizations, terminations, and severance.

• Partner with Operations, Sourcing, and vendor management teams to structure and govern vendor contracts, establish independent contractor and staffing classifications, and mitigate joint-employer/co-employment liabilities.

• Lead and oversee sensitive workplace investigations, resolve employee grievances, draft separation agreements, and manage administrative charges (EEOC and state agencies) and outside counsel.

• Author, maintain, and audit Wing’s employee handbooks, remote work policies, and disability/leave accommodation workflows, delivering engaging training programs for people managers.

• Provide specialized counseling on FAA/DOT Part 135 and Part 107 employment standards, mandatory DOT drug and alcohol testing programs for safety-sensitive flight operations, and OSHA safety protocols across flight facilities.

What You’ll Need:

• 12+ years of relevant employment law experience in a top-tier law firm and in-house legal department supporting technology, logistics, or multi-state operational workforces

• Active Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing with at least one US state bar

• Proven track record counseling high-growth tech or logistics organizations, scaling employment compliance frameworks, and managing multi-state remote workforces

• Deep expertise in federal and multi-state employment laws, FLSA wage and hour classifications, FMLA/state leaves, and ADA/FEHA accommodations, with substantial experience in contingent workforce governance

• Exceptional interpersonal, communication, and drafting skills with strong emotional intelligence and the ability to partner collaboratively across People, Legal, and Operations teams.

• Preferred: Experience with aviation, aerospace, or transportation labor regulations (e.g., FAA/DOT safety-sensitive roles, mandatory DOT drug/alcohol testing, OSHA compliance)

jobs.title: AFC Operations Investigator
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Imprint is on a mission to make every customer a regular.

You know how it feels when you walk into your favorite coffee shop and they know your name and start prepping your usual? Imprint makes it possible for the largest brands to create that experience at scale.

We bring payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence together in one platform, so brands can recognize and reward customers as individuals and keep them coming back. With the power of our technology and data, brands create financial products that their customers’ use everyday, earning more of their spend and increasing loyalty. Customers are rewarded with money and time saved, and surprised and delighted with a more unique, tailored experience.

We first proved our business in co-brand credit cards. For decades, the same few banks dominated the industry, building brands’ programs on mainframes older than the internet. We took a different approach, rebuilding the technology from the ground up. Today, Imprint has more than two million members, with partners like Shell, Kroger, H-E-B, and Booking.com http://Booking.com representing half a trillion dollars in total US consumer spend. Now, we’re growing our partnerships, bringing on more members, and expanding beyond credit cards so that brands offer more ways to pay and be rewarded to recognize their customers as individuals no matter their income or preferences.

Better yet, we’re doing it differently with a lean team of the most talented people on earth. Historically, companies scaled by adding people. Imprint is taking on our opportunity with a small team of exceptional people, with the best AI and technology dramatically amplifying what each person can accomplish. That means you’ll learn faster here than you could anywhere else. You’ll be one of the few people building an entirely new technology with the ownership and trust to shape what Imprint becomes. You’ll work alongside people who make you sharper everyday, armed with tools that turn your best ideas into reality faster than you thought possible. This is a rare chance to do the most important work of your career and to help prove that a small team can build what’s never been done before, inside industries that haven’t changed in decades.



Role Summary

As an AFC Operations Investigator, you will support our AFC (Anti-Financial Crimes) Operations team, which protects Imprint, our partner banks, and our cardholders by detecting, investigating, and reporting money laundering and other illicit activity in line with the Bank Secrecy Act and our BSA/AML program. You'll review transaction monitoring alerts, conduct thorough BSA/AML investigations, and make clear, well-documented case decisions, including preparing Unusual Activity Report (UAR) referrals to our partner banks.

We take an AI-native approach: questioning repetitive work, exploring better investigative methods, and finding practical ways to improve speed and quality, paired with sound investigative judgment, clear documentation, and accountability for every decision. As Imprint launches new products, you'll help us recognize emerging risks and strengthen how we investigate them.

This is a fully remote contract role, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM in your local time zone, with flexibility as needed.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

 - Working the AFC Operations alert queue independently, meeting established service level agreements with consistently high-quality decisions

 - Writing case narratives and UAR referrals that meet partner bank expectations with minimal revisions

 - Handling sanctions (OFAC) screening reviews and FinCEN 314(a) requests end to end

 - Identified at least one recurring workflow issue and proposed a practical fix, including where AI tools can safely speed up the work

 - Earned trust as a sharp, reliable investigator who raises emerging risks early

Responsibilities

 - Review transaction monitoring alerts in the AFC Operations queue and document clear, well-supported decisions

 - Conduct in-depth BSA/AML investigations into escalated cases to identify potential money laundering and other suspicious activity

 - Write clear, concise, and well-supported case narratives and UAR referrals that meet regulatory and partner bank expectations

 - Support sanctions (OFAC) screening reviews, FinCEN 314(a) requests, and other ad hoc BSA/AML investigations as needed

 - Determine which activity warrants referral, and escalate potential high-risk activity and emerging trends to partner banks in a timely manner

 - Manage case volume effectively, balancing productivity and urgency with quality decisions and established service level agreements

 - Use approved AI tools to support research, analysis, and documentation, verifying material facts against source records and owning the final case assessment

 - Identify emerging patterns, gaps in available information, and recurring workflow issues, and communicate clear examples and recommended next steps

 - Adapt to new products, transaction patterns, and investigative procedures while maintaining consistent standards for evidence and documentation

Qualifications

Required

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience reviewing transaction monitoring alerts and conducting BSA/AML investigations, including writing SAR/UAR narratives

 - Working knowledge of BSA/AML regulations, OFAC sanctions, suspicious activity red flags, and SAR/UAR filing requirements

 - Familiarity with KYC and enhanced due diligence (EDD) practices

 - Sound investigative judgment: you can identify patterns in transaction data, distinguish suspicious activity from unusual but explainable behavior, weigh conflicting evidence, and recognize when further investigation or escalation is needed

 - Experience writing investigative narratives that clearly support a case decision

 - Ability to use or quickly learn AI-assisted workflows, recognize unsupported conclusions, verify outputs, and handle sensitive information in line with company requirements

 - Ability to work independently and resolve cases within service level agreements

 - Ability to learn new products and tools quickly, manage changing priorities, and raise questions early when information or guidance is incomplete

 - Strong written and verbal communication, exceptional organization, and attention to detail

 - High school diploma, GED, or equivalent certification; Bachelor's degree preferred

Nice to Have

 - CAMS, CFE, or other AML or financial crimes certification

 - Experience with sanctions and politically exposed person (PEP) screening reviews

 - Credit card or fintech industry experience

 - Experience with SQL or Snowflake

 - Prior experience at a high-growth startup






PERKS & BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation and equity

 - Medical plan options fully paid by Imprint, including coverage for your dependents 

 - 100% company-paid dental and vision plan options

 - Mental health support through Spring Health, plus a confidential Employee Assistance Program

 - Healthcare navigation through Rightway, plus HSA, FSA and commuter benefits

 - Flexible paid time off

 - 20 weeks of paid parental leave for primary caregivers and 8 weeks for all new parents

 - The latest tools and technology, including AI, so you can do your best work
   
   

Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Are you ready to join a team committed to making a meaningful impact on cancer treatment through the discovery and development of precision medicines? At Kura Oncology, you have an opportunity to be a part of something bigger, with a lasting impact that you can be proud of.

At Kura Oncology, we are working to change the paradigm and improve the science of cancer treatment. As an organization, we strive to cultivate a diverse and talented professional culture driven to develop precision medicine therapeutics.

As we continue to build a leading biotech organization with a strong culture, a patient-focused mindset and a team focused on relentless execution, we are looking for innovative, passionate professionals to join us and make our vision a reality.

To succeed at Kura, you will need to have a demonstrated ability for excellence in drug discovery and development and a roll-up your sleeves attitude. The ideal candidate will possess a values-driven work style where integrity and grit drive all behaviors, decisions, and actions.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

As a key member of the CMC Leadership Team, the Executive Director, Supply Chain, will drive the strategic vision, operational execution, and regulatory compliance of our clinical supply operations. This role is responsible for ensuring the seamless and compliant global distribution of investigational medicinal products, supporting clinical programs critical to our pipeline. Reporting to the SVP, Manufacturing & Supply Chain, this leader will collaborate cross-functionally with Clinical Development, Clinical Operations, Regulatory, Quality, CMC, and Commercial teams, providing senior-level guidance on clinical supply strategy.

• Responsible for leading and developing drug supply strategy, planning, and overall management of all aspects of drug supply chain activities including global Phase I – III clinical studies as well as commercial drug supply chain activities.

• Responsible for providing strategic leadership and vision for Investigational Medicinal Supply Chain (IMSC) and associated department staff.

• Responsible for providing operational leadership and oversight of commercial drug packaging, labeling, distribution and 3PL activities in collaboration with the commercial sales organization.

• Responsible for management of IMSC activities and demonstrating operational excellence in developing, and executing interdependent workflows with Clinical Operations, Quality Assurance and Global Project Team management to ensure successful Drug Development Activities are achieved across all areas of IMSC deliverables.

• Contribute vital tactical support and leadership in supply chain and logistics management while identifying and pursuing strategic opportunities to improve IMSC capacity, forecasting & planning models, all IP materials including comedications, comparators, and processes, IVRS management, and overall IMSC performance and efficiencies.

• Establish operating policies and procedures and provide comprehensive coordination of complex global supply chain operations, inventories, materials, and procurement while ensuring compliance to worldwide regulations and guidelines.

• Coordinate drug supply delivery timelines with Clinical and CMC; Packaging, Labeling, and Distribution CRO’s; and indirectly with GMP manufacturers, QA, and Regulatory Affairs.

• Lead the team in monitoring and tracking global clinical supply inventories at the clinical site level for studies; maintain forecasts and provide inventory and logistics management of IP adjusting drug distribution plans with coordination of packaging, labeling at Contract Packaging and Procurement Vendors.

• Provide IMSC project leadership and management, and act as knowledgeable resource for establishment of effective collaboration with Clinical Operations for seamless delivery of IP to patients worldwide.

• Manage extensive internal and external touchpoints and maintain close communications with all IMSC groups to ensure the adequate supply of clinical supplies throughout the duration of multiple WW clinical trials including oversight of drug order requests, resupply, and processes.

• Support financial planning for global clinical supplies, including budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning activities for clinical trials; and reconciliation of drug distribution invoices with finance staff to maximize productivity, efficiency, and overall business performance.

• Contribute and review the preparation of clinical protocols, clinical trial pharmacy manuals, packaging methods, batch records, drug labels, shipping documents, destruction certification, and coordinate the origination, proofing and translation of clinical study labels and generation and updating with quality assurance all IMSC related SOP’s.

JOB SPECIFICATIONS:

• Technical degree or equivalent (BS / MS), preferably in a scientific or pharmaceutical discipline

• 15+ years of leadership experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry, with a proven track record of leading and scaling clinical supply chain organizations.

• Demonstrated ability to set and execute long-term strategic goals for clinical supply chain operations, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives.

• Extensive experience engaging with executive leadership teams, including presenting strategic plans, risk mitigation strategies, and operational performance metrics.

• Proven success managing complex global supply chain operations, including vendor partnerships, contract negotiations, and compliance with international regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.).

• Strong financial acumen, including oversight of clinical supply budgets, cost efficiency initiatives, and long-term investment planning.

• Enterprise-wide leadership experience, with the ability to influence and collaborate across departments, ensuring clinical supply chain integration into R&D and commercial strategies.

• Track record of building and leading high-performing teams, including succession planning, talent development, and organizational effectiveness.

• Proven expertise in managing regulatory inspections, audits, and compliance strategies in collaboration with Quality and Regulatory Affairs.

• Deep technical knowledge of clinical trial supply planning, including forecasting, IVRS/IRT systems, inventory management, and GMP/GCP compliance.

• Exceptional executive communication skills, with experience presenting to senior leadership, external partners, and regulatory agencies.

• Drives and influences high-impact, cross-functional decision-making at the portfolio level, shaping strategy and aligning senior stakeholders to achieve business objectives.

• Leads cross-functional decision-making by proactively shaping and aligning stakeholders across functions, influencing program strategy and key development milestones.

The base range for an Executive Director $288,000 - $328,000 per year. Individual pay may vary based on additional factors, including, and without limitation, job-related skills, experience, work location, and relevant education or training. Kura's compensation package also includes generous benefits, equity, and participation in an annual target bonus.

Kura’s Values that are used for candidate selection and performance assessments:

• We work as one for patients

• We are goal-focused and deliver with excellence

• We are science-driven courageous innovators

• We strive to bring out the best in each other and ourselves

The Kura Package

• Career advancement/ development opportunities

• Competitive comp package

• Bonus

• 401K + Employer contributions

• Generous stock options

• ESPP Plan

• 20 days of PTO to start

• 18 Holidays (Including Summer & Winter Break)

• Paid Paternity/Maternity Leave

• Home Office Setup

• Lifestyle Spending Stipend

• Regular employee social activities, including happy hours, monthly birthday celebrations, Kura Koffee Talks, and much more!

Kura Oncology is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering and developing innovative precision medicines to help patients with cancer lead better, longer lives.

Through our deep understanding of cancer biology and decades of experience in precision oncology, we are studying the underlying causes of treatment resistance. This enables us to design smart combination regimens with other cancer therapies to target tumors from multiple directions, with the goal of improving long-term clinical benefit.

Kura developed and is commercializing KOMZIFTI® (ziftomenib), the FDA-approved once-daily, oral menin inhibitor for the treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated acute myeloid leukemia, and continues to pioneer advancements in menin inhibition and farnesyl transferase inhibition. For additional information, please visit Kura’s website at www.kuraoncology.com and follow us on X and LinkedIn.

jobs.title: Co-op, Human Resources
jobs.description:
Why Join Us?

Be a hero for our rare disease patients

At Ultragenyx, we fundamentally believe that taking real impactful action to care for the needs of patients and our people is always the right thing to do. To achieve this goal, our vision is to lead the future of rare disease medicine. jobs.title: Technical Account Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT US


Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.



We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: connect, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on.



We’ve raised $28.4 million from top tier VCs (including Matrix, ARTIS and Y Combinator), found product market fit (multi million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health), and have years of runway ahead of us. If you’ve had a good healthcare experience in the past few years, there’s a good chance Metriport was behind it. That’s the version of healthcare we want people to not just expect, but demand. Join us and build the future.

About You 

We're a small, high output team, mostly former founders including YC alumni, and we operate with real autonomy and almost no bureaucracy. We hire on competence, not pedigree. Leaders are in the office six days a week, and we generally expect the team to be available six days a week too. Not because we count hours, but because there's always more wood to chop when revolutionizing how tomorrow’s healthcare providers deliver care to their patients today. We trust our team to take the time off they need and we've never said no to a time off request.

You have an entrepreneurial mindset and a strong sense of ownership. You don't wait to be told what's broken. Instead, you believe you can figure out any problem that lands in your lap even outside your exact domain. When someone scopes something for three weeks, you ask why it can't be done in three days, and you also know the difference between shipping a fast v0 and cutting a corner that comes back to bite you. You walk the tightrope between craft and speed without falling off either side.


 - You are obsessed with customer experience, your goal is not to simply maintain relationships, but expand them. You’re an expert relationship manager.

 - You blend your technical skills and knowledge with customer success and sales mindset to effectively solution with CTOs, CPOs, and other technical executives.

 - You’re in this for the marathon not a sprint. Metriport is looking for a committed team member to own some of our largest customer accounts long term.




THE ROLE

As a Technical Account Manager at Metriport, you'll be the technical bridge between our production customers and our product, ensuring they continuously can extract maximum value from Metriport's platform while building the kind of trust that makes expansion a natural outcome. This is not a traditional account management role. You’re technically fluent, spot customer needs with ease, and can hop on a call with a customer's team (engineering, clinical, etc.) and immediately earn their respect and consideration.



This role requires an expert relationships manager. You will pair your deep understanding of Metriport’s product and features with your intimate understanding of our customer’s needs to propose solutions and expansion. Additionally, you’ll be empowered and held accountable for creating and implementing new Customer Success processes, automated monitoring systems, and touch points with customers.



In the first few months, you’ll be working closely with our Chief of Staff, Founding Engineer, and Customer Success team to elevate Metriport’s account management efforts. You’ll be responsible for:



 - Owning Customer Health & Retention: Own the north star retention metrics for customers in production.

 - Driving Value Led Growth: Identify and unlock expansion opportunities organically by ensuring customers are fully utilizing the product and seeing measurable ROI. Revenue growth follows value delivery.

 - Evolving With Customers: Spot which of Metriport’s customers are not using features that could drive significant value for their organizations. Monitor customers’ usage so Metriport can scale with their needs.

 - Building Cadenced & Ad Hoc Customer Efforts: Build and further check in efforts with Metriport’s customers in production and ad hoc efforts
   
   


REQUIREMENTS

 - Experience: 7+ years working in a customer facing technical role (e.g., Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer) with 4+ years at one company. You’ve also dabbled in formal or informal Technical Sales roles and efforts.

 - Technical Fluency: Experience working on a technical product. Comfortable reading API documentation and translating technical concepts to non technical stakeholders (and vice versa).

 - Company Experience: We’re looking for a team member who has experience at both an early stage startup and a later stage company that has scaled Customer Success (Series D or larger).

 - Core Competency: Expert at managing complex enterprise deals for extended periods of time and increasing customer usage.

 - Ambiguity Tolerance: You thrive in fast paced environments and know how to drive projects to completion without a playbook.

 - Location: Based in San Francisco (or willing to relocate). Our team prioritizes collaborating in person together as frequently as possible during the week.

 - The "Metriport" Mindset: Low ego, high ownership. You ask "Why can't this be done in 3 days?" instead of 3 weeks.

 - Open to Travel: Minimal travel is expected, but we’re looking for a team member with the flexibility and willingness to do what it takes to provide our customers with the best experience possible.
   
   


BONUS POINTS

 - Domain: Expert level domain knowledge and experience in Healthcare IT or the Healthtech space, including relevant technical standards (e.g., FHIR, HL7).

 - Engineering Background: You've written production code, built or consumed REST APIs + webhooks, or come from a software engineering role before transitioning to a customer facing one.
   
   


BENEFITS

 - Equity: Competitive equity + compensation package 🚀

 - Healthcare: Full family Platinum health insurance, dental, and vision coverage 🦷

 - Retirement: 401(k) retirement plan + matching 💰

 - Flexibility: Flexible work from home or in office 🏢

 - Food: Healthy lunches complimentary when in office (and breakfast + dinners as needed) 🍏

 - Gear: MacBook provided by us 💻

 - PTO: Unlimited PTO (we work hard, but trust you to take the time you need to be at your best) 🧘‍♂️
   
   

Metriport provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff to the CFO
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview

Reporting to the CFO at Director level, you’ll work on the decisions that shape how CHAOS grows and how that growth is funded.

You will run the Finance operating cadence, CFO-sponsored initiatives through implementation, and re-architect the finance operating model ahead of each step change in scale. You will hold delegated decision rights in named areas, so the CFO’s attention goes only where the CFO’s attention is the thing that’s actually needed.

You’ll work with Finance, Growth, Operations, and People to connect the numbers to what’s happening on the ground. You will partner with Corporate Development and Investor Relations to drive internal diligence workstream in equity raises and support the CFO in selected investor discussions.

Responsibilities

• Set the agenda for CFO operating reviews. Write concise decision briefs, maintain the decision log, and escalate risks or commitments that need leadership attention.

• Own the CFO’s board preparation calendar. Work backward from each meeting to set drafting, review, and approval deadlines. Coordinate contributions with Finance and other teams and track follow-up.

• Represent the CFO in required forums. Own the weekly flash. Reconcile inputs on bookings, backlog, revenue, margin, cash, and hiring. Explain what moved, what drove it, and what needs a decision.

• Maintain a forward view of where the current finance operating model breaks. Identify which processes, controls, and systems fail at the next leg of growth, and drive the fix before they do.

• Be the CFO’s technical counterpart with Data and Engineering. You should be able to interrogate the data yourself rather than queue for someone who can.

• Draft investor updates, board materials, and pre-meeting briefs with the CFO and Corporate Development.

• Take CFO-sponsored initiatives, including capital allocation review, pricing and margin governance.

Minimum Requirements

• 4–8 years in one of strategic finance, investment banking, private equity, consulting or as a Chief of Staff to a CFO office.

• Ability to build and challenge an operating model, interpret financial and operating metrics, and write clearly for senior leaders.

• Experience leading a cross-functional workstream through delivery, securing commitments without formal authority, and following through when priorities shift.

• Sound judgment and discretion with confidential financial, investor, board, and personnel information.

Preferred Requirements

• Experience preparing materials for a board, investment committee, or investors, or running a transaction diligence workstream.

• Experience working with a CFO or senior executive in a growth business, including operating reviews or hiring with Recruiting.

• Exposure to defense, aerospace, manufacturing, or other hardware-software businesses.

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: rree daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $175,000–$250,000

jobs.title: Medical Science Liaison
jobs.description:
Remix Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel small molecule therapies designed to reprogram RNA processing and address disease drivers at their origin. Remix's REMaster™ technology platform leverages data science, biomolecular sciences, and chemistry to identify orally administered compounds that modulate gene expression. This approach led to the discovery of REM-422, an investigational small molecule designed to modulate RNA processing in oncology. REM-422 is being evaluated in two clinical programs: the ARIA Phase 1/2 study in adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC), and a Phase 1 study in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (HR-MDS).

In June 2026, Remix announced an agreement to merge with Passage Bio, with the combined company expected to operate as Remix Therapeutics and trade on Nasdaq. The announced transaction included a concurrent $100 million private placement intended to support continued development of its pipeline. Remix remains focused on translating its RNA-processing science into meaningful treatment options for patients with significant unmet medical needs.

Position Summary:

We are hiring two Medical Science Liaisons: one to cover the Eastern U.S. territory and one to cover the Western U.S. territory.

As one of our first Medical Science Liaisons, you will help establish how we engage the rare oncology community through credible, balanced scientific exchange and a deep understanding of the needs of patients and treating teams. With no approved targeted therapies for ACC today, there is a significant opportunity to deepen scientific understanding and educate the medical community.

This role is suited to a scientific or clinical professional who enjoys both external engagement and building practical capabilities from the ground up. You will focus on academic centers, initially in rare solid tumors such as ACC, while helping shape a field medical model that can support additional indications as the pipeline evolves.

Key Responsibilities:

• Build and maintain relationships with key opinion leaders (KOLs), healthcare professionals, and other stakeholders across the head and neck oncology community

• Communicate clinical and scientific data to KOLs and healthcare professionals through presentations, educational programs, and scientific discussions

• Lead disease-state and scientific education on ACC biology and unmet need

• Develop and execute strategic KOL engagement plans with clear objectives, relevant data sharing, and scientific alignment

• Support the generation of scientific and medical knowledge and apply subject matter expertise to company priorities

• Partner with Clinical Development and Clinical Operations on investigator and site engagement and scientific questions within approved study processes

• Contribute scientific expertise to medical plans, advisory boards, congress activities, educational materials, medical information responses, and training as the field medical function takes shape

• Work closely with colleagues in Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, Patient Advocacy, and other functions to support pre- and post-launch activities

• Act as an internal expert on therapeutic area trends, clinical practice insights, and competitive intelligence

• Document interactions appropriately; follow company policies for adverse-event and product-complaint reporting, unsolicited requests, and pre-approval scientific exchange

Qualifications:

• Advanced degree in a relevant scientific or clinical discipline required; PharmD, PhD, MD, DO, NP, or equivalent preferred

• Ability to discuss complex translational and clinical data with oncology specialists

jobs.title: Associate Security Engineer
jobs.description:
The Team + The Role

Pendo's Information Security team protects the data entrusted to Pendo and helps make sure our products are built with security and privacy by design. The team spans Security Operations, Product Security and Compliance. Security Operations monitors for threats, investigates alerts and responds to incidents across our Google Cloud environment, identities and SaaS apps. The team pairs traditional analyst work with security engineering, so people both investigate and build. We are moving toward AI-assisted workflows that take on repetitive triage while people stay accountable for high-impact decisions.

As an Associate Security Engineer, you will join Security Operations to help with threat detection, incident response, monitoring and security automation. You will learn the work by doing it: triaging alerts, investigating, and then building the detections and automation that make the next investigation faster. You will gain hands-on cloud security experience in a Google Cloud environment, plus exposure to detection engineering, identity and SaaS threats and shadow AI governance.

This role is based in our Raleigh HQ, three days per week in-person.

What this looks like day-to-day

• Alert triage and defense: You will review security alerts from the Pendo platform, our corporate systems and other sources. You will separate real threats from noise and escalate what needs a deeper look. You will use AI tools to summarize logs and speed up your investigations, and you will check their output before acting on it.

• Identity and access monitoring: You will detect and investigate unusual activity tied to user identities and misuse of privileged access. The goal is to catch intrusions early.

• Threat hunting: You will go looking for threats across endpoints, SaaS apps, Google Cloud infrastructure and APIs, rather than waiting for alerts to find you. You will ask why an alert fired and what else looks like it, then turn what you find into new detections.

• Incident response: You will investigate incidents that affect Google Cloud infrastructure, corporate SaaS and company systems. You will help the team carry out containment actions. You will show Bias to Act by making calls with incomplete information and adjusting as you learn more.

• Detection and SIEM health: You will build, test and tune custom detection logic. You will improve data collection in the SIEM and keep integrations and data sources healthy. You will also help build detections and defenses against automated and agent driven attacks, including WAF and DDoS protections and application layer defenses built with Product Security.

• Automation and AI-assisted workflows: You will help the team use orchestration and AI-assisted workflows for repetitive triage, data aggregation and playbook steps. When you see a manual task you repeat, you will automate it or write a detection for it. You will write Python scripts, work with Terraform and use AI coding assistants to draft and debug code, and you will review every line before it runs.

• Partnering with other teams: You will work alongside our Product Security and Compliance teams and partner with engineering and IT teams on security questions and findings. You will write up findings and explain risks in plain language so people know what to do and why. You will also keep alert hygiene, runbooks and playbooks current as you go.

• On-call: Join the team's on-call coverage after you've ramped up, with support from teammates.

Who You Are

Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work.

You're a builder, not a maintainer.

You're most energized when there isn't a clear path yet, and you get to define it. You don't wait for direction; you identify gaps, shape solutions, and drive them forward. At Pendo, great Associate Security Engineers don't just follow instructions; they operate as strategic advisors, influencing decisions, guiding stakeholders, and elevating how we work.

You're AI-curious - genuinely.

You're not using AI tools occasionally. You're rewiring how you work around them. You're faster, sharper, and more prolific because of it, and you bring that energy to everything — how you approach your work, how you prep, how you communicate, how you think. We want someone who sees AI as a multiplier, not a shortcut.

Must-haves

• Foundational knowledge of core security concepts, including identity and access management, networking and common attack techniques.

• Hands-on experience investigating security events or alerts, through work, internships, labs or personal projects.

• Ability to read and write basic scripts or queries in Python, SQL or a similar language to investigate and automate.

• Active use of AI tools in your work, and the habit of checking their output before you trust it. You show nimble learning by testing what works and verifying the results yourself.

• Clear written and verbal communication, including writing up findings for technical and non-technical readers.

• Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation.

• Willingness to raise hard issues early, ask for help early and help teammates without being asked.

Nice-to-haves

• Familiarity with cloud environments and logs (GCP is a plus).

• Experience with a SIEM, XDR or log analysis platform, and writing detection rules.

• Familiarity with identity threat detection, SaaS security posture or SaaS audit logs, for example Google Workspace, Okta or GitHub.

• Familiarity with an incident response lifecycle or the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

• Experience with automation or orchestration, including building AI-assisted workflows.

• A security certification such as CompTIA Security+, GCIH or GSEC, or a cloud security certification, or a degree in computer science, cybersecurity or a related field, or equivalent experience.

About Pendo

Pendo was founded in 2013 by former product managers, who combined their heads and hearts to build something they wanted but never had as product managers: a simple way to understand and attack what truly drives product success. Our mission is to improve society's experience with software. Come join one of the fastest-growing startups, supported by best-in-class institutions like Battery Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Spark Capital and Meritech.

Pendo Core Values: Bias to Act, Hone Your Craft, The Team is Pendo, and Maniacal Focus.

Location: Pendo is a hybrid culture. In-office 3 days per week unless designated remote.

Compensation: The expected salary range for this role to be performed in Raleigh, NC is $88,800 - $106,500.

Benefits: Highly competitive, employer-heavy coverage (including $0 premium options), strong 401(k) match, equity, and flexible time off.

EEOC: We are an equal opportunity employer and believe having diverse teams where everyone brings their whole self to Pendo is key to our success. We welcome all people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives.

Accessibility: Pendo is committed to working with, and providing access and reasonable accommodation to, applicants with mental and/or physical disabilities. If you think you may require an accommodation for any part of the recruitment process, please send a request to: accommodation@pendo.io. All requests for accommodations are treated discreetly and confidentially, as practical and permitted by law.

jobs.title: Manager, Corporate Security
jobs.description:
Manager, Corporate Security – New York City (HQ) based

The Global Safety & Security Team falls under the Operations team that runs many day-to-day operational functions that help keep our employees safe, happy and productive. We work closely with leadership and employees to ensure that Datadog continues to scale rapidly, yet smoothly and remains a fantastic place to work.

We’re seeking an experienced team member to join our growing global team and play a critical role in keeping Datadogs and our assets safe and secure. You will work directly with the Global Safety & Security Sr Manager - AMER and cross-functional teams to support safety and security operations across the enterprise. Ideal candidates will be passionate about security operations, program development, leadership, project management, customer service and collaboration.

This position is based in our New York City headquarters and may require occasional domestic and international travel. The role will focus particularly on three core pillars: Headquarters Security, Global Security Operations Center operations and occasional management of the executive protection program

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. This position requires being in-office 5 days a week.

What You’ll Do:

Headquarters Security:

• Manage daily safety and security operations at Datadog’s New York City headquarters, including contract security personnel, access control, visitor management, internal events and incident response.

• Oversee contract security personnel and vendors, including staffing, training, post orders, service levels, performance reviews and corrective actions. while maintaining a safe, professional and welcoming employee experience.

• Coordinate with building management, property security and internal teams to coordinate lobby operations, emergency response, life-safety matters and headquarters security incidents..

• Identify and address risks associated with operating in a high-profile urban environment, including protests, demonstrations, workplace violence, suspicious activity, property crime and other incidents that may affect Datadogs, visitors or business operations.

• Develop Security risk mitigation strategies. Support the implementation and management of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management and other technical security systems.

Global Security Operations Center:

• Advance Datadog’s GSOC as its central hub for global security monitoring, incident intake, triage, escalation, communication and response coordination.

• Develop and maintain GSOC standard operating procedures, escalation protocols, incident classifications, notification requirements, service levels and quality standards to ensure consistent global operations.

• Oversee resources supporting GSOC operations, including staffing, training, performance management, vendor relationships and operational readiness.

• Monitor global events, emerging threats and incidents that could affect Datadog’s employees, offices, executives, travelers, events or operations. Ensure timely and accurate communication during critical incidents, including security alerts, situation reports, leadership briefings and updates to impacted teams.

• Review incident trends, performance metrics and recurring risks to identify opportunities to improve processes, tools and response capabilities. Lead post-incident reviews and track corrective actions through completion.

Executive Protection:

• Manage and advance Datadog’s executive protection program, including protective intelligence, executive threat monitoring, travel and event security and response to identified or emerging threats.

• Partner with executives, executive assistants and internal stakeholders to provide security support that is discreet, practical and aligned with Datadog’s culture and business needs when necessary.

• Manage vendors, ensuring that providers meet Datadog’s expectations for professionalism, confidentiality, service and operational performance.

Who You Are:

• Experienced in managing corporate safety and security operations, ideally within a fast-paced technology environment, with a focus on headquarters security, GSOC operations and executive protection.

• Skilled in managing all aspects of a physical security program, including contract security personnel, access control, video surveillance, visitor management, event security, investigations and emergency response.

• Experienced in developing or managing a GSOC, security operations center, command center or similar 24/7 monitoring and incident response capability.

• Knowledgeable about GSOC operating standards, including incident intake, triage, escalation, communications, reporting, service levels, performance metrics and after-action reviews.

• Experienced in executive protection program management, including protective intelligence, threat monitoring, executive travel, advance planning, event security and third-party provider management.

• Able to assess complex or incomplete information, make sound decisions under pressure and communicate clear recommendations during sensitive or rapidly evolving situations.

• Experienced in conducting physical security and threat assessments, identifying vulnerabilities and developing proportionate mitigation strategies.

• Knowledgeable about workplace violence prevention, behavioral threat assessment, insider threat, crisis management and active assailant preparedness.

• Experienced with open-source intelligence, protective intelligence and threat-monitoring tools used to identify and evaluate potential risks involving employees, executives, facilities and business operations.

• Knowledgeable about technical security systems, with experience supporting physical security design and reviewing access control, surveillance, visitor management and intrusion detection solutions.

• An exceptional written and verbal communicator who can effectively convey security information across all levels of the organization, with a specific focus on executives and senior leadership.

• A strong cross-functional partner who can build trusted relationships with internal teams, building management, law enforcement, emergency services, peer organizations and external security providers.

• Experienced in building and growing safety and security programs that can scale with organizational needs while maintaining a strong employee and customer service focus.

• Able to exercise a high level of integrity, discretion and confidentiality when managing sensitive incidents, investigations and executive-related matters.

• Comfortable managing multiple priorities and operating with autonomy in a dynamic environment where risks, business needs and operational requirements may change quickly.

• 8+ years of progressively responsible experience in corporate security, physical security, GSOC operations, executive protection, law enforcement, intelligence, military security or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience managing contract security personnel or external security teams

• Able and willing to travel domestically and internationally and participate in an after-hours on-call rotation.

• Professional certifications or specialized training in corporate security, executive protection, threat assessment, emergency management or business continuity are preferred.

jobs.title: Care Specialist - (Bilingual English/Spanish)
jobs.description:
Company Overview:

Upward Health is an in-home, multidisciplinary medical group providing 24/7 whole-person care. Our clinical team treats physical, behavioral, and social health needs when and where a patient needs help. Everyone on our team from our doctors, nurses, and Care Specialists to our HR, Technology, and Business Services staff are driven by a desire to improve the lives of our patients. We are able to treat a wide range of needs – everything from addressing poorly controlled blood sugar to combatting anxiety to accessing medically tailored meals – because we know that health requires care for the whole person. It’s no wonder 98% of patients report being fully satisfied with Upward Health!

Job Title & Role Description:

The Care Specialist is a key member of the team responsible for delivering chronic care management to high-complexity patients. The Care Specialist primarily works in patients' homes and communities (90% of the time) and engages in virtual care (10% of the time). This role involves direct outreach to patients, guiding them through the enrollment process, facilitating virtual appointments with providers, and ensuring that patients adhere to care plans. By building relationships, coordinating care, and providing education, the Care Specialist plays a critical role in promoting health, preventing unnecessary hospitalizations, and improving patient outcomes.

Skills Required:

• Minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience (e.g., Community Health Worker, Peer Support Specialist, Medical Assistant, etc.).

• High school diploma or GED required.

• A valid driver’s license, auto liability insurance, and reliable transportation to travel within the assigned territory.

• Experience in chronic care management or working with chronically ill/elderly patients.

• Technologically proficient with basic computer skills (typing, using EMR systems).

• Experience with motivational interviewing, trauma-informed care, and care coordination.

• Strong interpersonal communication skills with the ability to engage patients and team members effectively.

• Ability to prioritize tasks, manage schedules, and work independently in an unstructured environment.

• Bilingual in English and Spanish.

• Prior home care and pediatric experience.

Key Behaviors:

Adaptability & Resilience:

• Ability to thrive in unstructured environments and pivot as needed to meet patient needs. Demonstrates perseverance in challenging situations.

Self-Starter & Motivation:

• Proactively takes initiative in managing patient care and outreach. Willingness to learn and adapt to new processes and systems.

Empathy & Compassion:

• Ability to work with individuals from diverse backgrounds and understand their complex needs. Skilled in building rapport through motivational interviewing and other patient-centered communication techniques.

Accountability & Integrity:

• Demonstrates personal responsibility and takes ownership of tasks, ensuring accuracy and timeliness in all activities.

Cultural Competence:

• Awareness of community dynamics and diversity, ensuring culturally sensitive and inclusive care.

Team Collaboration:

• Works collaboratively with interdisciplinary teams to meet patient and organizational goals.

Problem-Solving & Critical Thinking:

• Strong critical thinking skills to assess patient needs, analyze data, and develop appropriate care strategies.

Communication Skills:

• Excellent verbal and written communication, capable of explaining complex medical information to patients in a clear and supportive manner.

Competencies:

Care Coordination:

• Ability to engage patients in a comprehensive care plan, facilitating communication between patients, providers, and family members to ensure timely, effective care.

Health Education:

• Effectively educates patients about their medical conditions, care plans, and available resources, ensuring that patients can make informed decisions.

Patient Engagement:

• Uses various strategies, including phone calls, home visits, and community outreach, to engage patients and ensure continuous participation in their care.

Time Management & Organization:

• Demonstrates strong organizational skills by managing patient caseloads, schedules, and documentation efficiently.

Technology Proficiency:

• Skilled in using electronic health records (EMR) systems and other digital tools to document patient information and communicate within the team.

Motivational Interviewing & Patient-Centered Care:

• Uses motivational interviewing techniques to build rapport and empower patients to take ownership of their health decisions.

Data Management:

• Ensures accurate and timely documentation of patient data, ensuring continuity of care and compliance with organizational standards.

Outcome-Oriented Approach:

• Focuses on achieving key health outcomes, such as improved care adherence, reduction in emergency room visits, and enhanced self-management.

You will start by developing trusted relationships with our patients and providers and will assist with various patient-facing, administrative, and logistical tasks so that doctors can focus on delivering high-quality medical care to their patients. Navigators work for Main Street but go to work every day inside one of our partner clinics alongside clinic staff.  They meet with and call patients, enter data into our systems, contact the pharmacy to refill prescriptions, troubleshoot challenges with insurance coverage and more.  Main Street’s management and training teams will equip you with the training and tools you need to perform these duties.   You will:

• Educate patients on their healthcare options, insurance benefits, and common medical conditions​

• Help patients access various community resources

At Two Six Technologies, we build, deploy, and implement innovative products that solve the world’s most complex challenges today. Through unrivaled collaboration and unwavering trust, we push the boundaries of what’s possible to empower our team and support our customers in building a safer global future.

Compensation & Incentive Highlights

Overview of Opportunity

Join the Trusted Electronics & Effects business unit of Two Six Technologies, where you’ll immerse yourself in reverse engineering and vulnerability research on a wide range of embedded systems, software, and operational processes. Working alongside reverse engineers and security researchers, you’ll identify vulnerabilities, analyze attack vectors, and assess operational impacts on some of the most critical systems for our customers. Our fast-growing roster of government customers relies on us to deliver advanced security solutions, and we’re looking for a Senior Vulnerability Researcher to help us continue pushing boundaries. If you’re passionate about vulnerability research that can make a tangible impact on national security, we want you on our team.

• Proficiency in Linux command-line environments

• Experience using a decompiler such as IDA Pro, Binary Ninja, or Ghidra

• Experience using vulnerability research tools such as emulators or fuzzers

• Experience using a software debugger such as GDB or WinDbg

• Ability to work on-site at the Linthicum, Maryland customer site regularly

Nice If You Have (Preferred):

• Experience producing technical briefings for operational stakeholders

• Experience using a hardware debugger

• Experience with UART, SPI, I2C

jobs.title: Sr Product Operations Manager
jobs.description:
The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.

Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.

The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.

What We Are Looking

We are looking for a driven, energetic Senior Product Operations Manager who will be part of a global Product Operations team within our product organization. You’ll partner closely with product, R&D, and the commercial business to ensure we are continuously translating product strategy into clear priorities, aligned execution, and measurable outcomes.

You are a force multiplier for the R&D organization — driving clarity, discipline, transparency, and alignment across product and company leadership. You shift fluently between strategic, operational, and communication flows. You will tune and evolve the systems and rhythms that connect strategy formulation to goals, delivery, and client impact. You drive adoption of standards that enable scalable, data-driven operations, partnering with cross-functional teams to resolve friction and deliver on shared objectives.

You are essential to the successful delivery of great products. You have deep empathy for internal and external customer needs, build scalable feedback mechanisms that weave quantitative and qualitative data into cohesive insights, and translate those insights into prioritized product opportunities that influence roadmaps to drive progress against measurable outcomes.

What You Will Be Doing

You will be focused on contributing to product operating rhythms and amplifying capabilities across the R&D organization. You will help the product organization evolve processes and operate at scale, ensuring that what we develop connects to both customer and business outcomes. You will support Product Ops Leadership in developing and delivering against strategies that tie the team’s work to The Trade Desk’s ability to bring the right products to market.

Responsibilities

Roadmap Ownership & Governance

• Drive end-to-end facilitation of the product roadmap process, including strategy formulation, investment area definition, opportunity sizing, capacity planning, and scenario/tradeoff analysis

• Facilitate formal roadmap presentations to leadership, commercial, and revenue teams to build alignment on strategic priorities, resource allocation, sequencing, and explicit tradeoffs

• Document and socialize roadmap decisions; maintain version control of all roadmap artifacts

• Integrate lifecycle expertise across multiple initiatives, anticipating systemic risks, cross-team dependencies, and cross-platform impacts; shape planning rituals and readiness standards across the organization

Release Readiness & Launch Preparedness

• Own operational readiness strategy for key product features, leveraging release readiness frameworks to drive alignment across multiple product domains

• Anticipate systemic risks, define scalable playbooks, and influence senior stakeholders to ensure enterprise-wide launch preparedness and accountability for upstream and downstream adoption

• Partner with Product and Ops leadership to evolve lifecycle frameworks, improving predictability, quality, and execution consistency

Goal Setting, Measurement & Analytics

• Facilitate regular cadence goal-setting for each product area and PM, ensuring goals ladder to roadmap investment areas and company goals

• Collaborate with Data Science and Analytics partners to translate measurement frameworks into actionable tracking plans; embed defined KPIs in execution workflows and ensure insights drive meaningful adjustments in process and delivery outcomes

• Design frameworks and quality controls used across Product Ops that enable teams to extract signal from noise and link insights to business outcomes

• Monitor progress via structured weekly updates and proactively escalate risks, tradeoffs, slippage, or misalignment to product leadership

Field Feedback & User Advocacy

• Operate the regional intake process to collect structured pain point requests from field teams and route validate, strategically aligned opportunities to PMs for investigation

• Build scalable mechanisms for collecting, synthesizing, and communicating user needs; integrate quantitative and qualitative data into cohesive insights that directly inform roadmap prioritization and feature decisions

• Standardize how requests are documented, categorized, and themed; close the loop with field stakeholders on prioritization and progress

• Champion adoption of user-centered practices within and across teams; drive measurable improvements in customer and product outcomes

Product Ceremonies & Operating Rhythm

• Own agenda design and management for product team meeting cadences: weekly leadership meetings, goal-tracking reviews, and cross-functional alignment sessions

• Establish communication cadences and documentation standards that sustain alignment over time; ensure meetings are purposeful, high-leverage, and tied to current priorities

• Facilitate alignment across multiple leadership groups and initiatives; anticipate friction points, reframe conflicts constructively, and guide teams toward evidence-based decisions

Program, Process & Change Leadership

• Lead complex change initiatives spanning multiple teams; design transition plans, stakeholder communications, and feedback loops to sustain adoption; anticipate resistance and implement strategies that maintain morale and clarity

• Introduce tooling or automation to streamline processes or reduce overhead; partner with leaders to measure impact and drive continuous improvement across teams

• Facilitate collaboration among cross-functional teams and influence decision-making within senior-level audiences; lead execution against recommendations quickly and accurately

• Support psychological safety, team health, and happiness within the product org

About You

• You are passionate about operational process

• You are a systems thinker who can effectively break down problems and scope solutions

• You have experience successfully managing multiple programs simultaneously from start to finish, building durable collaboration structures that enhance decision velocity and accountability

• You are data-driven and use evidence-driven storytelling to influence prioritization and senior stakeholders

• You are empathetic to customer needs, and able to build sustainable feedback loops to promote customer advocacy across product areas

• You use analysis and business context to identify root causes, proactively surface risks, and develop practical solutions that prevent recurrence on complex issues

• You communicate persuasively to influence decision-making, presenting complex information with clarity and confidence to diverse audiences

• You are able to manage expectations, mitigate conflict, and foster understanding across departments

• You respond and adapt quickly while maintaining strategic momentum when solving problems

• You are comfortable with ambiguity, resilient to change, and able to adapt or change course without losing momentum

• You act with autonomy and can proactively bring fresh ideas to drive work forward

Qualifications

• 5+ years of experience in a technology company in product management, product operations, or program management with significant interface with technical and business teams

• Demonstrated experience driving product roadmap processes, investment planning, or strategic planning cycles

• Experience with release readiness or launch operations, including building playbooks and driving cross-functional launch preparedness

• Experience facilitating senior level alignment meetings and communicating complex tradeoffs to senior stakeholders

• Familiarity with field feedback or voice-of-customer programs; ability to integrate qualitative and quantitative data into actionable product direction

• Experience partnering with Data Science or Analytics teams to define KPIs, build tracking plans, and embed measurement into delivery workflows

• Comfortable working across product, engineering, revenue, and operations teams to drive cross-functional alignment

• Familiar with product and design tools such as Jira, Confluence, Salesforce, and whiteboarding tools

• Experience with goal-setting frameworks (OKRs or similar) and progress tracking at the organizational level

• Strong written and verbal communication skills to create clarity across a large organization

jobs.location: 9400 S Cicero, Suite, 306, Oak Lawn, IL  60453
jobs.description:
💥 $5,000 Sign-On Bonus! 💥

The Clinical Supervisor (After-School BCBA) is a full-time, hybrid role ideal for clinicians who are passionate about delivering high-quality ABA services while mentoring and supporting Registered Behavior Technicians (RBTs). jobs.title: Chemical Engineering Technician
jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

The Role

The Chemical Engineering Technician is responsible for assisting with the stand-up and operation of pilot facilities supporting chemical and black powder research, collaborating with cross-functional teams — including operations, quality control, and research & development — to bring these systems and facilities online.

The position reports to the Lead Chemical Technician and is part of the Engineering Chemicals Team based in Penrose, CO. This is a full-time, onsite role in Penrose, CO, working a 9/80 schedule.

In this role, the essential functions are:

• Install, repair, and maintain piping systems, including threading and assembling NPT fittings, plastic piping (PEX, PVC, CPVC), sanitary pipe fittings, and other plumbing methods.

• Support day-to-day pilot plant operations by assisting the engineering team with running equipment and helping resolve issues as they arise.

• Maintain and repair mechanical equipment such as pumps, valves, and general hardware components.

• Assemble and install structural systems using materials such as Unistrut, t-slot framing, concrete mounting, and basic carpentry/fabrication techniques.

• Troubleshoot mechanical and basic electrical issues to ensure smooth, efficient operations and minimize equipment downtime.

• Maintain and organize the pilot plant, including spare parts inventory, to ensure critical components are available for operations and repairs.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams — including operations, quality control, and research & development — to stand up new pilot systems and facilities.

Required Qualifications:

• High School Diploma or equivalent with 4+ years of experience in industrial manufacturing, mechanical technician work, or other relevant experience OR Associate’s degree in Engineering Technology with 2+ years of relevant experience

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to diagnose mechanical issues and implement effective solutions quickly

• Hand and shop tool knowledge (power tools, saws, grinders, etc.)

• Excellent communication skills to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams

• Excellent time management skills with a proven ability to meet deadlines

• Ability to function well in a high-paced and at times stressful environment

• Proactive and self-directed with the ability to work independently and as part of a team

• Understanding of basic design principles (sizing of hardware and plumbing, material selection, material compatibility, etc.)

Preferred Qualifications:

• Basic knowledge of electrical systems with the ability to troubleshoot issues using a digital multimeter

• Fabrication experience, including mounting and modifying existing equipment in place

Travel, Physical and/or Government Mandated Requirements:

• Travel up to 10%, primarily local travel between site facilities

• Frequent movement through a manufacturing environment; regular use of personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate to the work location

• Ability to lift, move, or carry equipment and materials up to 50 pounds

• Ability to sit or stand at a desk and use a computer and keyboard for portions of the workday

Work Authorization:

Must be a US citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident, or a protected individual as defined in 8 USC 1324b.

The good faith hourly range for this role is $27.00 - $32.00 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base pay only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

• Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their families, with a significant portion of premiums covered by the company and many benefits paid at 100% for employees

• Flexible, affordable gym memberships with 12,700+ options nationwide, including 24 Hour Fitness, EoS Fitness, Crunch Fitness, Anytime Fitness, Blink Fitness, Chuze Fitness, and more! No long-term contracts and FREE on-demand workout videos before you enroll

• 401(k) retirement plan with a 50% company match on contributions up to 8%, supporting long-term financial security

• Company wellness programs that support physical and mental well-being

• Additional voluntary benefits and employee support resources

• The opportunity to work alongside a highly talented team in an innovative, mission-driven environment

Voyager is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.title: Tax Senior
jobs.description:
About Ascend

Backed by private equity from people-focused Alpine Investors, Ascend is building a dynamic platform for regional accounting firms that enables them to stay independent while accessing the resources of a Top 25 firm to help them grow. Ascend provides access to growth capital, robust talent acquisition and training, leading quality management resources, best-of-breed technology, AI tools, an offshore captive, shared back-office services, a catalytic leadership system, and modernized equity incentives so that firms can surmount today's industry challenges to reach their full potential. For more information, visit www.ascendtogether.com.

About Kreischer Miller

Kreischer Miller is a leading regional accounting and advisory firm with nearly 300 team members, known for serving closely held businesses, business owners, and high-net-worth individuals. The firm's tax professionals bring international firm and Fortune 500 experience alongside deep middle-market expertise, and are dedicated to providing sophisticated, yet practical solutions that help clients reduce their overall tax burden. Kreischer Miller continues to grow, and is seeking a Tax Senior to join its Tax Strategies team. For more information, visit www.kmco.com.

About the Role

As a Tax Senior, you will work on a diverse mix of tax engagements for business owners and individuals across a variety of industries, learning directly from firm leaders. You will prepare and review returns, conduct tax research, and help train and supervise staff while building the technical and client-service skills needed to advance toward the manager level.

Key Responsibilities

• Prepare and review federal, state, and local tax returns for businesses, flow-through entities, closely held corporations, and individuals.

• Conduct tax research and assist with tax planning and advisory projects.

• Review work prepared by staff, providing timely, constructive feedback.

• Support client relationships and communicate effectively with clients and colleagues at all levels of the firm.

• Assist with responses to federal, state, and local tax notices and audits.

• Train, mentor, and develop tax staff and interns.

• Prioritize and manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

• Maintain technical knowledge through continuing education, professional publications, and networking.

• Contribute to special projects and process improvements as needed.

What We're Seeking

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

• 3–5 years of tax experience in public accounting preparing business and individual returns.

• CPA license or active progress toward licensure preferred.

• Working knowledge of federal, state, and local tax compliance.

• Strong analytical, project management, and communication skills.

• Ability to multi-task and meet deadlines, with a positive, team-oriented attitude and a willingness to learn.

• Interest in career advancement, including future leadership responsibilities.

We provide a fair and equal employment opportunity for all candidates regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, age, marital status, disability, or any other legally protected characteristic.
