• Work Experience 7+ years of clinical research or clinical operations experience within biotechnology, pharmaceutical, CRO, or related environments Demonstrated experience supporting Phase I-III clinical studies Strong experience overseeing CRO and vendor oversight Experience managing clinical studies from study start-up, site management, enrollment strategies, database lock, to study closeout activities Experience managing study budgets and vendor contracts Prior experience supporting regulatory inspections and audit readiness Rare disease and ophthalmology experience preferred

jobs.description:
Who we are:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About the Role:

Motive is seeking a Sr. Manager, Enterprise Security Architecture to own how we protect our most sensitive data across our cloud, data platforms, and media pipelines. Reporting directly to the CISO, you will be the founding leader of the Enterprise Security Architecture function, setting the technical standards for data governance, zero-standing-privilege access management, and security posture across our US and EU environments. You will hire, coach, and lead a small team of security architects while partnering closely with Platform, Data, AI/ML, Product, Privacy, Legal, IT, and GRC teams to embed security early into engineering design. You will ground decisions in hands-on validation and evidence, proving target architectures in working prototypes before turning them into scalable paved roads for engineering. This is a principal-engineer-style player-coach role: you will spend roughly half your time staying hands-on—designing reference architectures, writing infrastructure and policy as code, and building proofs of concept yourself—and the other half leading your team and driving cross-functional alignment. This is a high-visibility, 0-to-1 leadership opportunity to shape the foundational security architecture behind Motive’s data and AI platforms.

What You’ll Do:

• Define data classification, ownership, retention, and handling standards for structured and unstructured data, including customer media, telemetry, and AI/ML training data.

• Design reference architectures for data protection across AWS, Snowflake, and surrounding data platforms, including customer-managed encryption keys, key separation by data class, and multi-region (US and EU) data residency controls.

• Architect access management that eliminates standing human access through least-privilege design, federated identity, just-in-time elevation, and approval-gated exceptions.

• Define authentication, authorization, registration, review, and revocation standards for services, pipelines, and AI agents, alongside strong guardrails to prevent data exfiltration.

• Run hands-on proofs of concept for data security posture management (DSPM), cloud and data access analytics, secure media review environments, and ephemeral compute to drive data-backed build-versus-buy decisions.

• Write infrastructure as code, policy as code, and detection logic, and review engineering designs and pull requests to turn successful prototypes into documented, self-service paved roads.

• Hire, coach, and grow a team of security architects focused on IAM, data governance, and AI security, setting technical direction, priorities, and the quality bar.

• Partner across Platform, Data, AI/ML, Product, Privacy, Legal, IT, and GRC to embed controls early, and report posture metrics, risk trade-offs, and progress to security and engineering leadership.

What We’re Looking For:

• 8+ years in security engineering or architecture, including at least 5 years designing cloud and data security for large, regulated, or data-intensive environments.

• Deep AWS security expertise paired with hands-on experience securing Snowflake or comparable data platforms (such as Databricks or BigQuery), including RBAC design, masking, row access policies, private connectivity, data sharing, and audit controls.

• Proven track record designing data governance and access management architectures, including data classification, least privilege, just-in-time elevation, workload identity, and privileged access.

• Practical experience with data security posture management (DSPM) and data loss prevention (DLP), from running proofs of concept and tuning findings to operationalizing controls at scale.

• Strong coding ability in Python or Go and Terraform to build prototypes, policy as code, and automation, combined with proficiency using AI coding tools to accelerate engineering solutions.

• 3+ years leading or mentoring security engineers or architects, either formally as a manager or as a technical lead.

• Ability to turn architectural standards into broad engineering adoption through clear design docs, cross-functional influence, and pragmatic risk communication.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Pay Transparency
Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). jobs.title: Software Engineer II, AI Experience (Remote Eligible)
jobs.description:
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smart Assist is Smartsheet's AI agent for work management, used by enterprise customers to analyze, create, and act on their work. AI Experiences builds the orchestration for Smart Assist and the user-facing implementations that expose Smartsheet's Intelligent Work capabilities to any AI surface, so users can reach the right intelligence at the right time through a coherent, reliable experience.

AI Experiences is a pillar within Applied AI, and this is a full-stack team. The work spans these areas: the Smart Assist frontend (UI components, interaction patterns, and rendering for AI experiences across Smartsheet); the Smart Assist backend and orchestrator; UX for Smart Assist tools and agents, from response formatting and onboarding to error states. On the backend, the orchestrator routes each request to the right sub-agent based on user intent, keeps conversation state across multi-turn interactions, handles fallbacks when sub-agents are unavailable, and controls feature-flagged rollout of new capabilities. We partner closely with Agent Engineering on much of this logic.

The role. You will own features and components of Smart Assist from prototype to production, across the front end, the orchestrator and back-end services. You will turn ambiguous product asks into reliable, well-measured behavior customers can trust, and work with product, design, and AI Experience to ship.

You Will:

• Own a core piece of the Smartsheet AI experience, or a significant part of one (for example conversational analytics, chart-to-dashboard creation, or a new entry point into the assistant) from design through production.

• Build full-stack: user-facing components, the services behind them, and the contracts between the two, with typed APIs, clear error states, and tests.

• Design and ship agent tools, skills, MCP tools, and MCP Apps with contracts the model can use reliably, and decide when an action belongs in a tool, a service, or the model.

• Shape how agent output appears to users: streaming responses, loading and failure states, and handling of long or partial results, working with design and product.

• Build and evolve the Smart Assist orchestrator: intent-based routing to sub-agents, multi-turn conversation state, fallback and degradation handling, and feature-flag rollout of new capabilities, partnering closely with Agent Engineering. Populate the context the agent receives, such as user locale, timezone, and workspace state.

• Define how quality is measured for your area: build golden cases and scorers, set regression gates, and use traces and production signals to decide whether a failure needs a prompt, tool, context, or UI fix.

• Instrument features with tracing, structured logs, and latency, cost, and error dashboards, and act on what they show.

• Take part in on-call, security, and cost work for Smart Assist, shared with Agent Engineering. Reproduce production failures and review code for your team.

• Partner with PMs, designers, Agent Engineering, AI Platform, MCP, and data teams. Learn how customers use what you build and flag gaps in requirements and tests.

• Use AI coding tools to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

What we're building next:

Our goal for the coming year is to make Smart Assist safe to trust and hard to leave. You will help shape work across four themes:

• Be everywhere: an assistant that understands what you are looking at, such as the rows you have selected, and meets you in the flow of work, including smoother import and file upload.

• Build the habit: an assistant that remembers how you like to work, with personal, team, and organization profiles, quick commands, and a growing UI component catalog.

• Earn the trust: previews before changes apply, linked sources and explanations for results, AI edits visible in history and activity logs, and a view into the agent's reasoning.

• Work together: a directory of agents, @mentions, and the ability to save and share results as pages.

Further out, the vision is a Smart Assist that finds you before you ask: a proactive, insight-first surface that learns how your workspace works, suggests prompts personalized to you, brings in context from tools like Slack, Zoom, and documents, supports multiplayer conversations, and offers help inside the chat itself. You would help define the trust model for that experience from real customer learnings and feedback.

You Have:

• 2–4 years of professional software engineering shipping production systems.

• Strong in Python and/or TypeScript/React, with good habits in testing, code review, and debugging.

• Experience building and shipping customer-facing features end to end, including APIs, data modeling, and user-facing behavior.

• 1+ years building LLM-powered features in production: tool or function calling, agent loops, prompt and context design, or multi-step workflows.

• Working knowledge of how agents fail (bad tool choice, context overflow, hallucinated arguments, runaway cost) and how to design around it.

• Experience designing eval scorers and golden datasets, and using results to make and defend a decision.

• Experience with MCP tools and MCP Apps, structured tool calling, or reusable agent skills.

• Comfort with production observability and with data-heavy environments (Databricks or equivalent).

• Evidence of using AI coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

• Clear communication of quality, cost, and reliability findings to technical and non-technical audiences.

• Legally eligible to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis.

Strong plus:

Experience with conversational or chat UI at scale; LLM tracing tools (LangSmith, Phoenix, Braintrust or similar); prompt versioning or CI-integrated evals; dashboard, charting, or data-visualization products; enterprise SaaS permissions and entitlements; prompt-injection mitigation and output validation.

What success looks like:

• First 90 days: ship a feature or improvement to production with eval coverage, and take your first on-call rotation.

• First 6 months: own a feature or significant part of a project with measured gains in task success, latency, or user adoption, and contribute at least one reusable component or pattern.

Why this role:

• You build the Smart Assist experience used by enterprise customers, with real users and a measurable quality bar.

• You work across the stack, from the interface to the agent tools behind it, so you see your work reach customers end to end.

• The problems are distinctive: enterprise-grade permissions and security, and one assistant that works across a broad work-management product.

• You work on the hard parts of production agents, on a team that values engineering rigor and diverse perspectives.

Current US Perks & Benefits:

• Employer subsidized medical/vision and dental coverage for full-time employees

• 401k Match to help you save for your future (50% of your contribution up to the first 6% of your eligible pay)

• Monthly stipend to support your work and productivity

• Flexible Time Away Program, plus Sick Time Off

• US employees are automatically covered under Smartsheet-sponsored life insurance, short-term, and long-term disability plans

• US employees receive 12 paid holidays per year

• Up to 24 weeks of Parental Leave

• Personal paid Volunteer Day to support our community

• Opportunities for professional growth and development including access to Udemy online courses

• Company Funded Perks, including a counseling membership, local retail discounts, and your own personal Smartsheet account

• Teleworking options from any registered location in the U.S. (role specific)

Smartsheet provides a competitive base salary range for roles that may be hired in different geographic areas we are licensed to operate our business from. Actual compensation is determined by several factors including, but not limited to, level of professional, educational experience, skills, and specific candidate location. In addition, this role will be eligible for a market competitive incentive opportunity.

US Base Salary Pay Range

$125,000—$175,000 USD

Get to Know Us:

At Smartsheet, your ideas are heard, your potential is supported, and your contributions have real impact. You’ll have the freedom to explore, push boundaries, and grow beyond your role. We welcome diverse perspectives and nontraditional paths—because we know that impact comes from individuals who care deeply and challenge thoughtfully. When you’re doing work that stretches you, excites you, and connects you to something bigger, that’s magic at work. Let’s build what’s next, together.

jobs.description:
About Blueprint

Blueprint is a technology solutions firm headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with teams across the United States. We help organizations turn complex challenges into meaningful outcomes by connecting strategy and execution across AI, cloud, data, product development, and emerging technology.

Our culture is built by people who care deeply about doing exceptional work. We set high standards, take ownership, and continually challenge ourselves and one another to be better. We work hard, support each other, and take genuine pride in what we deliver for our clients, partners, and teams.

At Blueprint, you’ll work alongside talented people with different experiences, expertise, and perspectives. You’ll have opportunities to take on meaningful challenges, expand your skills, and see the impact of what you build.

Bring your perspective. Raise the standard. Build what matters.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Vietnamese Games Translation & Localization Specialist to join our world-class localization team. In this role, you’ll translate and localize gaming content into Vietnamese with exceptional linguistic quality, cultural relevance, and attention to detail. You’ll collaborate with fellow localization specialists and cross-functional partners to deliver accurate, engaging content for players and customers.

This role is ideal for someone who combines deep Vietnamese language expertise with a genuine passion for gaming. You’ll work across new releases, marketing materials, support content, and other customer-facing communications while managing changing priorities and occasional last-minute updates.

What You'll Do

• Translate and localize gaming and technical content from English into Vietnamese.

• Support new releases, marketing materials, knowledge-base articles, and other customer-facing content.

• Ensure translations are accurate, culturally relevant, and consistent in tone, terminology, grammar, and style.

• Review and refine localized content to maintain high standards of linguistic quality.

• Manage short-term and long-term translation projects while meeting deadlines and quality expectations.

• Reprioritize work effectively when source materials or project requirements change.

• Use computer-assisted translation tools to manage terminology, translation memory, and workflow consistency.

• Collaborate closely with other translators, reviewers, project teams, and stakeholders.

• Stay informed about gaming terminology, genres, platforms, hardware, and player communities.

• Contribute to a team culture focused on quality, continuous improvement, innovation, and shared success.

What You'll Bring

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification, preferably in translation, localization, linguistics, game design, or a related field.

• Native-level written and verbal proficiency in Vietnamese, including exceptional command of grammar, spelling, punctuation, and style.

• Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.

• Professional translation or localization experience.

• Strong familiarity with gaming terminology and the ability to translate content accurately within a gaming context.

• Experience with computer-assisted translation tools such as Crowdin, memoQ, Memsource, SDL Trados, Wordfast, or similar platforms.

• Excellent organization, prioritization, and time-management skills.

• Ability to manage multiple projects, adapt to quick turnaround times, and maintain quality when priorities change.

• A collaborative approach and the ability to communicate effectively in a highly team-oriented environment.

• Strong knowledge of operating systems, including Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and SharePoint.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience translating or localizing gaming and technical content.

• Passion for PC or console gaming.

• Familiarity with computer hardware, software development, or game design.

• Familiarity with game distribution platforms.

• Knowledge of different game genres and online gaming communities.

• Knowledge of gaming hardware and platform ecosystems.

Compensation

At Blueprint, we strive to offer competitive pay that reflects the value of our team members. Compensation for this role is influenced by a variety of factors, including skills, education, responsibilities, experience, and geographic market.

For candidates based in Washington State, the anticipated compensation range is $33.65 to $43.25 USD per hour, with a midpoint of $38.45 USD per hour. Please note that we typically do not hire new employees at the top of the posted range. Actual starting pay will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity. The final compensation and job title may vary depending on the selected candidate’s qualifications.

Remote, United States

This role may be performed remotely from within the United States. The team’s core coverage hours are 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time. Alternative schedules may be available based on the employee’s time zone and existing team coverage. When Pacific Time coverage is needed, employees must be available to work the established core hours.

jobs.description:
Job Opportunity: Lead Production Technician with Formative 3D in Falls Church, VA

Are you experienced with hand tools and power tools and enjoy helping others develop their skills? Do you take pride in quality work, solving technical challenges, and keeping production moving? Ready to bring your hands-on experience to advanced manufacturing and 3D printing? If so, we’d love to meet you!

As a Lead Production Technician, you’ll support manufacturing and post-processing operations at our new production facility. Working closely with the Post-Processing Manager, you’ll perform advanced finishing and assembly work, provide hands-on training to Production Technicians, and help coordinate daily production activities.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys staying actively involved in production while providing technical guidance to others. You’ll help ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and to quality standards while contributing to our first project and helping grow the business. This is a hands-on leadership role, not a direct supervisory position.

Salary range: $28-$34 per hour, depending on experience.

Key Responsibilities:

• Perform advanced post-processing tasks on 3D-printed parts, including drilling, hole cutting, sanding, trimming, deburring, and finishing.

• Provide hands-on training and technical guidance on the safe and proper use of hand tools, power tools, and equipment.

• Support the Post-Processing Manager in coordinating daily tasks, prioritizing work, and maintaining efficient production workflows.

• Review completed work for quality, accuracy, and consistency with established standards.

• Help develop and improve work instructions, standard operating procedures, and post-processing techniques.

• Troubleshoot technical challenges and recommend practical solutions to improve productivity and reduce rework.

• Support assembly operations, material handling, and organization of finished parts and supplies.

• Promote a clean, safe, and organized work environment, reinforcing safety procedures and proper PPE use.

• Communicate production progress, technical concerns, and operational needs to the Post-Processing Manager.

Qualifications:

• Strong hands-on experience operating hand tools and power tools, including drills, impact drivers, hole saws, sanders, and cutting equipment.

• Previous experience in manufacturing, construction, carpentry, fabrication, or assembly.

• Ability to accurately measure, drill, cut, assemble, and finish materials with minimal supervision.

• Strong attention to detail and ability to identify and resolve quality issues.

• Ability to train, guide, and support team members with patience and clear communication.

• Strong organizational skills and ability to balance hands-on work with team coordination.

• Ability to follow and reinforce work instructions, measurements, safety requirements, and standard operating procedures.

• Dependable, proactive, and comfortable taking initiative in a fast-paced production environment.

• CNC machine experience preferred; experience with 3D printing or advanced manufacturing is a plus. Neither is required.

• Willingness to work weekends.

• Ability to move regularly between production areas, assembly stations, and shipping/receiving; stand or walk for extended periods, up to 8 hours per day, 6 days a week; and regularly lift materials or equipment weighing 25–50 pounds.

• Ability to work in an industrial environment with noise, dust, and varying temperatures, using required PPE such as safety glasses, gloves, and hearing protection.

What We Offer:

• Comprehensive healthcare benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage.

• Competitive paid time off plans.

• Competitive retirement plans.

• Opportunity to develop your technical and leadership skills as we grow our advanced manufacturing operations.

Why Join Formative 3D?

At Formative 3D, we’re a 3D-printing startup on a mission to change the built environment. By leveraging large-format and FDM additive manufacturing, we’re building sustainable, scalable, modular systems.

Our shared purpose is to build trust with our clients, partners, subcontractors, and teammates while creating extraordinary experiences. No matter your background, education, or career path, if you share that vision, you belong at Formative 3D.

As we launch our new production facility, we’re looking for dependable, hands-on team members to help produce our first project and grow the business. Join us to share your expertise, support our production team, and contribute to a new approach to manufacturing.

Apply online today to join our team!

Bethesda Brings out the Best in Talented, Caring People!

Summary

Provides patient care related support including services relative to hygiene, nutrition, ambulation, elimination, and safety as directed by Charge Nurse per established departmental guidelines. Documents appropriately into patient record charting based on skill level and follows established standards and guidelines. Upon admission, accurately completes personal belonging sheet, obtains and records height, weight, and vital signs, orientates new resident to the facility and unit, ensures that resident receives an arm band and provides resident with a labeled admission kit. Interacts and maintains effective working relationships with other team members, charge nurse, and department managers. Maintains discretion in handling confidential information. Gives report to Charge Nurse at the end of each shift and completes walking rounds with the oncoming or leaving shift. May be assigned other duties as appropriate.

• CPR certification, or willing to obtain within six months of employment

• Ability to transfer and move patients who vary with ability to assist weighing 200+lbs using proper lifting techniques and with assistance when necessary

S&B USA is seeking an initiative-taking and analytical Sustainability & Business Analytics Intern to support the Vice President of External Affairs and Sustainability in advancing the company's sustainability strategy and reporting initiatives. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of sustainability, infrastructure delivery, business performance, and corporate strategy.

The successful candidate will contribute directly to the development of S&B USA's Annual Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Sustainability Report, assist with greenhouse gas emissions analysis, develop project-specific sustainability roadmaps for major heavy civil construction projects, and identify data-driven opportunities to improve both project outcomes and corporate performance.

This internship is ideal for an initiative-taker who is curious, detail-oriented, and interested in applying business, engineering, sustainability, or analytical skills to solve real-world challenges in the construction and infrastructure industry.

Key Responsibilities

CSR & Sustainability Reporting

• Support the preparation and publication of S&B USA's Annual CSR and Sustainability Report.

• Collect, validate, and analyze sustainability performance data from across the organization.

• Assist in developing report narratives, project case studies, graphics, and key performance indicators.

• Benchmark sustainability reporting practices and emerging industry trends.

Greenhouse Gas Emissions Analysis

• Assist with Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions inventory development and analysis.

• Evaluate fuel consumption, fleet usage, electricity consumption, and other emissions-related datasets.

• Develop visualizations and insights to communicate emissions performance and reduction opportunities.

• Support identification of data collection improvements to enhance future reporting.

Scope 3 Case Studies & Circular Economy Analysis

• Develop project-based case studies demonstrating Scope 3 emissions reductions achieved through innovative demolition, recycling, and material recovery practices.

• Quantify avoided emissions associated with material reuse, recycling, and diversion efforts.

• Research industry best practices for embodied carbon reduction and circular construction strategies.

• Assist in documenting sustainability success stories for clients, stakeholders, and corporate reporting.

Project Sustainability Roadmaps

• Support development of sustainability roadmaps for heavy civil construction projects, identifying practical opportunities to:

• Reduce emissions and fuel consumption

• Minimize waste generation

• Increase material recycling and reuse

• Improve water and resource efficiency

• Enhance community and environmental outcomes

• Collaborate with project teams to integrate sustainability considerations into project planning and execution.

Business Intelligence & Strategic Analysis

• Analyze operational and sustainability data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Assist in developing dashboards, scorecards, and executive-level reporting tools.

• Prepare recommendations that support strategic business objectives while advancing sustainability goals.

• Conduct research on emerging technologies, policy developments, industry benchmarks, and client expectations related to sustainable infrastructure development.

Cross-Functional Engagement

• Collaborate with operations, project management, environmental compliance, finance, equipment, and executive leadership teams.

• Support preparation of presentations, briefing materials, and strategic communications related to sustainability initiatives.

• Present findings and recommendations to company leadership at the conclusion of the internship.

Qualifications

Education

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in:

• Civil Engineering

• Environmental Engineering

• Construction Management

• Sustainability

• Environmental Science

• Business Analytics

• Data Analytics

• Economics

• Public Policy

• Or a related discipline

Preferred Skills

• Strong analytical and quantitative problem-solving abilities.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data analysis, pivot tables, and data visualization.

• Experience working with large datasets and developing actionable insights.

• Familiarity with sustainability reporting frameworks, greenhouse gas accounting principles, life-cycle assessment methodologies, or ESG reporting concepts.

• Experience with Power BI, Tableau, GIS, or other analytics software is a plus.

• Knowledge of heavy civil construction, infrastructure, transportation, or environmental systems is desirable but not required.

Desired Characteristics

• Self-starter with the ability to work independently and manage multiple projects.

• Naturally curious and eager to learn.

• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.

• Ability to translate technical information into actionable business insights.

• Comfortable collaborating across disciplines and interacting with both field and corporate personnel.

• Passion for sustainability, infrastructure, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Logistics

• Valid driver's license and ability to travel periodically to project sites.

• Ability to work safely in active construction environments while adhering to all company safety requirements and PPE protocols.

What You'll Gain

• Direct exposure to executive-level sustainability strategy and decision-making.

• Hands-on experience preparing a corporate sustainability report.

• Experience with greenhouse gas accounting and emissions management in the construction industry.

• Opportunities to influence sustainability initiatives on high-profile infrastructure projects.

• Exposure to business analytics, project delivery, and strategic communications.

• Mentorship from company leaders across operations, sustainability, and external affairs.

Core Values:

• Work Safely: Safety is our Culture

• Deliver Return: Earning a fair profit increases our long-term value

• Value People: Take Care of Employees and They Will Take Care of Clients

• Act with Integrity: Honesty Builds Trust

• Provide Solutions: Better Solutions Yield Greater Satisfaction

Many of our intern students go on to become full-time employees with us upon graduation!

Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Vice President, Navy Programs
jobs.description:
The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch.

We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

Role Summary

The Vice President, Navy Programs is accountable for Ursa Major's Navy portfolio end to end: program execution, contract performance, customer relationships and technical growth within the Navy account. You will lead a small Navy and DoD focused team, partner closely with the VP of Business Development, who owns capture and sales, and act as the senior executive face to the Navy's systems commands and program offices, its ﬂeet and requirements sponsors, the Navy's professional and industry associations, and the integrators who partner with us.

Recent Navy awards put Ursa Major on several major missile propulsion programs: the MK 104 motor for the Standard Missile family, the Compact Air-to-Air Missile (CAAM) and the Naval Modular Missile (NMM). These programs are early in their lives, and how well they are advanced and shaped over the next several years will decide Ursa Major's place in the Navy's missile supply base. The Vice President, Navy Programs is the executive who keeps advancing and shaping those programs and turns awarded work into delivered capability and a trusted customer relationship, working alongside the VP of Business Development, who leads capture and new-business pursuit. In October 2026 the Navy awarded Ursa Major two contracts totaling $137M to develop and qualify solid

rocket motors: $91M for CAAM and $46M for the NMM medium-range variant. In July 2026 it awarded $10M to take the MK 104 motor through critical design review and static ﬁre, building on a 2024 prototype contract and a $25M manufacturing pathﬁnder program with the Navy and the Office of Strategic Capital. Ursa Major has also recently won an award from Raytheon for the Tomahawk booster motor.

This is a role for a distinguished naval leader: someone who has earned ﬂag-officer-level trust and carried responsibility for sailors, budgets and mission outcomes at national scale. We want a strategic mind who sees the operational need and the industrial base that must meet it, whose judgment is respected in the Pentagon, at sea and on the factory ﬂoor, who speaks the Navy's language because they have lived it, and who builds teams that earn trust by delivering.

• Reports to: Chief Strategy Officer and Vice President for Defense

• Direct reports: Naval and Marine Corps portfolio directors

• Type: Full-time, executive team member

Key Responsibilities

• Own the Navy strategy. Set a multi-year plan to keep advancing and shaping Ursa Major's Navy programs, including MK 104, CAAM and NMM, aligned to Navy budget priorities, emerging requirements and the company's product roadmap.

• Support growth. Team with the VP of Business Development on Navy pursuits, including the follow-on phases of the CAAM and NMM programs, with technical strategy, customer insight and program credibility, and own the transition of awards into follow-on and production work.

• Deliver on contract. Work with program managers accountable for cost, schedule, technical performance and test milestones on MK 104, CAAM, NMM and future Navy motors, from critical design review and static ﬁre through qualiﬁcation, and resolve issues with the customer before they escalate.

• Build the customer relationship. Maintain senior relationships with PEO Integrated Warfare Systems, the Navy's systems commands, the Office of Naval Research, the Naval Energetic Systems and Technologies program, ﬂeet and requirements sponsors, and Congress-facing stakeholders where appropriate.

• Be the face of Ursa Major to the Navy community. Serve as the company's lead executive and public face to the Navy's professional and industry associations, such as the Navy League of the United States, the Surface Navy Association, the Naval Submarine League and the Association of Naval Aviation, representing Ursa Major at their symposia, exhibitions and events.

• Partner with primes and teammates. Execute teaming, subcontract and integration agreements with missile integrators, platform primes and other suppliers, with Business Development leading negotiation of new agreements.

• Shape requirements. Work with Engineering and Manufacturing to translate ﬂeet needs into propulsion solutions, shape emerging Navy requirements early, and scale from prototype to qualiﬁed, high-rate production.

• Help manage the P&L. Own margin, cost performance and delivered revenue for Navy programs, with disciplined forecasting to the executive team and board.

• Ensure compliance. Keep the business in line with FAR/DFARS, export controls (ITAR/EAR), cybersecurity (CMMC) and security requirements, including facility clearance and classiﬁed-contracting readiness as the company moves into Top Secret work.

• Lead and develop people. Hire, coach and retain a high-performing team in a fast-moving, mission-driven culture.

• Guide the broader service portfolio. Work across Ursa Major's other military-service portfolios, including the U.S. Air Force, Army and Space Force, and help shape engagement and leadership selection for portfolios that do not yet have a dedicated leader.

Required Qualiﬁcations

• Senior executive leadership at the ﬂag officer level, or Senior Executive Service equivalent, ideally with Navy command and acquisition experience and a record of leading large organizations, budgets and operational outcomes.

• 15+ years in aerospace and defense, with at least 8 years leading Navy or Marine Corps programs or major program execution at the director level or above.

• Track record of delivering and growing programs of record, OTAs or SBIR Phase III awards, with measurable results on cost, schedule and performance.

• Deep knowledge of Navy acquisition: the Navy's systems commands, program executive offices such as PEO Integrated Warfare Systems, the Office of Naval Research and the planning, programming, budgeting and execution (PPBE) cycle.

• Hands-on experience with propulsion, missiles, hypersonics, munitions or space systems, enough to speak credibly with engineers and customers.

• Demonstrated P&L accountability and experience managing cost-type and ﬁxed-price contracts.

• Working command of FAR/DFARS, ITAR/EAR and DoD security requirements.

• Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, business or a related ﬁeld.

• Active U.S. Top Secret clearance, or the ability to obtain one.

Preferred Qualiﬁcations

• Prior service as a Navy or Marine Corps ﬂag officer or acquisition leader, or a senior civilian role in a Navy systems command or program office.

• Experience taking a technology from lab demonstration to production with a startup or high-growth defense company.

• Prior experience with solid rocket motors, energetics, missile qualiﬁcation or additive

manufacturing.

• Established relationships with Navy and Department of Defense senior leaders and prime contractor program teams.

• MBA or advanced degree in engineering, public policy or a related discipline.

What Success Looks Like at 6, 12 and 24 Months

• By 6 months: a written Navy program plan, agreed with the Chief Strategy Officer and Senior Vice

President for Defense and approved by the executive team, with named targets by mission area.

• By 6 months: a joint pursuit plan with Business Development for the top Navy opportunities, including the follow-on phases of CAAM and NMM, and a clear view of leadership needs across the other service portfolios.

• By 12 months: existing Navy contracts on cost and schedule, with MK 104 through critical design

review and static ﬁre and every active CAAM and NMM milestone tracked and met or recovered.

• By 12 months: regular senior engagement across Navy systems commands, program offices and ﬂeet sponsors, and a set of strategic teaming agreements with integrators.

• By 24 months: a stable leadership bench under you with clear roles for program delivery, test and customer engagement; Navy leadership sees Ursa Major as a trusted propulsion partner; and at least one program has moved from development toward qualiﬁed, high-rate production

Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $265,000 - $325,000 determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

Classification: Full-time Exempt

Benefits Include: (Please note, Interns are not eligible for benefits)

• Unlimited PTO - Vacation, Sick, Personal, and Bereavement

• Paid Parental and Adoptive Leave

• Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance

• Tax Advantage Accounts (HSA/FSA)

• Employer Paid Short and Long Term Disability, Basic Life, AD&D

• Additional Benefit Options Including Voluntary Life and Emergency Medical Transport

• EAP Program

• Retirement Savings Plan - 401k with Company Match

How To Apply:
Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by filling out the application below and clicking "Submit Application". This position will be posted for a minimum of 3 days and will remain open until filled or adjusted based on the volume of applicants.

NOTE: Research suggests that women and BIPOC individuals may self-select out of opportunities if they don't meet 100% of the job requirements. We encourage anyone who believes they have the skills and the drive necessary to succeed here to apply for this role.

Must be a U.S. Person (this includes U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents).

Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

We’re an equal-opportunity employer. You will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

No outside recruiters, please.

jobs.title: Senior Medical Science Liaison, South East Region
jobs.description:
Using living cells to treat – and sometimes even cure – cancer is one of the most dramatic advances in modern medicine. Patients with hematologic malignancies have been successfully treated with cell therapies. However, these profound results have not yet been achieved in patients with solid tumors, representing approximately 90% of all cancers. And for patients with hematologic malignancies, there is a need for next-generation cell therapies that can deliver increased response rates and longer duration of response.  We are a clinical-stage company advancing a pipeline of next-generation CAR T-cell therapies for patients with solid tumors or hematologic malignancies. Lyell’s product candidates are enhanced with novel technology designed to generate T cells that resist exhaustion and have qualities of durable stemness in order to drive durable tumor cytotoxicity and achieve consistent and long-lasting clinical response. We were founded by cell therapy pioneers whose decades of research elevated the broader understanding of T-cell biology and its interaction with cancer. In our quest to advance next-generation CAR T-cell therapies, we have built a fully integrated company capable of discovering new technologies, translating science into therapies, manufacturing cell therapy products, and clinically evaluating them in patients. Our culture is based on Science, Respect, Collaboration, and Courage and reflects who we are, the environment we create, and our mission's urgency.

Lyell is a late-stage clinical company advancing a pipeline of next-generation CAR T-cell therapies for patients with hematologic malignancies and solid tumors.

As a member of Lyell's U.S. Field Medical Team, the Senior Medical Science Liaison will serve as a field-based scientific resource on cellular therapy for the external health care professional (HCP) community and internal partners. Reporting to Director, Field Medical, this experienced field medical professional will execute regional medical strategy, maintain strong scientific relationships with key stakeholders and clinical trial sites, and generate actionable insights through robust territory engagement in support of Lyell's clinical programs. This role is expected to bring AI-fluency to daily field medical practice — leveraging emerging tools for scientific synthesis, engagement planning, and insight capture to operate with exceptional speed and quality.

This role operates as an individual contributor with the expectation of mentoring MSLs, along with meaningful opportunities for regional peer leadership and project ownership as the field team scales.  Candidates must reside in the South East U.S. territory. Ideal locations include major hub cities such as Miami, FL; Atlanta, GA; or Tampa, FL, but other South East U.S. locations with convenient airport access will be considered.

KEY ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Territory Execution

• Develop and execute a comprehensive territory strategy aligned with Medical Affairs priorities through mapping and engagement of HCPs, cellular therapy treatment centers, CAR-T referring networks, and disease-area influencers.

• Leverage deep local knowledge of the territory landscape — augmented by AI-powered landscape tools, literature synthesis platforms, and digital signal monitoring — to implement tactical execution at the regional level.

• Proactively identify field medical resource and educational gaps and recommend internal and external solutions.

Scientific Exchange & Stakeholder Engagement

• Serve as a regional scientific resource in cellular immunotherapy, delivering high-impact, fair-balanced scientific exchange tailored to the needs of: Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) Academic investigators Transplant and cell therapy centers Community oncology and hematology treaters

• Engage in deep, peer-to-peer scientific discussions across complex topics such as CAR-T mechanism, safety management, durability, immune cell fitness, and trial protocols.

• Represent the organization with field presence at local regional conferences and major scientific meetings (e.g., ASH, ASCO, ESMO, SITC); facilitate advisory boards with national-level KOLs and multidisciplinary community HCPs.

• Utilize AI-assisted tools for pre-call planning, scientific literature synthesis, and post-interaction insight capture to maximize the quality and consistency of HCP engagements.

Strategic Impact, Peer Leadership & Quality Adherence

• Generate high-quality, actionable medical insights by applying deep scientific acumen across scientific conversations, clinical practice patterns, and competitive intelligence — using AI-enabled tools to accelerate synthesis, summarization, and insight delivery to internal stakeholders.

• Actively contribute to field medical projects and workstreams, with opportunity to serve in regional project leadership roles (e.g., compound medical insights lead, study lead, congress lead, onboarding/training lead).

• Partner with Clinical Operations and Clinical Development to support site identification, study start-up and enrollment, and scientific training to investigators, sub-investigators, research staff, and referral sites for pivotal clinical trials.

• As an individual contributor, mentor MSLs and contribute to team development, including support of MSL hiring and onboarding under direction of functional leadership.

• Maintain strict adherence to compliance standards and accurate and timely documentation of field activity, insights, and expenses.

• Contribute to the responsible adoption of AI tools within the field medical function, while maintaining compliance and data integrity standards.

PREFERRED EDUCATION

• PharmD, PhD, MD, or DO with residency/fellowship and board certification for clinical degrees preferred. Advanced degree in health sciences (NP, PA, RN) considered if extensive clinical/medical experience in therapeutic areas.

• Oncology/hematology specialty required; lymphoma and/or CAR-T cell therapy experience preferred. Solid tumor experience (particularly GI oncology) and launch experience valued.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

• 8+ years pharmaceutical/biotech industry experience, with 2+ years in a field medical or MSL role. Prior experience in a Senior MSL capacity preferred.

• Demonstrated success engaging multi-disciplinary academic and community providers.

• Track record of problem solving and proactive innovation in medical affairs.

• Demonstrated experience incorporating technology such as AI tools into field medical workflows, with a track record of rapid technology adoption.

• Experience contributing to MSL team development a plus.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

• Strong knowledge of clinical trial processes, CAR-T operational pathways, and latest immuno-oncology science.

• Expertise tailoring complex scientific and clinical data into relevant scientific exchange.

• Exceptional communication, presence, and scientific storytelling abilities.

• Comfort operating at the intersection of immuno-oncology science and emerging technology, including AI-enabled field operations.

• Proactive self-starter with the ability to work autonomously in a rapidly evolving, high-growth biotech environment.

• Strong scientific curiosity, adaptability, and comfort with ambiguity.

• Demonstrated ability to mentor or informally lead peers in a field medical setting.

• Exceptional collaboration and influence.

• Strong ethical judgment and integrity.

• Passion for transforming patient outcomes through cutting-edge science.

Frequent travel (up to 50-70%), including visits to cellular treatment centers, community practices, and local regional conferences.

The salary range for this position is $190,000 to $230,000, annually, with the opportunity to earn an annual bonus. The salary range is an estimate, and the actual salary may vary based on Lyell’s compensation practices and an applicant’s qualifications and experience. Employees are also eligible to participate in Lyell’s Equity Incentive Plan.

jobs.title: Strategic Alliances Manager, Partnerships
jobs.description:
The Strategic Alliances Manager develops and grows revenue-generating partnerships that expand market access, create qualified pipeline, and deliver long-term value for Relias, its partners, and customers. The role owns assigned alliances from joint planning through commercial execution, aligning partner priorities with Relias capabilities and coordinating Sales, Solutions, Marketing, Product, Legal, Finance, and customer-facing teams. This individual contributor applies partnership management and consultative sales expertise to build reciprocal relationships, activate partner sellers, and convert shared opportunities into measurable business results.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

Alliance Strategy, Relationship Management, and Growth

• Owning the strategy and commercial performance of assigned alliances, including partner-sourced pipeline, revenue, relationship health, and agreed growth goals.
• Building trusted relationships with partner executives, sales leaders, and account teams; understand each partner’s business model, customers, economics, and strategic priorities to shape a mutually beneficial value proposition.
• Identifying growth opportunities within existing partnerships and evaluate prospective alliances based on strategic fit, customer value, revenue potential, and execution requirements.

Joint Business Planning and Performance Management

• Developing and executing joint business plans with shared revenue objectives, target accounts, sales activities, investments, owners, milestones, and measures of progress.
• Leading regular partner business reviews, evaluate performance against shared commitments, and recommend where to expand, adjust, or discontinue activities based on results.
• Maintaining accurate partner plans, opportunity records, attribution, and forecasts in CRM; distinguish partner-sourced and partner-influenced business under agreed definitions.

Co-Selling, Opportunity Development, and Sales Execution

• Partnering with Relias sales leaders and account executives on account mapping, prospecting, discovery, opportunity qualification, business-case development, and pursuit strategy.
• Applying consultative selling practices to uncover business challenges, navigate buying groups, articulate value, and advance partner-related opportunities through the sales cycle.
• Engaging Solutions and other subject-matter experts early to connect customer needs to appropriate capabilities across the Relias portfolio and maintain clear ownership and next steps.

Partner Activation and Go-to-Market Programs

• Activating partner sales teams through enablement, account alignment, coordinated outreach, and clear referral or co-selling processes that convert introductions into qualified opportunities.
• Collaborating with Marketing and Product Marketing on partner campaigns, webinars, events, and customer communications tied to defined audiences, pipeline objectives, and follow-up plans.
• Developing and test partnership approaches such as joint offerings, referral programs, co-selling motions, and new routes to market; use results to determine whether to refine, scale, or stop an approach.

Commercial Agreements and Cross-Functional Execution

• Supporting commercial proposals, partnership negotiations, agreement renewals, and operating terms in collaboration with leadership, Legal, and Finance.
• Coordinating across Sales, Solutions, Product, Marketing, Legal, Finance, and customer-facing teams to fulfill commitments, resolve barriers, and sustain momentum.
• Surfacing recurring customer and partner insights that can inform partner strategy, offering development, and go-to-market improvements.

YOU'VE GOT WHAT IT TAKES IF YOU HAVE:

• 5+ years of combined experience in strategic alliances, partnerships, consultative B2B sales, channel management, or business development.
• Direct experience developing or growing revenue-generating partnerships through joint business planning, partner activation, and measurable pipeline or revenue outcomes.
• Demonstrated success in a quota-bearing or commercially accountable environment, including opportunity management, forecasting, and commercial relationship growth.
• Experience collaborating with sales leaders and account executives on account planning, joint pursuits, opportunity progression, and closing partner-related business.
• Bachelor’s Degree

Salary Information:

We are targeting an On-Target-Earnings of ~$85,000 - $120,000 annually. Relias considers many factors when making an offer including; established salary range, internal budgets, business need, education and years of applicable work experience possessed by the applicant. Further, salary is only one element of our total compensation and benefits package.

IN OFFICE REQUIREMENT:

Relias values collaboration and wants to ensure that our team members have opportuniites to work with their managers regularly for professional development opportunities.  This role requires that you live in the state of North Carolina, within a commutable distance to our office.  You would be expected to work in our Morrisville, NC Headquarters approximately 30 days/quarter.

jobs.title: Associate Director - IT Mergers, Acquisitions, Divestitures, and Collaborations
jobs.description:
Our Business Technology Solutions (BTS) team shapes the digital transformation accelerating the future of medicine at AbbVie - and we do it together, asking bold questions and taking on tough challenges through deep, honest collaboration. In the role of Associate Director, Mergers, Acquisitions, Divestitures and Collaborations, you will join a diverse, global team that invests in your customized career growth and uses technology and data to positively impact people’s lives.

This role represents the BTS organization as the overall Integration Lead working directly with cross-functional business and BTS teams to execute deal transactions to further grow AbbVie’s Therapeutic Areas. This role performs as the primary BTS Integration Lead responsible for planning and executing deals addressing cross-functional dependencies to achieve AbbVie’s desired end-state operating model as we integrate or divest companies.

For anyone who wants to use technology and data to make a difference in people’s lives, shape the digital transformation of a leading biopharmaceutical company, and secure sustainable career growth within a diverse, global team: we are ready for you. In this role, you can expect competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits for every career stage and a commitment to your well-being in the workplace. Additionally, you will add your unique experience to an employee-driven culture with vibrant Employee Resource Groups and a passion for equity, equality, inclusion, and diversity that reflects the diversity of our communities and the patients and customers we serve.

Mergers & Acquisitions (M&As) include multiple types of transactions that require BTS leadership.  “M&A” transactions include R&D Ventures, Partnerships & Alliances, Co-Promotion, Co-Development, Divesting Products and/or Sites, Plant Acquisitions and Divestitures, and Full Company Acquisitions.

​​This is a critical role in partnering with business leadership to further define the strategy to evolve BTS’s M&A organization, services, and playbooks for the various types of M&A deals.  This will include cross-functional engagement and leadership across the BTS organization and working with AbbVie’s business leaders, Search and Evaluation, Business Development, and our Transition Office.

Responsibilities:

• ​​​Lead BTS due diligence on target companies, assessing systems, data, cybersecurity, to inform deal decision, integration costs, and Day 1 readiness.
• ​Deal Lead over multiple deal transactions responsible for overall program health, financials, and reporting. For each deal, establish the cross-functional BTS team fully accountable to integrate or divest people, facilities, data, and systems.
• ​​Work with the business and BTS functional leads to clearly define business decisions, solution options and recommendations for a given deal based on deal model, size, complexity, risk, and speed to business value.
• ​​Own IT financial model and integration budget for each deal from due diligence estimates to execution.
• ​Responsible for escalating cross-functional risks and issues and driving them to resolution, and driving risks and issues cross-functionally.
• ​​Presenting BTS updates to the function SVPs in the Executive Steering Committee.
• ​​Continuous improvement projects to drive speed and agility in BTS M&A services and capabilities.
• Identify and implement AI innovative solutions and capabilities to challenge status quo and bring value to the business faster.
• ​​Responsible for compliance with BTS’s SLC, Corporate and Divisional policies and procedures.

Required:

• Bachelor's Degree with 9 years of experience OR Master's Degree with 8 years of experience OR PhD with 4 years of experience.
• ​Experience working on mergers, acquisitions, and divestiture projects across a largescale enterprise.
• ​​Experience leading a portfolio of business applications and leading large, complex cross-functional global IT implementations.
• ​​​Skilled in creating AI agents and tools to reimagine or improve a process or capability. Led and implemented multiple projects that drove speed, efficiencies, and/or cost savings.
• ​​Strong Project Management, Executive Stakeholder Engagement, Business Systems Applications and delivering complex cross-functional global programs.

jobs.title: Senior Director Communications & Mobilization - North America Advocacy
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ONE CAMPAIGN

ONE is a global, nonpartisan organization fighting for a more just world by demanding the investments needed to create economic opportunities and healthier lives in Africa. We do this by deploying trusted and dynamic advocacy that leverages hard-hitting data, credible grassroots activism, creative political engagement, and strategic partnerships. We use all this to influence decision-makers to take action and tackle the world’s biggest challenges. Read more at www.one.org.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Director, Communications & Mobilization is a newly created, senior leadership role that brings together ONE’s public voice and its people power in the United States and Canada. Reporting to the Executive Director, North America, the Senior Director will lead an integrated function spanning press and media relations, digital, website, creative and social media, and membership mobilization, including campaigning and in-person activations.

This leader will set one unified strategy that connects what ONE says with what ONE does: shaping the public narrative, driving earned media coverage, growing and activating a diverse coalitions and base of volunteers, and turning that combined visibility and advocacy into concrete support for ONE’s policy objectives with the US and Canadian governments.

The Senior Director will lead an integrated team of 11 professionals spanning media relations, digital campaigns, content, social media and design and membership mobilization. This includes managing the Senior Director, Membership Mobilization, who leads ONE’s campaigns and regional organizing team.

As a member of the North America Advocacy Leadership Team, the Senior Director will line manage the Communications and Membership Mobilization teams, including managers, and partner closely with Government Relations, Policy, and global Communications, Content, Brand and Campaigns colleagues.

The successful candidate will be a strong leader with a track record of running integrated communications and campaigning programs, a deep understanding of the North American media and political landscapes, and a passion for development, economic justice, or global health.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

Integrated Strategy & Leadership

• Develop and lead an integrated North America communications and mobilization strategy, aligned with global campaigns and ONE’s annual advocacy goals, that connects earned, owned, and social media with coalition building and grassroots and in-person organizing.

• Set annual plans, goals, and success metrics for the Communications and Membership Mobilization teams, and hold the function accountable for delivering against them.

• Serve as a member of the North America Advocacy Leadership Team, working collaboratively with Government Relations, Policy, and Canada team leaders to design campaigns that move decision-makers.

• Represent North America in global discussions on communications, campaigns, membership, and metrics, and serve as a thought partner to the Chief Communications Officer and global Communications leadership.

Communications, Media & Narrative

• Oversee all North America press and media work, including media relations, press releases, op-eds, talking points, letters to the editor, and background briefings, to generate high-impact coverage.

• In partnership with the North America media manager, cultivate strong relationships with journalists, editors, and outlets at the local, regional, and national levels across the US and Canada, including development and global affairs reporters.

• Shape the public voice and presence of the Executive Director and other senior spokespeople, and serve as a senior spokesperson for ONE in North America.

• Lead crisis and reputation management for North America, escalating to the CCO and outside experts in extreme situations.

Digital, Social, Website & Creative

• Oversee North America digital, website, social media, and creative work, including content plans across platforms, in collaboration with the global Content, Brand and Creative teams.

• Ensure ONE’s North America channels are active, timely, on-brand, and aligned with campaign priorities, and that press and campaign content is reflected across the website and digital platforms.

• Drive innovation across traditional and emerging channels, including creator and influencer partnerships, to reach new and diverse audiences.

• Partner with Content and Creative Partnerships teams to build long-term relationships with artists, content creators, and public figures who can amplify ONE’s mission.

Membership Mobilization & Campaigning

• Provide strategic leadership to ONE’s North America membership mobilization efforts, managing and partnering with the Senior Director, Membership Mobilization to set direction, priorities, and goals for campaigns and regional organizing.

• Evolve ONE’s mobilization model, testing new organizing tactics, digital-to-field pathways, and distributed and relational organizing approaches, and scaling what works.

• Ensure grassroots campaigns, in-person activations, lobby days, and events are fully integrated with media, digital, content, and creative, so every mobilization moment reaches decision-makers and the public.

• Set the strategy for growing and deepening a diverse base of volunteers, leaders, activists, and members, including engagement with college campuses, faith leaders, and African diaspora communities.

• Oversee partner and coalition relationships that extend ONE’s reach and influence, working with the Events and Partnerships team.

• Champion data-driven campaigning, holding the function accountable for clear metrics on member growth, actions, and campaign impact.

Team, Budget & Operations

• Lead, mentor, and develop the Communications and Membership Mobilization teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, high-performing culture.

• Build one team culture across communications and mobilization that is collaborative, inclusive, creative, and high-performing, with clear roles and shared goals.

• Own the budget for the Communications and Mobilization function, ensuring spending is aligned with the strategic plan and properly managed and controlled.

• Lead resource allocation and workforce planning across the function, including the use of consultants, agencies, and vendors.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

• Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Political Science, Public Relations, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.

• A minimum of 12 years’ relevant professional experience in communications, campaigning, and/or advocacy, within a non-profit, political organization, PR agency, newsroom, or similar environment.

• At least 7 years of people management experience, including leading multi-disciplinary teams and managing managers.

• A proven record of leading integrated campaigns that combine earned media, digital, and grassroots mobilization to achieve policy or legislative outcomes.

• A track record of securing earned coverage in mainstream North American media, with strong, established relationships with journalists.

• Subject matter expertise in the workings of Congress and the Executive Branch, contemporary campaign tactics, and techniques for cultivating grassroots advocates; knowledge of Canadian politics a plus.

• Demonstrated success in budget management, resource planning, and strategic planning.

• Experience in crisis communications and reputation management.

• Strong knowledge of, and interest in, North American politics, foreign affairs, and/or global development, and a clear appreciation of ONE’s nonpartisan approach.

• Working knowledge of digital, social, and campaign platforms and tools.

• Willingness and legal authorization to travel to both the United States and Canada on a regular basis.

• Ability to maintain the highest degree of confidentiality regarding all aspects of work at all times.

• Legal authorization to work in the United States without restrictions.

OTHER ATTRIBUTES

• A leader of leaders who can build shared purpose across distinct disciplines

• An understanding of the complexities surrounding collaboration in a global matrixed organization

• Strategic and creative, with the ability to simplify complex policy issues into compelling messages

• Action oriented and results focused

• Collaborative mindset and strong interpersonal, diplomatic, and relationship-building skills

• Sound judgment and composure in high-pressure situations

• Highly organized, detail oriented, analytical, and self-motivated

• Flexible, resourceful, and an independent problem solver

TRAVEL & LANGUAGE SKILLS: Travel up to 25% international and domestic, including regular travel to Ottawa. Fluency in English required. Fluency in French preferred.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS/WORK ENVIRONMENT: This role is a hybrid position, with the expectation of being in the office three days per week. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

COMPENSATION: USD$150,000 - $180,000. New hires are typically brought in between the minimum and midpoint of the job level salary range depending on qualifications, experience and internal equity.

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS: If you are ready to join the fight for a more just world, please submit a resume and cover letter to this opening at ONE jobs (http://www.one.org/jobs).

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants. When an applicant with a disability needs an accommodation to have an equal opportunity to compete for a job, they may request it orally or in writing (please email recruiting@one.org). ONE will process requests for reasonable accommodation and will provide reasonable accommodations where appropriate, in a prompt and efficient manner.

We understand that a diversity of strengths, experiences, and backgrounds makes our team stronger. If this position interests you, we encourage you to apply and tell us why you are a great candidate for the role. ONE does not discriminate in its selection and employment practices. We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. To learn more about our diversity and inclusion work and priorities, visit https://www.one.org/about/diversity.

Due to the number of inquiries that ONE receives, we thank all candidates for their interest yet only those who are selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
Wealth.com http://Wealth.com is the industry’s leading AI Wealth Management platform, empowering financial advisors to offer modern, comprehensive estate planning solutions to their clients. By combining cutting-edge technology, AI, and unmatched human expertise, we deliver a seamless experience that sets us apart. Beyond having one of the most coveted domain names in FinTech, wealth.com http://wealth.com is a dynamic, revenue-generating startup experiencing rapid yet sustainable growth.

 

A key reason behind our position as the #1 estate planning platform is our team. Our people thrive in a collaborative, supportive culture that fosters innovation and makes wealth.com http://wealth.com a place where everyone truly enjoys working. Wealth.com http://Wealth.com is certified as a Great Place to Work for 2024 and named a 2024 finalist for Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Innovators!



About the Role

Wealth.com http://Wealth.com is looking for a GTM Engineer to build and maintain the automation and integration layer that powers our revenue operations. You will report directly to the Director of Revenue Operations, GTM Systems, and be the hands-on builder who turns strategy into working systems.

This is a technical execution role. You will spend your time building, configuring, debugging, and optimizing across a modern GTM stack. If you like seeing the thing you built actually ship and make a team faster, this role is for you.



What You'll Own

Automation & Integrations

 - Build and maintain automated workflows across our GTM stack.

 - Own the integration layer between Salesforce, Outreach, Gong, ChiliPiper, DealHub, and other tools in the stack

 - Build and maintain API connections, webhooks, and data syncs that keep our systems in agreement

 - Identify and automate manual processes across the sales and marketing motion

Salesforce Administration

 - Handle day-to-day Salesforce administration including object configuration, flows, workflow rules, and permission sets

 - Support data hygiene initiatives including deduplication, enrichment, and validation rules

 - Assist in implementing data model changes as the business evolves

AI-Assisted Workflows

 - Implement LLM-assisted automations including call summaries, enrichment pipelines, and follow-up draft generation

 - Maintain and iterate on prompt-based workflows under the direction of the Director

 - Evaluate and integrate AI tools into existing workflows as the stack grows

Revenue Data & Reporting

 - Own the accuracy of data flowing between systems including audit processes and alerting for data breaks

 - Build and maintain enrichment pipelines that keep account and contact data current

 - Support attribution reporting and pipeline analytics



What We're Looking For

Required

 - 2-4 years in a technical RevOps or sales systems role with direct ownership of Salesforce administration, workflow automation, or GTM integrations.

 - Salesforce proficiency including flows, reports, custom objects, and core admin tasks

 - Experience building AI-assisted workflows or working with LLM integrations

 - Comfortable working with APIs, webhooks, and basic data transformation.

 - Detail-oriented with strong data instincts. You catch errors before they propagate.

 - Background in B2B SaaS.

Preferred

 - Experience with Outreach, Gong, ChiliPiper, and/or DealHub

 - Basic scripting ability in Python or JavaScript

 - Familiarity with SQL or BI tools (Omni, Looker, or similar)

 - Experience in fintech, or wealth management



What Success Looks Like
