 - Built In’s 2023 - 2025 Best Startups to Work For In New York City https://builtin.com/awards/new-york-city/2025/best-startup-places-to-work#brigit

 - Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies of 2022 https://www.fastcompany.com/90724459/most-innovative-companies-personal-finance-2022

 - Business Insider’s Most Promising Consumer Startups 2022 https://www.businessinsider.com/most-promising-consumer-tech-startups-of-2022-8#brigit-a-automated-money-lender-5

 - Forbes Fintech 50 2022 https://www.forbes.com/sites/isabelcontreras/2022/06/07/the-future-of-personal-finance-fintech-50-2022/?sh=1fbbd36d5235

Role overview

Brigit is looking for a Senior IT Operations Manager to build, mature, and scale our internal IT Operations function. You'll partner closely with our VP of Engineering, Security, Compliance, and People teams to develop and execute Brigit's IT strategy. While you'll oversee one IT Support Specialist responsible for day-to-day help desk operations, this role is primarily focused on building scalable processes, improving security and compliance, driving automation, and ensuring operational excellence as Brigit continues to grow.



We're looking for someone who enjoys creating structure where it doesn't yet exist-someone who is a builder, a problem solver, and a hands-on leader who takes ownership, drives execution, and isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves to get things done.



What you’ll be doing

 - Day-to-Day IT Operations
   
   - Own Brigit's day-to-day IT Operations strategy while partnering with our IT Support Specialist on daily support activities, providing mentorship, coaching, and prioritization
   
   - Work with our MSP to provision hardware and manage user onboarding and offboarding
   
   - Own VPN infrastructure - troubleshoot connectivity issues and manage certificate-based device access
   
   - Ensure compliance and consistent adherence to existing IT policies and procedures and develop/mature policies where they don’t exist
   
   - Review and update our IT Risk assessment on a quarterly basis

 - Identity & Access Management
   
   - Own Identity & Access Management (IAM) across Brigit
   
   - Administer and continuously improve our Single Sign-On (SSO) environment with Okta, including SAML, SCIM, provisioning, deprovisioning, and role-based access control

 - Security Infrastructure & Operations
   
   - Implement and maintain security configurations across software, hardware, and cloud infrastructure in line with audit standards
   
   - Manage security tooling: firewalls, SIEM, and intrusion detection/prevention systems
   
   - Evaluate new technologies that improve security, scalability, automation, and the employee experience
   
   - Serve as Brigit's IT/security point of contact with our parent company (Upbound) and affiliated brands - coordinating incident communication, aligning on policies, and pushing back where needed

 - IT Audit Management & Support
   
   - Serve as primary liaison for third-party IT audits (SOC I & II, PCI, penetration tests, SOX) in partnership with our compliance team
   
   - Drive remediation planning for any audit findings

 - Incident Management
   
   - Participate in and help improve Brigit's incident response process
   
   - Define escalation paths, classification standards, and post-incident review practices

 - Documentation & Operational Excellence
   
   - Own the creation, refinement, maintenance, and governance of all IT documentation, including system architecture docs, SOPs, operational runbooks, onboarding/offboarding documentation, knowledge base articles, and internal IT policies
   
   - Develop and improve our Jira-based internal help desk, including process improvements and automation
   
   - Establish documentation standards that improve consistency, knowledge sharing, audit readiness, and operational maturity
   
   - Identify gaps in existing documentation and proactively build scalable processes where none currently exist

 - Collaboration & Training
   
   - Partner with Engineering to strengthen authentication, access controls, and security best practices across the organization
   
   - Conduct internal security training to promote security awareness across the company
   
   - Build trusted relationships with vendors, external partners, and third-party auditors to continuously assess and improve Brigit's security posture and IT ecosystem
   
   - Contribute to Brigit’s internal AI task force from an IT and security lens
     
     

What you have

 - 6+ years of experience in IT, with 2+ years at a fast-growing tech company or startup environment required

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Management Information Systems (MIS), or related field

 - Hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure (ideally GCP).

 - Experience managing an IDP Platform such as Okta

 - Experience managing a managed service provider (MSP) such as Rippling

 - Experience with Jira for help desk or project management is a plus

 - Experience serving as the IT lead or primary liaison during SOC 1, SOC 2, PCI, penetration testing, or similar compliance audits.

 - Strong understanding of security frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, or similar.

 - Experience with implementing security tools and monitoring systems.

 - Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally.

 - Ability to balance long-term strategic initiatives with day-to-day operational needs.

 - Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or equivalent are a plus.



Location

 - NYC/NJ Candidates: If you are located within reasonable commuting distance to the NYC office, the expectation would be a hybrid onsite schedule of 3x per week.

 - Remote candidates: Travel to NYC for 1 week per month would be required.



Compensation

The anticipated annual base salary for this position is $135,000 - $160,000. This range does not include any other compensation components or other benefits for which an individual may be eligible (other benefits listed below). The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, which may include as applicable, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.

 

Our benefits and team

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - Flexible PTO Policy

 - 401k plan

 - Paid Parental Leave

 - Physical and mental wellbeing benefits including Wellhub for access to virtual workouts and discounted gym memberships, and Headspace Care for covered virtual therapy sessions and unlimited on demand health support

 - Monthly reimbursements to use against wifi and cell phone bills

 - Annual reimbursement for Learning & Development

 - Help hard working Americans build a brighter financial future

 - High-growth company

 - A dynamic, flexible and collaborative start-up work environment with a highly talented team
   
   

Brigit is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees without regard to race, religion, color, sex, pregnancy (including breast feeding and related medical conditions), national origin, citizenship status, uniform service member status, age, genetic information, disability, or any other protected status in accordance with all applicable federal, state and local laws. jobs.title: Associate Manager, Paid Social, NYT Wirecutter
jobs.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

About Wirecutter

Wirecutter, part of The New York Times, helps people make decisions through rigorous product testing and recommendations. Its authority depends on reader trust, editorial independence and a clear point of view.

About the role

Wirecutter is looking for an Associate Manager of Paid Social to grow our paid social program. You'll report to the Performance Marketing Manager, joining a multidisciplinary performance marketing team working across search, social, display, video, and emerging channels.

You will oversee paid social operations across our Affiliate and Store businesses, driving direct-response revenue and audience growth. You will blend in-platform campaign building with copywriting, creative briefing, and A/B testing to establish paid social as a predictable growth engine. You'll work with other marketing associates, leaders, legal teams, freelancers, and in-house creatives to turn campaign goals into work that reflects Wirecutter's trusted voice.

Responsibilities

• In-Platform Execution: Build, launch, QA, and improve campaigns within Meta Ads Manager and other platforms (TikTok, Pinterest, etc.), maintaining strict account hygiene and QA standards.

• Span Lines of Business: Support marketing for both the Affiliate and Wirecutter Store businesses, which involve direct-response revenue and broader Wirecutter brand-awareness campaigns. Build context on work across both businesses and how their performance and audiences can affect one another.

• Guide Creative & Copy: Write high-converting ad and on-image copy, brief in-house and freelance creative partners, and usher assets through brand and legal compliance processes.

• Scale Through Testing: Partner with the Performance Marketing Manager and analytics colleagues to design and implement iterative tests across creative concepts, copy hooks, formats, placements, new platforms, and audience segments and apply the insights.

• Analyze Performance: Monitor daily pacing and performance metrics (CPA, ROAS, CVR, revenue), turning campaign data into optimization roadmaps and insights for the broader Wirecutter team.

• Collaborate: Align paid social efforts with our cross-channel team (Search, Display, Email/Klaviyo) and product teams across both the Affiliate and Wirecutter Store businesses.

• Industry Updates: Stay current on platform changes, privacy and measurement developments, and paid social best practices; share useful updates and opportunities with teammates.

• Exemplify Our Values: Demonstrate support for Wirecutter's commitment to reader trust and The New York Times's journalistic independence.

Basic Qualifications

jobs.title: Field Operations Manager I, Plant Maintenance
jobs.description:
At gFiber, we believe that great internet has the power to drive innovation, strengthen communities, enable the impossible, and do all the everyday things that make all of our world go round. And the job of creating better internet is never done - so we’re growing! Our team is committed to building a place where people who want to make a difference can grow their careers and find their spot to belong.

The application window will be open until at least November 29th, 2026. This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the specified date.

Role Description

As the Field Operations Manager I, you will oversee all field support, splitting time between the central office and field, for local operations, including planning, coaching, scheduling, and coordination of all team activities. You’ll oversee a team that includes Construction Technicians, OSP Plant Maintenance Technicians I and II, and Residential Installers. Using your experience of Fiber to the Home (FTTH), Gigabit Passive Optical Network (GPON), 10 Gigabit Passive Optical Network (XGS) network construction, you will ensure the internal team and vendors understand the proper methods for installation, maintenance, and repair of network infrastructure as well as safety standards like Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). In this management role, you’ll also focus on resolving complex interactions between customers and team members, making sure everyone feels heard and process iteration occurs.

In this role, you’ll:

Field Operations Leadership:

• Lead and manage a team of technicians, overseeing all aspects of field operations including planning, scheduling, and coordinating construction, installation, repair, and maintenance activities.

• Foster team development by actively promoting best practices, identifying skill development opportunities, and creating personalized plans for individual growth.

Technical Expertise:

• Troubleshoot and resolve service issues across the network, from the central office to customer premises.

• Possess proficiency in various technical tasks like installing Ethernet jacks, making telecom space cross-connects, and handling radio installations, maintenance, and troubleshooting.

Customer Service:

• Navigate complex customer interactions with exceptional client service, professionalism, and thoroughness.

• Communicate effectively with internal colleagues and external customers.

• Cultivate relationships with property managers and building owners through advanced technical knowledge, effective communication, and collaboration.

Teamwork and Leadership:

• Execute operational processes and procedures with attention to detail.

• Foster a culture of continuous learning by collaborating with team members to achieve proficiency in troubleshooting complex issues affecting network connectivity and inside wiring.

Additional Responsibilities:

• Ability to work non-standard working hours, including nights, weekends, holidays, and varying shifts, and be willing to travel domestically up to 10% of the time.

At a minimum we'd like you to have:

• 5 years of experience in Fiber to the Home (FTTH)/ Gigabit Passive Optical Network (GPON)/ 10 Gigabit Passive Optical Network (XGS) network construction and/or large scale fiber network deployments.

• 5 years of experience managing relationships with contractors and suppliers.

• 3 years in a people manager position.

• Experience with physical layer components of networking infrastructure, including twisted pair copper cabling (Category 5 or greater), 66 blocks, 110 blocks, patch panels, fiber optic cabling, etc.

• Ability to lift/move up to 50lbs of equipment as required.

• Valid driver's license.

• Ability to pass a motor vehicle record check that meets company standards.

• Ability to work non-standard working hours as needed including nights, weekends, holidays, and differing work rotations/shifts as well as 10% domestic travel.

It's preferred if you have :

• 5 years of experience in building and operating fiber networks for business-to-business (B2B) and enterprise environments.

• Experience interfacing with local pole owners and utility companies, coordinating with city/local permitting offices, and subject matter expertise in outside plant Fiber to the Home (OSP FTTH) deployments with experience in service drop installations.

• Experience troubleshooting Ethernet network issues related to routers, switches and hubs.

• Experience with rack and stack work, assembling server stanchions, telemetry closet work (MPOE, DMARC, etc.), and patch panels.

• Ability to operate Google Workspace and Salesforce applications.

Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

• Work hand-in-hand with the Scout team to identify the right suppliers to build and supply parts & services, including participating in pre-souring audits to confirm acceptability of new suppliers.

• Establish sourcing strategy, business plan (long term conditions) for assigned commodities and product groups, lead the sourcing process up to and including contract award for Interior commodity purchasing to ensure the material cost and tooling targets are met or exceeded.

• Lead the sourcing strategy presentation in the multi level sourcing committee environment.

• Prepare and execute negotiated contractual documents and nomination agreements.

• Act as program manager during the pre-production phase, ensuring that all industrialization at suppliers achieve the project requirements in terms of timing, cost, and quality.

• Evaluate and apply technical changes to parts / services, ensuring that cost, quality and delivery objectives are met.

• Lead cross-functional evaluation of suppliers’ preparedness for mass-production, together with Scout Quality, Engineering, and Logistics teams.

• Manage supplier relationships and performance through key performance metrics.

• Support development phase, pre-production design & engineering changes, cost and tooling negotiations

• This role will be based out of the Scout Motors location in Novi, Michigan.

• This role requires 4 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

• 4+ years in purchasing environment with experience developing and executing procurement commodity strategies

• Proactivity, initiative and the ability to work across multiple workstreams

• A passion for creating something new

• Ability to find creative solutions to complex problems

• A collaborative approach - working as a team to achieve ambitious goals

• Previous experiences with interior parts, and production processes as plastic injection, compression molding, and wrapping are highly desirable

• Expertise in interior plastics such as PP, PC, PC-ABS, PE, TPO, GF and decorative materials such as fabrics, PVC, PU, leather is preferred qualification

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up.  This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation.  In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. jobs.title: Director of Business Development
jobs.description:
Kraus Hamdani Aerospace (KHA) is an aerospace company specializing in long-endurance unmanned aerial platforms for a wide variety of industries. KHA supports a number of customers to carry out missions involving aerial reconnaissance, survey, communication relay and communications provisioning. Endurance, enabled by effective design, is key to these applications and KHA aircraft utilize cutting-edge aircraft design together with on-board intelligence to deliver value for these customers.

Job Title: Director of Business Development
Department: Sales & Business Development
Location: Remote, United States
Employment: Full-Time

Position Summary

Kraus Hamdani Aerospace
U.S. Defense & Unmanned Systems

Employment: Full-Time
Location: United States | Significant travel required
Focus: U.S. DoW, Army Aviation, Special Operations, and Joint Force Programs

About Kraus Hamdani Aerospace

Kraus Hamdani Aerospace is redefining the future of unmanned aviation through persistent, autonomous, software-defined airborne infrastructure.

Our mission is simple: Save lives and connect the world.

Our flagship K1000ULE is a combat-proven, fully electric, long-endurance unmanned aircraft system designed to deliver persistent intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, communications, and multi-domain operational capabilities.

With growing deployments across the U.S. military and international defense partners, KHA is entering an exciting phase of expansion. We are seeking an exceptional business development leader who can help accelerate adoption of our technologies across the U.S. DoW.

The Opportunity

We are not looking for a traditional salesperson.

We are looking for a hunter, a closer, and a trusted member of the warfighter community. Someone who understands military operations from firsthand experience, speaks the language of the end user, and knows how to navigate the complex ecosystem of military requirements, acquisition, appropriations, and procurement.

The ideal candidate combines deep operational credibility with commercial instincts, an entrepreneurial mindset, and an extraordinary network across the U.S. defense community.

This person should be equally comfortable engaging a Chief Warrant Officer on the flight line, a program manager at PEO Aviation, a senior commander discussing operational capability gaps, or an acquisition executive evaluating procurement priorities.

We particularly value candidates with military aviation or UAS operational backgrounds, including Senior Enlisted Leaders (SELs), warrant officers, and other military leaders with trusted relationships across the defense community.

Above all, we want someone who has fire in the belly - someone who takes ownership, thrives on competition, creates opportunities rather than waiting for them, and is genuinely excited about getting transformational technology into the hands of warfighters.

Key Responsibilities

1. Drive Revenue and Capture New Business

• Own and execute business development strategies that translate into meaningful revenue growth and long-term program adoption.

• Identify, qualify, pursue, and win opportunities across Army, SOCOM, Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy, and joint operational commands.

• Develop a robust, actionable pipeline spanning immediate procurement opportunities, program-of-record pathways, and longer-term strategic pursuits.

• Convert operational demonstrations, field evaluations, and end-user advocacy into funded procurement opportunities.

• Personally drive high-value pursuits from initial customer engagement through capture, award, and follow-on expansion.

• Develop relationships and partnerships that position KHA for repeatable, scalable revenue rather than isolated one-off sales.

2. Leverage Deep Military Relationships

• Bring an established, trusted network across Army Aviation, UAS units, senior enlisted leaders, warrant officer communities, operational commands, and acquisition organizations.

• Build strong relationships with operational leaders, capability developers, program managers, requirements officers, and acquisition decision-makers.

• Understand the distinction between operational influence, requirements ownership, budget authority, and contracting authority.

• Engage directly with warfighters to identify capability gaps and translate those needs into viable acquisition opportunities.

• Build sustained champions across operational and institutional Army organizations.

3. Navigate Defense Acquisition and Procurement

• Demonstrate practical knowledge of the DoW acquisition ecosystem, including requirements generation, budgeting, contracting, and fielding.

• Understand the roles of PEO Aviation, PM UAS, Army Futures Command, Army requirements organizations, and relevant joint acquisition stakeholders.

• Navigate procurement mechanisms such as IDIQs, OTAs, rapid acquisition pathways, SBIR transitions, and traditional FAR-based contracts.

• Understand the PPBE process, POM cycles, congressional appropriations, and the distinction between RDT&E, procurement, and O&M funding.

• Identify funded requirements and understand how to align KHA capabilities with available and emerging budget opportunities.

• Help shape acquisition strategies that accelerate the transition from experimentation to operational procurement.

4. Translate Operational Requirements Into Solutions

• Possess a strong working understanding of Group 1-3 UAS, with particular depth in Group 2 systems, long-endurance ISR, and tactical unmanned aviation.

• Understand operational concepts including ISR, targeting support, electronic warfare, communications relay, contested logistics, and multi-domain operations.

• Communicate credibly about payload integration, endurance, range, tactical employment, command and control, and operational constraints.

• Understand the practical challenges of deploying, sustaining, and integrating UAS in contested environments.

• Work closely with KHA's engineering, product, and operations teams to ensure customer requirements inform capability development.

5. Build a Winning Market Strategy

• Identify emerging requirements, acquisition priorities, and competitive threats across the defense UAS market.

• Develop strategic account plans for priority military organizations and programs.

• Position KHA's differentiated capabilities against incumbent defense primes and emerging unmanned systems competitors.

• Support demonstrations, exercises, industry engagements, and operational evaluations that lead to procurement.

• Establish measurable business development objectives, capture milestones, and revenue forecasts.

• Represent KHA with professionalism, integrity, urgency, and conviction.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Military Background and Credibility

Highly desirable:

• Experienced Senior Enlisted Leaders (SELs), warrant officers, or other military leaders with significant UAS, military aviation, or operational expertise.

• Extensive experience in military aviation, unmanned systems operations, operational planning, capability development, or acquisition.

• Deep professional relationships with senior enlisted and other military leaders, especially in aviation, UAS, and operational communities.

• Familiarity with tactical and operational units, including combat aviation brigades, division-level formations, multidomain task forces, and special operations organizations.

• Firsthand understanding of how commanders and operators evaluate and adopt new technologies.

Prior military service is required for this position. Candidates must demonstrate operational credibility, relationships, and defense business development success.

Security Clearance

• Must possess an active U.S. government security clearance or be eligible to obtain and maintain one as required for the position.

Defense Acquisition Expertise

• Strong understanding of DoW procurement, military budgeting, requirements development, and acquisition processes.

• Demonstrated ability to identify funded opportunities and navigate the stakeholders required to achieve contract awards.

• Familiarity with Army PEOs, PMs, requirements organizations, and operational experimentation pathways.

• Understanding of defense industry competitive dynamics, contracting timelines, and government buying behavior.

Commercial Track Record

• Demonstrated success generating and closing defense contracts, expanding military accounts, or transitioning capabilities into programs.

• Ability to personally originate business opportunities rather than relying exclusively on established company pipelines.

• Strong capture management, strategic account development, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.

• Experience selling complex defense technologies with long and often unpredictable sales cycles.

• Ability to operate independently while maintaining disciplined pipeline management and accountability.

Personal Attributes

This is where we will be exceptionally selective.

We want someone who is:

• Relentlessly driven: Has genuine hunger to win and the energy to pursue difficult opportunities.

• A natural hunter: Creates opportunities, opens doors, and follows through until results are achieved.

• Operationally authentic: Earns respect because they understand the mission, not because they know the right buzzwords.

• Entrepreneurial: Thrives in a fast-growing company where initiative, resourcefulness, and ownership matter.

• Connected and trusted: Has meaningful relationships built on professional credibility, not simply a list of contacts.

• Strategic and tactical: Can discuss long-term acquisition strategy in the morning and work directly with operators in the field that afternoon.

• Accountable: Measures success through contracts, revenue, customer adoption, and operational impact.

• Mission-driven: Believes in providing warfighters with technology that improves mission effectiveness and saves lives.

• A team player: Works collaboratively with engineering, operations, executive leadership, and customers without ego.

Why Join KHA?

This is an opportunity to help shape the future of unmanned aviation at a company whose technology is already being deployed to support real-world missions.

Unlike traditional defense organizations, KHA combines proven operational capabilities with the agility, speed, and entrepreneurial culture of an emerging aerospace leader.

You will work directly with executive leadership, influence strategic growth priorities, and play a critical role in getting mission-essential technology into the hands of the people who need it most.

We believe in People, Purpose, and Prosperity for All.

We are looking for someone who shares that conviction and is ready to build something extraordinary.

If you understand the mission, know the market, have the relationships, and possess the drive to win, we want to talk.

jobs.title: Ramps Lead
jobs.description:
About the Role

Our client is a fast-growing global payments and payroll platform looking for a Ramps Lead based in the United States to own the infrastructure that moves money in and out of their platform.

Ramps are how money enters and leaves the platform: fiat to stablecoin on-ramps, stablecoin to fiat off-ramps, bank rails and the partner integrations that connect them. Ramps already run in production, and every payment on the platform crosses one. This role owns them end to end.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role, roughly 70% writing production code and 30% leading a small team of 1 to 2 engineers. You'll make the ramps more resilient, scale them with growing volume, and extend them with new rails and partners.

This role is best suited for a backend engineer with real banking experience who has already led engineers, enjoys owning problems end to end, and wants to move quickly in a fast-paced, AI-first startup environment.


Key Responsibilities

 - Ramps Ownership: Own the architecture and delivery of on-ramp and off-ramp infrastructure that moves funds between traditional finance and on-chain.

 - Backend Development: Build and maintain the Node.js and TypeScript services that orchestrate fiat and crypto settlement, partner APIs, reconciliation and ledgering.

 - Banking & Partner Integrations: Evaluate, integrate and manage banking, liquidity and ramp partners, including banks, banking-as-a-service providers, stablecoin issuers and payment processors.

 - Resilient Payment Processing: Build idempotent and retry-safe flows, reconciliation against partner and on-chain records, failover across providers, and clear recovery paths for stuck or failed transactions.

 - Compliance Partnership: Work with Compliance and Finance on transaction monitoring, AML, treasury and reconciliation requirements.

 - Monitoring & On-Call: Own observability for ramp flows, including the metrics, alerts and dashboards that catch stalled transactions and partner issues before customers do. You carry the pager for the systems you build.

 - Roadmap Execution: Partner with the Director of Product to turn ramps priorities into a sequenced technical plan, and bring engineering tradeoffs and risks into product decisions early.

 - Team Leadership: Lead and mentor a small team of engineers, review code and raise the bar for quality and security.

 - AI-First Engineering: Use AI tools like Claude daily to accelerate design, coding, testing, debugging and documentation, and help the team do the same.
   

Requirements

 - 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, with at least 2 years leading engineers or owning a technical domain.

 - Real banking integration experience: direct work with bank partners, banking-as-a-service providers or regulated money transmitters on settlement, ACH, wires and SEPA. Experience limited to payment processor APIs is not enough.

 - Strong grasp of ledgering, reconciliation, settlement windows, returns and reversals, and how funds actually move between institutions.

 - Experience with transaction monitoring, AML and KYC/KYB integrations.

 - Strong production experience with Node.js and TypeScript, including API design, background workers and event-driven systems.

 - Proven experience building and operating payment systems that handle real money, including on-call ownership and failure recovery.

 - Daily use of AI tools in your engineering workflow, with a clear point of view on how to use them well and safely.

 - Strong, confident communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Comfortable with SQL (MySQL or similar) and cloud infrastructure.

 - Based in and authorized to work in the United States, and able to pass background and credit checks.
   

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience or strong interest in crypto, especially Ethereum and EVM chains (Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, Optimism). On-chain skills can be learned on the job by a strong banking engineer.

 - Experience with Solidity, wallets, transaction signing or stablecoin settlement.

 - Google Cloud Platform experience (Cloud Run, BigQuery).

 - Background in treasury, liquidity management or FX.

 - Prior work at a payments, payroll, banking infrastructure or crypto company.
   

Compensation & Logistics

 - Location: Fully remote, United States only.

 - Compensation: 170,000 to 210,000 USD base salary per year, plus meaningful equity.

 - Benefits: Health, dental and vision coverage, 401(k) with a 3% company contribution, unlimited PTO, flexible schedule, and home office and learning stipend.
   

What Success Looks Like in the First 3 to 6 Months

 - Get up to speed quickly on the ramps architecture, partners and codebase, and start shipping code changes early.

 - Use AI tools to diagnose issues and build features faster.

 - Visibly increase the productivity and output of the ramps team.

 - Move the ramps roadmap forward in close partnership with the Director of Product.

 - Strengthen reliability across partners, with better monitoring, reconciliation and recovery for stuck or failed transactions.

 - Build strong working relationships with Compliance, Finance, Product and Engineering.
   
   

Company Overview
Our client is a global payments and payroll platform built for the way modern teams actually work, across borders, currencies and rails. Companies use it to pay full-time employees, contractors and freelancers anywhere in the world, in fiat or digital assets, with compliance, tax and identity infrastructure handled underneath.

Because the company moves money for real people, security and correctness are first-order concerns in everything it ships. The team is fully remote, with a bias toward written and async communication, small teams with high ownership, direct access to leadership and short feedback loops. AI is part of how they build: every engineer uses AI tools daily and keeps improving how they use them.

Ennoble Care’s clinicians go to the home of the patient, providing continuum of care for those with chronic conditions and limited mobility. Job Summary:

The role involves providing emotional and practical support to patients and their families during end-of-life care, ensuring they receive compassionate and personalized care.

Responsibilities:

• Conduct a psychosocial assessment as part of the comprehensive assessment within 5 days of admission to the hospice program. • Worker practice through formal education, attendance at workshops and conferences, active participation in professional and related organizational meetings, and/or individual research and reading.

jobs.title: Supply Planner
jobs.description:
The Supply Planner independently develops and manages an executable supply plan that balances demand, capacity, material availability, inventory, lead times, quality requirements, and customer priorities. The role converts demand into production, procurement, transfer, and replenishment actions while proactively managing constraints and supply risks. The Supply Planner owns planning performance for an assigned scope and serves as the primary planning contact for cross-functional stakeholders.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to capably perform each of the following essential duties:

• Develop and maintain short-, medium-, and long-term supply plans that balance demand, capacity, inventory, material availability, lead times, and quality-release requirements; communicate plans to stakeholders.
• Interpret MRP results and resolve shortages, excess inventory, overdue supply, rescheduling messages, and schedule disruptions.
• Maintain accurate production and supply orders, planning parameters, dates, quantities, lot sizes, safety stocks, and priorities in the ERP system.
• Develop production sequences, batch and campaign plans, and changeover assumptions that support realistic schedules.
• Set and communicate realistic supply, availability, and customer commitment dates based on manufacturing and quality milestones.
• Coordinate cross-functional recovery actions when material, labor, equipment, testing, storage, or planning-data constraints threaten the supply plan.
• Partner with Purchasing and suppliers to address shortages, lead-time risks, delivery performance, and recovery actions.
• Lead routine planning meetings and document decisions, owners, actions, and escalations.
• Provide supply, inventory, capacity, backlog, and risk inputs for SIOP reviews.
• Support product introductions, transfers, changes, discontinuations, and other product lifecycle events.
• Lead root-cause analysis, process standardization, and continuous-improvement activities for planning processes.

**ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE AND QUALIFICATIONS:**

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related field; or equivalent combination of education and professional experience
• Three to five years of relevant experience in supply planning, production planning, materials management, manufacturing, or inventory planning
• Working proficiency with an ERP/MRP platform (such as SAP, IFS, or comparable integrated system)
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookup formulas, and data visualization
• Strong knowledge of MRP, inventory management, capacity planning, lead times, lot sizing, safety stock, production-order management, and planning master data
• Demonstrated ability to analyze supply chain constraints, evaluate trade-offs, recommend corrective actions, and communicate realistic supply commitments

**DESIRED KNOWLEDGE AND QUALIFICATIONS:**

• Hands-on experience with SAP, IFS, or comparable integrated systems
• Experience with Tableau, Snowflake, or approved AI-enabled analytical tools
• Regulated-industry experience and SIOP (Sales and Operations Planning) participation
• APICS/ASCM certification (CSCP or equivalent supply chain credential)
• Knowledge of lean or Six Sigma methodologies

**BEHAVIORAL AND INTERPERSONAL COMPETENCIES:**

• Alignment with LGC's core values: Passion, Curiosity, Integrity, Brilliance, and Respect
• Ability to independently own priorities, decisions, transactions, and cross-functional communication for an assigned supply plan
• Sound judgment in resolving planning exceptions and escalating higher-impact issues
• Capability to build positive working relationships and secure clear commitments from stakeholders
• Clear communication of trade-offs, assumptions, recovery actions, and realistic dates
• Proficiency in managing multiple priorities and adapting to changing business needs
• Commitment to using data responsibly and reinforcing quality, safety, compliance, and data-integrity requirements

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist PNE-Central Operations, Casual Status Rotating Shifts
jobs.description:
The Clinical Pharmacist PNE reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Pharmacist PNE is responsible for identifying, preventing, and/or resolving medication related problems; for providing authoritative  information to other health care professionals, patients, and the public; and for assuring that the informational, clinical, and drug distribution components of pharmacy services function as an integrated system to provide patient centered care to the patients and staff of Northwestern Medicine.

The mission of the Department of Pharmacy is to deliver the safest, highest quality, most effective and efficient patient care while developing the best people, advancing research, and integrating pharmacy services to successfully coordinate care across the Northwestern Medicine enterprise.

The vision of the Department of Pharmacy is to be a recognized as a national leader in advancing the pharmacy enterprise through excellence, innovation, education and research.

Meets the professional exemption under FLSA; but works an irregular schedule.

Responsibilities:

• Interprets medication orders to ensure safety and proper use of medications and is alert to compatibilities, incompatibilities, medication duplication, medication allergies, and potential medication administration errors. Coordinates the solving of medication related problems between pharmacy, nursing, and prescribers, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment.
• Monitors medication therapy for significant drug-drug, drug-diet, or drug-laboratory test interactions. Intervenes in circumstances of significant interactions, therapeutic duplications, and other occasions where pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic expertise is warranted.
• Evaluates and documents that the medication(s) selected are appropriate for achieving the desired therapeutic outcome. Communicates potential problems and likely solutions to the prescriber.
• Acts as a consultant in the areas of pharmacokinetics and adverse reactions to physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals. Participates in all therapeutic drug monitoring or intervention programs; adjusting therapy as indicated by patient condition and laboratory results.
• Processes all medication order information into the Electronic Health Record to ensure accuracy of records regarding past, current and future dispensing and charging.
• Maintains a comprehensive pharmacy patient profile. The profile should include age, maturation, weight, allergies, diagnosis, estimated and actual pharmacokinetic parameters, and pertinent information which may affect medication therapy decisions.
• Oversees the packaging labeling, and distribution of medications for all patients and employees according to established policies, procedures, and guidelines. Monitors the use of scheduled medications on the nursing units and maintains controlled inventories of medication in the dispensing areas.
• Compounds and dispenses pharmaceuticals including sterile products, chemotherapy and parenteral nutrition products.
• Verifies medication orders before delivery to patient care areas and ensures accuracy and completeness. Resolves discrepancies as necessary.
• Reviews all laboratory data for appropriateness of medication use and recommends changes when needed. Including microbial culture and sensitivity data, toxicology, therapeutic drug monitoring, etc.
• Develops and presents orientation, education and training programs for medical, nursing, hospital and pharmacy staff, as well as assisting in the educating of pharmacy students, residents, and fellows.
• Educates patients and their families about specific medications.
• Responds to emergency situations to assist with medication management (e.g. response to cardiac arrests)
• Provides accurate and timely medication information and or teaching to healthcare professionals or patients.
• Maintains the hospital formulary and acts to limit medication usage to formulary items when appropriate
• Documents all clinical activities and interventions performed. Collects data, maintains logs, records and other documentation as required by the department
• Communicates professional knowledge effectively in both oral and written forms to patients and other health professionals.
• Participates in quality improvement and medication use review activities of the department.
• Organizes, prioritizes, and plans workload within given time constraints. Works cooperatively with fellow pharmacists to oversee and direct the activities of the work area, to assign work to technicians, and to assure that the established department objectives are accomplished
• Reviews restocking automated dispensing cabinets (ADC’s) throughout the hospital and resolves any problems.
• Ensures compliance with hazardous waste collection and disposal procedures.
• Maintains proficiency and expertise in area/s of practice through continuous professional development.
• All other job duties as assigned.

Required

• Active Clinical Pharmacist license in the state of Illinois (IDFPR)
• Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy Degree

Preferred

• Training and knowledge of specialty areas (neonatology, critical care, oncology, etc.)
• Completion of a pharmacy residency program or equivalent hospital pharmacy experience

jobs.title: Executive Assistant (Associate), OCEO
jobs.description:
Executive Assistant (Associate), OCEO

Acumen is seeking an Executive Assistant to provide exceptionally reliable, detail-oriented support to the CEO and the Office of the CEO (OCEO). This is more than an administrative role: it calls for strong judgment, discretion, and anticipation. Reliability and clear communication are central to the role. Acumen’s New York office operates on a hybrid schedule, with in-office work Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.

About Acumen

Acumen is a global force of entrepreneurs, investors, philanthropists, and social innovators working together to build a world based on dignity. We were founded by Jacqueline Novogratz on the radical idea that business, when cultivated with moral imagination, can break the cycle of poverty. We invest in transformational companies, sustainable markets, and prepare leaders with the tools they need to create a more just and inclusive future. Since 2001, we have scaled companies and shaped markets in some of the hardest-to-reach communities on the planet, impacting over half-a-billion lives. To learn more visit acumen.org.

About the Office of the CEO

The Office of the CEO (OCEO) enables Jacqueline Novogratz to engage effectively across Acumen and with external stakeholders. The team works in close partnership across executive strategy, engagement, operations, and administrative execution, with clear decision rights and shared visibility.

About the Role

The Executive Assistant carries out logistics, travel, and administrative support for Jacqueline Novogratz, who travels roughly 60 to 70 percent of the year. The role also provides in-person support in the New York office. It reports to the Manager, Executive Operations, who is the focal point for scheduling, and works closely with the Chief of Staff.

Accountabilities Include:

Logistics and in-person support

• Executes day-to-day scheduling across time zones at the Manager’s direction, and supports scheduling for the Chief of Staff as needed

• Supports high-volume communications and inbox management with discernment, helping prioritize, draft, and respond, and escalating to the Manager when needed

• Provides in-person support when Jacqueline is in the New York office, keeping her day on track, ensuring smooth transitions between meetings, and preparing her briefing binder

• Coordinates logistics for dinners, salons, and other events in partnership with the Manager

• Supports coordination with external organizations and initiatives Jacqueline is engaged with, as directed by the Manager

Travel

• Books Jacqueline’s travel once the Manager has confirmed trip details, researching options, handling routine changes, applying her preferences, and flagging constraints early

• Prepares travel packs with itineraries, meeting schedules, clearance materials, and relevant background, and secures visas, passport pages, and other documents well ahead of international trips

• Handles travel logistics for board trips in partnership with the Manager and the Chief of Staff

Relationship support and correspondence

• Supports the Manager on the outreach cadence and quarterly correspondence review, tracking follow-up and preparing inputs ahead of each review

• Supports the Manager on inbound and outbound correspondence through the CEO’s inbox

• Drafts follow-up correspondence in partnership with the Chief of Staff

Research and media monitoring

• Monitors the press and news on key contacts, flagging relevant coverage and escalating material developments to the OCEO team

• Conducts relationship-tracking research ahead of board trips and key meetings, and provides memo and research support

• Takes on additional assignments as needed, including operational support

Expenses, invoices, timesheets, and documents

• Prepares and tracks expense reports and processes invoices and expenses in accordance with Acumen’s Travel & Expense Policy

• Reviews and advises on expense reports for the CEO and her direct reports.

• Manages the CEO’s timesheets

• Coordinates with Talent, Legal, and Finance on contracts, signatures, approvals, and related documentation, and tracks signatures and information for CEO-related documents through to delivery

Briefings, meetings, and projects

• Helps prepare briefings and talking points

• Schedules and supports logistics for the standing meeting with Development & Partnerships and the regional focal points

• Supports the Chief of Staff and the Manager on special projects as needed

How the Role Operates

Reliability, accuracy, and clear communication are core expectations of this role, not extras.

• Proactive communication. Keeps the Manager continuously informed, and the Chief of Staff when working with her directly. Surfaces changes, conflicts, risks, and open questions early, without waiting to be asked.

• Responsiveness. Responds in a timely, consistent, and reliable manner, especially when working remotely. Is a clear communicator who makes it easy to see what is needed and by when.

• A consistent rhythm. Joins the weekly team sync with the Chief of Staff and the Manager, and the Monday look-ahead, so support is integrated rather than siloed.

• Attention to detail. Delivers expense reports, timesheets, documents, and correspondence that are accurate, complete, and ready without rework, in line with Acumen policies.

• Consistency. Delivers the same high standard every week, not just during busy periods, so the Manager and the Chief of Staff can rely on the work without checking it.

• Follow-through. Closes the loop on every request, tracks signatures and approvals through to completion, and flags anything delayed or unresolved before it becomes a problem.

• Sound judgment. Knows what needs escalation and brings it to the Manager early, with a recommendation where possible. Stays calm when plans change.

• Discretion. Handles confidential and sensitive information, including family, board, donor, financial, and personnel matters, with care.

• Clear handoffs. Provides written handoff notes before any time out of office, so coverage is seamless and the Manager knows what is in flight and what is needed.

Skills & Qualifications

• While a minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience is preferred, we welcome applications from more recent graduates who can demonstrate exceptional attention to detail, the ability to navigate ambiguity, and adaptability in a fast-paced, evolving environment

• Exceptional attention to detail and a track record of accurate, consistent, on-time work, with the ability to manage competing priorities and tight timelines

• Familiarity with and comfort with utilizing AI-powered tools

• Clear, proactive, and responsive communication, including when working remotely, with the habit of keeping colleagues informed without being asked

• Excellent verbal and written communication: crisp, clear, and kind, including the ability to draft warm correspondence

• Ability to anticipate needs, navigate ambiguity, and make sound decisions in real time, escalating to the Manager when needed and bringing a recommendation rather than just a problem

• Ability to plan and execute with the end goal in mind, to communicate the implications of changes, and to stay calm when plans change or go awry

• Excellent relationship management skills: the ability to understand the stakeholders, their needs, and their timelines, and to treat them with dignity

• Excellent project management skills: the ability to coordinate across stakeholders, manage competing priorities, and drive execution

• Working knowledge of expense reporting and timesheet processes, and experience coordinating contracts, approvals, and signatures across teams such as Talent, Legal, and Finance

• Demonstrated expertise of tools such as Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Gmail, and Zoom, and comfort with CRM systems such as Salesforce

• Strong research skills and the ability to design clear presentations

• Total discretion with confidential and sensitive information, including family, board, and donor matters

• Ability to collaborate across geographies, backgrounds, and levels of seniority, with self-reflection and deep alignment with Acumen’s mission and values, and curiosity about the ideas, people, and places at the intersection of capital, poverty, and climate

• Permanent authorization to work in the United States

• Must be based in New York City

Location

New York, USA

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $70,000 to $75,000 USD and is eligible for overtime, plus a performance-based bonus. This range represents the present low and high end of pay range for this role. Actual compensation will vary based on various factors including but not limited to experience. Acumen has equal pay, so pay is determined through comparison to a cohort of employees in the market at the same level of accountability.

#LI-ACU

jobs.title: Sales Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Sales Operations Manager | New York, NY

Who We Are:

Pixability is the leading AI-driven technology company empowering the world’s largest brands and their agencies to maximize the value of their advertising, organic and creator strategies on YouTube. Our platform, Pixability360, brings paid media, brand channels and creator partnerships together in one place, powered by proprietary data on YouTube channels and videos. Our AI agent, Pixie, curates and optimizes YouTube channels for advertising and creator campaigns. In 2026 we launched the industry’s first MCP-enabled AI agent for YouTube advertising and creator intelligence, so clients can bring Pixability’s YouTube data straight into their own AI workflows. Pixability works with top media agencies including Dentsu, OMC, Publicis, Havas and WPP Media, and brands such as Titleist, KIND, McDonald’s, CVS, Homes.com and Puma. For more information about Pixability, please visit www.pixability.com.

Our Award-Winning Culture:

Our team is the heart of our culture. We value innovation, collaboration and curiosity, and we have a passion for getting things done. We work to hire and develop the best people, and we foster a diverse and inclusive culture of open communication and transparency. We’re driven and hard-working, and we make time for fun along the way with happy hours, team outings and flexible paid time off. We’re proud to have won Best Contextual Targeting Offering at the 2025 Digiday Media Awards for our work with Molson Coors. Google selected us as a launch member of its YouTube Activation Program, we rank in the top 3% of Google Partners worldwide, and we’ve been listed on the Inc. 5000 for nine consecutive years. Earlier honors include Best Buy-Side Programmatic Platform at the Digiday Technology Awards and the Global Award for Video Innovation at the Google Premier Partner Awards.

The Team:

On the Sales team we love video, technology, our clients and keeping up with what's next across YouTube and CTV. Sales Operations sits inside Sales and keeps our sellers focused on selling: clean pipeline, a clear process, the right tools and reliable data for every decision. The role owns Salesforce and our sales dashboards, and works closely with Revenue Operations in Finance, which owns the company forecast model and compensation.

What You’ll Do

• Own sales execution operations for the Sales team, reporting to the Chief Revenue Officer and partnering day to day with Revenue Operations in Finance

• Own the KPI dashboards that serve as the single source of truth for conversion, velocity, win/loss and quota attainment, in Salesforce and Looker

• Keep pipeline clean by holding sellers to accurate stage, close date and amount, and run the weekly pipeline review

• Collect seller and manager forecast calls each week, submit the Sales forecast to Revenue Operations, and supply deal-level upside and risk for scenario planning

• Own Salesforce configuration, permissions and data governance, including fields, page layouts, validation rules, automation and user management

• Own the sales process: stage definitions, exit criteria and handoffs from Lead Gen to seller to Account Management, and build the supporting changes in Salesforce

• Build and maintain sales playbooks with sales leadership

• Analyze rep productivity, including activity, blockers and coaching inputs for managers, and build manager views and reports

• Recommend territory coverage and account assignments, and propose quota distribution across sellers and regions for Finance approval

• Serve as first line for seller questions on commission payouts and triage disputes, and give input on comp plan design

• Administer Claude, Showpad and Gong, train sellers and drive adoption; lead evaluation of seller productivity tools and define requirements for seller-facing workflows such as lead routing

• Track lead follow-up SLAs with Marketing and support upsell and cross-sell motions with Customer Success

• Bring field feedback into pricing, packaging and go-to-market discussions

• Own the Sales team's GTM AI tools: build and maintain the prompts, workflows and automations that help sellers research accounts, draft outreach and prepare for meetings, train the team to use them, and use AI to automate recurring reporting

What You Bring to the Party

• 4–7 years in sales operations, revenue operations or sales strategy, ideally in ad tech, media or B2B SaaS

• Hands-on Salesforce administration experience, including configuration, Flows, permissions, reports and dashboards (Salesforce Administrator certification preferred), plus experience with Gong, Google Suite, Looker or similar tools

• Comfortable running pipeline and forecast meetings with senior sellers and sales leaders

• Experience with territory planning, quota setting and incentive compensation processes

• Experience building dashboards in Salesforce and Looker or another BI tool, plus advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills

• Process-minded and organized, with clear written documentation

• Hands-on experience building with AI tools such as Claude, including prompts, workflows and automations that sales teams use every day

• Based in New York, NY

The pay range for this role is ($110,000 - $135,000 total compensation (base + Bonus) with potential bonus opportunity and equity. At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

At LinkedIn we believe that marketing is what accelerates business growth and that nearly all the levers of business growth are driven by marketing. Because of this, we are passionate about helping B2B marketers around the world and across industries to unlock growth for their companies and thrive professionally. We work with our customers to empower them to make more effective marketing and business decisions with insights leveraging one of the richest proprietary data sets in the world – LinkedIn’s unique economic graph.

At LinkedIn, we strive to help our employees find passion and purpose. Join us in advancing our vision to create economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce by helping organizations thrive and grow through marketing excellence. LinkedIn Marketing Solutions (LMS) Marketing Science & Technology teams is searching for a passionate and inspirational senior leader to for our regional NAMER team. This strategic business leader will join our team to advance commercially focused marketing analytics and customer insights advisory capabilities in region and beyond working closely with Marketing Science & Technology leaders across regions, as well as internal sales, marketing and other cross-functional partners.

Ideal leaders for this role will be adept at providing strategic direction to a team of marketing and analytics professionals who deliver world-class insights to customers to unlock value for their businesses and to help deliver more effective outcomes.  This regional leader will be responsible for working with their team to collectively drive incremental sales and deepen strategic relationships with LMS marketing and advertising clients.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Development

• Inspire and manage a high-performing team.
• Identify growth opportunities, build a leadership bench, and nurture future leaders.
• Foster a culture of diversity, inclusion, and belonging aligned with LinkedIn’s values.

Strategic Execution

• Lead the strategic execution of LMS Marketing Science & Technology roadmaps.
• Develop and scale programs, products, and tools that fuel LMS business growth and client outcomes.
• Drive alignment with commercial priorities across Sales, Product, and Marketing.

Measurement & Methodology

• Champion B2B measurement approaches and products.
• Push clients to adopt learning agendas that improve marketing effectiveness.

Client & Stakeholder Engagement

• Build and maintain relationships with executive-level marketers and C-suite leaders.
• Represent the Marketing Science & Technology team at senior client meetings and industry events.
• Drive strategic partnerships with key sales leadership and cross-functional teams.

Innovation & Enablement

• Pilot new methodologies and initiatives that shape B2B marketing’s future.
• Advance adoption of Marketing Science & Technology solutions through enablement and education.
• Collaborate with data engineering and tools teams to evolve data foundations.

Why Join Us?

• This is a unique opportunity to lead transformational change in the marketing industry. You’ll be at the forefront of innovation, working with world-class teams to make marketing measurable, data-driven, and impactful. If you’re passionate about leadership, strategy, and collaboration, we want to hear from you.

Basic Requirements

• 12+ years working in the marketing/advertising industry with working knowledge of quantitative marketing analytics & large data sets
• 6+ years of people management experience
• Bachelor’s degree in Math, Economics, Statistics, Engineering, or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

• Passion for developing high-performing teams and creating transformational career opportunities.
• A strategic thinker with excellent business judgment, strong solutions, and very strong analytical skills
• Expertise in marketing methods, advertising, marketing technology and marketing intelligence or business consulting – preferably in B2B.
• Demonstrated excellence in data analytics with experience managing analytical and quantitative teams.
• Expertise and knowledge of quantitative research, advanced analytics, predictive modelling techniques & marketing analytics methodologies.
• Ability to establish strong relationships with senior stakeholders and influence colleagues to effectively contribute to and lead cross-functional teams responsible for advancing strategic initiatives.
• Strong commercial and customer success orientation, with proven track record developing intelligence solutions and advisory capabilities aligned to commercial outcomes.
• Excellent communication, presentation skills and experience presenting to executive stakeholders and influencing senior leadership.

Suggested Skills

• Stakeholder Management
• Marketing Analytics
• Team management

jobs.title: MSL/Senior MSL Oncology, Ovarian (NYC & NJ)
jobs.description:
The Medical Science Liaison is a field based scientific expert that strategically supports the research and business objectives of a designated therapeutic area across the product life cycle for a specific geography/territory. The Medical Science Liaison is the primary communicator of Abbvie science within a specific geography with healthcare professionals. The Medical Science Liaison develops and maintains professional relationships with internal and external customers to provide comprehensive medical and scientific support to AbbVie initiatives in assigned therapeutic areas. The Medical Science Liaison is viewed as a peer scientific expert in a designated therapeutic area/product.

Responsibilities

• Identify, develop, and maintain professional relationships with thought leaders, academic centers, and researchers in assigned areas of therapeutic interest to ensure access to current medical and scientific information on the designated therapeutic/product area.
• Present scientific information and education relative to disease state, therapeutic landscape, and AbbVie products across the product lifecycle to healthcare professionals including physicians, academic institutions, researchers, and other health care professionals.
• Support research initiatives as requested by AbbVie R&D, Clinical Operations, and Medical Affairs Departments and physician-initiated projects including, but not limited to, site evaluation and identification, recruitment, investigator meetings, external expert identification, and external collaboration management.
• Prepares marketplace in new therapeutic areas of interest, which includes creating awareness and relationships for AbbVie in the Medical community.
• Creates, maintains, and collaborates in relationships with internal cross-functional partnerships, Works with in-field commercial teams, as appropriate, to develop and execute Account plans designed to support and meet shared business objectives. Serves as a scientific resource to commercial partners, as appropriate, to support activities.
• Serve as a medical/scientific resource to healthcare providers through answering unsolicited medical questions and addressing other clinically related medical information issues.
• Support and provide Conduct on-going training to medical affairs, field sales and other internal personnel as directed.
• Practices core capabilities in strategic segmentation, as well as optimal resource utilization.
• Responsible for compliance with applicable Corporate and Divisional Policies and Procedure, including accurate and timely documentation as it relates to HCP (Healthcare Professionals) interactions. Responsible for maintaining annual expenses within assigned budget parameters.

• Advanced degree required (i.e., Pharm D, MD/DO, PhD, APP (i.e.: Physician Associate or Nurse Practitioner) in a relevant scientific discipline. Doctorate strongly preferred in a health science or clinical discipline.
• Typically requires a minimum of 2+ years relevant experience.
• Must be able to identify, analyze, and translate specific territory and corporate needs to support internal and external customers and achieve business and clinical objectives.
• Proficiency in Excel, Word, Power Point, and other software skills; Excellent written/verbal communication skills.
• Strong interpersonal skills, presentation, and teaching skills; Ability to work independently and in a team structure; Ability to adjust effectively to work within new structures, processes, requirements, or cultures; Strong planning and organizational skills; team and leadership skills.
• An essential requirement of the position is to meet health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to enter facilities and organizations in your assigned territory. These HCIR credentialing requirements may include, but are not limited to, background checks, drug screens, and proof of immunization/vaccination for various diseases.
• Ability to learn and convey clinical and non-clinical technical information effectively.
• Ability to engage the audience and help them understand and retain information.
• Must be willing to travel up to 75% of the time.

The candidate must live in the territory or willing to self-relocate within the territory which includes Jersey City, NJ, New York, NY
