jobs.title: H&M Sales Advisor - Miracle Mile
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Sales Advisor, you'll be responsible for providing excellent customer service, welcoming & guiding customers through your store to actively sell our products and providing customers with support & guidance. You'll use your fashion and product knowledge to provide our customers with all the relevant information they need for the best experience. You'll also work on garment refill & care, presentation and contribute to a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house, working closely with the rest of your store team to deliver an excellent customer experience.

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Customer Sales & Profit

• Provide excellent customer service: welcoming & guiding customers through the store & OMNI experience where available, supporting them with direct customer service
• Willingness to engage and have conversations with customers to provide excellent service
• Guide customers through our fashion trends, stories & products in all areas of the store
• Ability to effectively promote and sell our products to customers
• Actively promote our Customer Loyalty App (Hello Member) & in-store sustainability initiatives
• Representing yourself and the H&M brand positively during all customer interactions
• Support with commercial or operational actions to reach sales targets with store management team

General Information

Fashion & Trend Awareness

• Keep up-to-date with fashion scene, trends, tendencies, styles, brands, products, competitors, and relevant influencers, etc.
• Use your product & fashion knowledge to share relevant information to customers

Team & Development

• Retain and share your service, fashion and store operations knowledge and skills with colleagues
• Follow all procedures, routines, and legal requirements in all areas of the store
• Give & receive feedback with your colleagues to learn, develop & support each other
• Participate in relevant available Onboarding, introduction processes & trainings and courses relevant for your role & future development

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

• Complete full garment cycle from unpacking and refill to steaming and ensure good garment care
• Operate fitting room and checkout areas according to best practice & processes
• Contribute to a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house (including stockrooms)
• Support with garment presentation, execution and maintain attractive merchandise displays, clear trends & stories according to visual & commercial guidelines
• Ensure good stock levels with replenishment routines on sales floor
• Upkeep & follow best practice for any in-store OMNI Services & in-store tech services/tools, etc (Instore Care App, Click & Collect, Smart Store etc)
• Support with opening and closing of the store
• Following all H&S guidelines and legal requirements applicable to role and responsibilities

Who You Are

• As a Sales Advisor, you'll be passionate about fashion and everything we create in-store.
• Motivated by giving customers a great experience.
• You should also be communicative, creative and curious, motivated, flexible, decisive, and action-oriented.
• You should also enjoy working in a collaborative and dynamic environment.
• You have sales experience working in a dynamic and collaborative environment that you can apply to your role
• Experience working with customer service in fashion, retail or other service-related industries

Why You'll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years
• You'll have access to our Colleague Resource Groups (CRGs) to find community and networking opportunities among colleagues
• We are an inclusive company where you're encouraged to be yourself at work
• You will have access to a large global talent community, where career growth and aspirations have no limits
• We believe in supporting your overall wellbeing and offer comprehensive benefits inclusive of health insurance, wellness and family support programs, company match retirement plan, paid leave programs, and paid time off, including a community day to serve your local community
• You'll be able to express your personal style with our employee discount at H&M, & Other Stories, and COS

Job Status: Hourly, Non-Exempt

EEOC Code: SLS

Compensation: Sales Associates Pay Rate $14.00 per hour**

*This job posting highlights the most critical responsibilities and requirements of the job and is not all-inclusive. There may be additional duties, and responsibilities assigned for this job at the company's discretion.

**H&M, in good faith, has assessed this posted range of compensation as the accurate range for this role and location at the time of this posting. H&M may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on candidate qualifications. This range may be modified in the future.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at https://hm.ethicspoint.com, and use Ask a Question.

Benefits:

We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET, Afound. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here.

In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries.

Inclusion & Diversity:

H&M is a part of H&M Group. At H&M Group, we’re determined to create and maintain inclusive, diverse and equitable workplaces throughout our organization. Our teams should consist of a variety of people that share and combine their knowledge, experience and ideas. Having a diverse workforce leads to a positive impact on how we address challenges, on what we perceive possible and on how we choose to relate to our colleagues and customers all over the world. Hence, all diversity dimensions are considered in our recruitment process.

We strive to have a fair and equal process and therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter in your application as they often contain information that easily can trigger unintentional biases.

Company Description:

H&M is a fashion brand that offers the latest styles and inspiration, from fashion pieces and unique designer collaborations to affordable wardrobe essentials. Our business idea is fashion & quality at the best price in a sustainable way. Learn more about H&M here.

H&M Fashion USA, Inc. – Maki Assessment Tool:

We use an online assessment tool called Maki for skills-based selection of applicants for sales advisor positions within some of our stores. Maki is not an automated decision-making tool. Rather, it is a tool that uses an AI-created avatar to present to you a set of multiple-choice questions. These questions are prepared by the H&M hiring team to assess candidates’ ability to perform the duties of the position for which they are applying. The assessment calculates your total score based on predefined point values provided by our H&M team. The hiring team will review your whole application, including your assessment score, to decide whether to advance each candidate to the next stage. Doing the assessment is optional. If you choose to complete the assessment, your score will be one factor that the hiring team considers.

If you have any difficulties or concerns with the online assessment method, you can request an alternative method of assessment by contacting recruitment_support@hm.com. Choosing an alternative method will not affect your chances of being considered for the position, nor does any assessment method provide an advantage or disadvantage in the selection process. You will have the opportunity to provide optional feedback immediately after the assessment and you may always ask questions.

When you take the assessment, we collect your responses and use this information to evaluate your suitability for the role to which you have applied. The answers are saved in your applicant profile. We do not sell the information captured in the questionnaire and do not use any personal information to train any AI models. Our applicant tracking system provider has access to this information but is contractually prohibited from using it for any other purpose.

During this process, we may collect information from you through cookies, with your consent. This may include details such as your electronic network activity information (IP address, timestamps, and device identifiers). This information is accessible to our hiring team but is otherwise kept confidential. For more information, please refer to our Cookie Notice.

We retain this information for 3 years in your applicant file and use it as set forth in our Applicant Privacy Notice. For more information on how your personal data is processed by us, please refer to our Applicant Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Principal Scientist I - Chemistry
jobs.description:
We are seeking an accomplished computational engineer to lead the Cross-Functional Modeling Forum (CMF) and the Computational Assisted Process Engineering (CAPE) group, and to coordinate AI activities in a broader cross-functional context. This is a three-part leadership role that combines direct people leadership of a small, specialized, and highly motivated engineering team, enterprise-wide technical stewardship of AbbVie’s process modeling and simulation capability, and coordination of AI activities across the Small Molecule CMC organization. The successful candidate will set and communicate the computational engineering strategy for the function, translate that strategy into a prioritized capability roadmap, and hold accountability for the credibility, adoption, and business impact of the models the organization relies upon.

The ideal candidate is a mechanical engineer by training with deep competence in computational engineering and several years of hands-on, industrially relevant experience in multi-physics simulation, complemented by initial experience leading a small team of engineers who themselves bring strong modeling expertise. Acting effectively as a principal investigator, the candidate will generate original technical ideas and development strategies, serve as the accountable engineering leader for complex multidisciplinary challenges, and make timely, well-reasoned recommendations when the evidence base is incomplete – clearly communicating assumptions, trade-offs, risks, and mitigations. The candidate is expected to be recognized, or to become recognized, as a company-wide authority in computational process engineering, to provide decisive consultation across multiple programs, and to represent Process Engineering at consequential program and portfolio milestones.

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead the Cross-Functional Modeling Forum (CMF): set the agenda, convene modeling practitioners from R&D, Operations, and partner functions, and establish the governance, review cycles, decision rights, and model credibility standards that keep the organization’s computational practices effective, current, and aligned with business strategy.

• Lead the Computational Assisted Process Engineering (CAPE) group: directly supervise, mentor, and develop a team of modeling engineers; evaluate individual performance and own accountability for the effective performance of the team; sponsor emerging leaders, design meaningful development assignments, and recommend resource allocations.

• Coordinate AI activities across the entire Small Molecule (SM) CMC organization: drive best-practice sharing and AI tool management, and guide, train, and motivate colleagues in the effective use of AI.

• Set and communicate the computational process engineering strategy across drug-development programs and major capabilities, aligning technical priorities, resource recommendations, and risk decisions with program and portfolio needs.

• Own the integrated computational engineering strategy from laboratory and modeling understanding through scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing readiness; define critical uncertainties, scale-up strategy, and manufacturing-readiness criteria, and direct the generation of data required to test key hypotheses.

• Function as a principal investigator: independently conceive, execute, and communicate novel multi-disciplinary modeling and development strategies that achieve project and area goals, while contributing scientific insight to multiple other projects.

• Direct the development, qualification, and deployment of multi-physics and mechanistic models – including CFD, discrete element and particle-based methods, structural, thermal, and fluid-structure interaction analysis, transport phenomena, reaction and crystallization kinetics, and reduced-order or hybrid digital twins – to address equipment design, process design space definition, scale-up, and manufacturing challenges.

• Anticipate future program and portfolio challenges and establish new engineering strategies, technical proposals, and capability investments that address emerging scientific, regulatory, and manufacturing needs; recommend build, buy, partner, or stop decisions for modeling tools, platforms, and workstreams.

• Serve as the accountable engineering leader for complex, multidisciplinary technical issues; establish decision criteria, lead the resolution of unprecedented problems, and provide decisive consultation to multiple programs and partner functions.

• Champion creative, ‘out of the box’ thinking and new technologies – including advanced simulation methods, automation, surrogate and machine-learning-assisted modeling, high-performance and cloud computing, and modern data and software engineering practices – and move them from demonstration into routine, governed program use.

• Establish and sustain verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification practices so that model-based conclusions are defensible internally and in regulatory interactions; lead or review the engineering justification supporting CMC regulatory content.

• Build durable internal and external networks that accelerate decisions, mobilize the right expertise, and strengthen the influence of Process Engineering; convene technical forums and establish strategic external relationships with academic groups, software vendors, and consortia.

• Create a sustained, externally visible body of scientific work: act as senior or corresponding author of publications, primary inventor of patents, invited speaker at leading scientific conferences, and lead author of major technical or regulatory documents and standards.

• Champion a safe, compliant, inclusive, and high-learning culture; set clear expectations, reinforce constructive challenge, and convert lessons learned from programs, campaigns, and audits into sustainable systems and practices.

• Shape Process Engineering and Center of Excellence strategy through long-range capability planning, talent priorities, resource recommendations, and cross-functional operating models.

• Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, GxP compliance, and animal care where applicable.

Qualifications:

• BS or equivalent education and extensive, Typically, 14+ years of experience; MS or equivalent education with typically 12+ years of experience; PhD with typically 6+ years of experience in area or scientific area of discipline. Demonstrated depth in computational engineering, with several years of applied, industrially relevant experience in multi-physics simulation and a proven record of translating simulation results into design, process, or manufacturing decisions.

• Demonstrated experience leading a small team of engineers with strong modeling competence, including delegation of meaningful ownership, technical coaching, performance feedback, and accountability for team deliverables.

• Proven command of engineering fundamentals – fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, solid mechanics, thermodynamics, mixing, and reaction engineering – combined with the numerical methods, meshing, solver, and convergence judgment required to produce trustworthy results.

• Proficiency with leading commercial and open-source simulation environments (e.g., ANSYS Fluent or Mechanical, COMSOL Multiphysics, STAR-CCM+, Abaqus, OpenFOAM) and with scientific programming and data workflows in Python, MATLAB, or an equivalent ecosystem.

• Demonstrated ability to solve difficult technical problems, champion new technologies, and establish new capabilities that achieve project and organizational goals.

• Demonstrated scientific and organizational leadership, with the influence and credibility to lead a cross-functional forum, align stakeholders with competing priorities, and drive consensus on methods, standards, and investment.

• Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to translate complex computational concepts into clear, actionable recommendations for technical experts, cross-functional partners, and senior leadership.

Preferred:

• Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another regulated industry, including exposure to GxP compliance, technology transfer, and CMC regulatory content.

• Experience applying computational methods to pharmaceutical unit operations such as mixing and blending, crystallization, filtration and drying, lyophilization, granulation, tableting, spray drying, sterile and aseptic processing, single-use systems, or fill-finish.

• Experience with discrete element modeling (DEM), population balance modeling, multiphase and free-surface flows, non-Newtonian rheology, and coupled CFD-DEM or fluid-structure interaction approaches.

• Experience with mechanistic process modeling, flowsheet simulation, digital twins, and model-based design space definition in support of Quality by Design.

• Familiarity with molecular modeling or molecular dynamics and an understanding of how molecular-scale insight can be coupled to continuum-scale process models.

• Experience with model verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, surrogate modeling, reduced-order modeling, and optimization under uncertainty.

• Experience with machine learning and data-driven or hybrid modeling approaches applied to engineering and process data.

• Experience with high-performance, cluster, or cloud computing environments and with software engineering practices such as version control, automated testing, containerization, and reproducible workflows.

• Experience with process analytical technology (PAT), design of experiments, and statistical tools, and with integrating measurement and modeling into a single evidence base.

• Familiarity with the operation, design, and qualification of chemical, biochemical, and drug product process equipment and systems, and with pilot-plant and commercial scale-up activities.

• Experience establishing or governing a modeling community of practice, center of excellence, or equivalent cross-functional capability.

• Record of peer-reviewed publications, patents, invited presentations, or leadership roles in professional and standards-setting organizations.

Key Leadership Competencies:

• Sets a compelling technical vision and translates it into strategy, governance, and a prioritized capability roadmap that the organization can execute.

• Comfortable with multi-disciplinary interactions. Builds strong relationships with peers and cross-functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.

• Develops talent deliberately: delegates meaningful ownership, coaches emerging leaders, gives candid feedback, and is accountable for the performance and growth of the team.

• Decides with incomplete information, makes assumptions and trade-offs explicit, and takes clear accountability for recommendations and outcomes.

• Learns fast, grasps the ‘essence’, and can change course quickly where indicated.

• Raises the bar and is never satisfied with the status quo.

• Creates a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement.

• Embraces the ideas of others, nurtures innovation and enables innovation to reality.

• Influences without authority across functions and levels, and represents Process Engineering credibly with senior leadership and external partners.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer (Contract)
jobs.description:
The Motley Fool is looking for a Senior Product Designer to guide and elevate the user experience for our membership products and websites.

This is an opportunity for a highly creative, ideas-driven designer who thrives at the intersection of product strategy, design, and technology. A strong background in fintech, financial services, or investing products is essential, along with a deep understanding of the needs and behaviors of investors.

You'll work closely with product managers, engineering leads, and executive stakeholders to envision what's possible, create new products and experiences from the ground up, and reimagine existing systems. We're looking for someone who brings curiosity, thoughtful ideas, and a strong design perspective while remaining open to collaboration, feedback, and different points of view. The ideal candidate can influence strategic decisions, build trust across teams, and translate ambitious concepts into intuitive, scalable experiences.

You'll work within an empowered product team, ensuring customer value, business viability, and technical feasibility are aligned with world-class UX/UI design.

This is a 100% remote contract position. We expect the work to take roughly 40 hours per week.

About The Motley Fool

The Motley Fool is a purpose-driven financial services company on a mission to make the world smarter, happier, and richer. For 30 years we’ve been helping people make better investment decisions through transparency, education, and Foolish fun. We’re a fast-moving, collaborative team that values high-quality work, curiosity, and initiative. We care deeply about what we do, and we’re driven by the impact our work has on real people’s financial futures.

As a Senior Product Designer, you'll be part of a cross-functional group that leverages modern tools and emerging technologies to build intuitive, engaging, and scalable experiences for our users.

What would you do in this role?

• Define and evolve the design vision for our premium membership and Fool.com, aligning customer needs with business objectives and technical capabilities.

• Own the member experience. UX is key: create simple, outstanding experiences with a clear eye for detail and a strong taste for aesthetic design, starting with our premium membership.

• Lead the design of new greenfield products that help the world get smarter, happier, and richer, from first concept to launch.

• Build and own our design system and component library as the foundation of how we work. Make it easy for product managers and engineers to build and ship fast without waiting for custom design on every feature.

• Work AI-native: use AI tools and agents across research, prototyping, and design-to-code, and create the guidelines, components, and workflows that let our product managers, engineers, and their agents produce on-brand, accessible experiences on their own.

• Partner with executive stakeholders, product managers, and engineering leads to generate ideas, influence product direction, and build alignment around strategic priorities.

• Translate customer insights and complex financial concepts into intuitive, accessible experiences through research, rapid prototyping, and usability testing. Focus your hands-on design time on new concepts and the moments that matter most.

• Use analytics, A/B testing, and user feedback to evaluate design decisions and continuously improve experiences.

• Champion design best practices and accessibility while collaborating across teams and mentoring other designers.

What do you need to apply?

• 5+ years of product or UX design experience, leading consumer-facing web or mobile products.

• Significant experience and passion for designing digital products in fintech, financial services, investing, or related industries, with a strong understanding of investor needs and financial products.

• Experience and passion for designing AI-powered products, intelligent interfaces, or AI-enabled design systems.

• Ability to translate complex financial information and data into intuitive, engaging, and trustworthy customer experiences.

• A highly creative, ideas-driven mindset with experience developing new products and redesigning or modernizing established platforms.

• Experience partnering with executive stakeholders and influencing product strategy through strong communication, thoughtful ideas, and a collaborative, low-ego approach.

• Expert proficiency in Figma, plus proven expertise in keeping designs in sync with Claude and our code base, so that designs, design system components, and the shipped experience stay consistent.

• Strong knowledge of responsive design, information architecture, visual hierarchy, and scalable design systems.

• Hands-on with modern front-end frameworks such as Next.js, React, or Vue.js, and a working knowledge of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. You create small pull requests yourself for design changes, using AI coding tools and agents to do so.

• Experience with user research, usability testing, and data-informed design decisions.

Compensation:

Below is our target compensation range. While we are budget conscious, we’re also eager to find the right person for this role, so if your target is outside of this range, please don’t hesitate to apply and we’d be happy to have a conversation.

Hourly Pay Range

$100—$125 USD

By applying on this site, you acknowledge that The Motley Fool will be collecting the personal data you provide for our recruiting purposes. Please see our Applicant Privacy Notice for additional information about how we process, transfer, and store your data, including where that data is stored, and about any additional privacy rights you may have based on your jurisdiction.

jobs.title: Legal Expert Pleno - Célula de Peças · Jus IA
jobs.description:
Você deveria fazer parte do Jusbrasil

Transformar o sistema de Justiça com tecnologia não é trivial. Estamos construindo uma inteligência artificial dentro de casa: o Jus IA tem 43% menos alucinações que IAs generalistas. Essa é a prova concreta de que aqui tecnologia não é discurso, e sustenta a nossa missão: elevar a justiça.

Lidamos com mais de 7 bilhões de documentos jurídicos e mais de 1.400 fontes de dados oficiais. É desafio de escala e precisão que poucas empresas no país enfrentam.

Somos 670 pessoas jusbrasileiras, quase metade em engenharia e produto, espalhadas por mais de 125 cidades no Brasil e fora. O modelo é remoto: você escolhe onde viver, a vaga não muda.

Aqui, quem chama pra si o problema sem dono e entrega algo acima do esperado cresce rápido. Quem prefere o caminho óbvio, não.

Conheça nosso impacto

• site jurídico nº1 do mundo em número de acessos

• mais de 20 milhões de usuários por mês

• mais de 7 bilhões de documentos jurídicos de interesse público

• mais de 80% dos advogados brasileiros cadastrados

• 670 pessoas jusbrasileiras, quase metade em tecnologia e produto

• presença em mais de 125 cidades no Brasil e fora

• modelo remoto: liberdade de escolher onde viver, sem perder a vaga certa

Sobre a vaga

O Jus IA é o assistente jurídico do Jusbrasil. A nossa aposta é que ele vire o lugar onde a advocacia conduz um processo judicial do começo ao fim: da estratégia e da pesquisa de jurisprudência, doutrina e legislação até a peça pronta para protocolo.

A célula de Peças é onde o conhecimento jurídico vira produto. É aqui que a gente define o que é uma boa peça, como o Jus IA chega nela e como mede se chegou. Estamos buscando uma pessoa Legal Expert Pleno para ser a terceira expert da célula e dar sustentação jurídica a duas frentes: evolução do produto e avaliação de qualidade. Tem muita mão na massa, e o que a gente espera de volta é leitura crítica, não só a tarefa feita.

Contexto do time e do negócio

Você vai trabalhar numa célula com poucas pessoas experts e muitos engenheiros, ao lado de produto e design, num ambiente remoto e assíncrono. Usamos IA de verdade no dia a dia: as experts da célula constroem avaliações automáticas, trabalham com Claude Code e chegam a subir mudanças no código, mesmo sem ser engenheiras. Ninguém espera que você chegue sabendo isso tudo, mas espera que você tenha curiosidade para aprender rápido.

O que você vai fazer

• Montar gabaritos que servem de referência para o que é uma boa peça.

• Analisar conversas reais de usuários com o Jus IA (as threads) para avaliar a qualidade das respostas e das peças geradas.

• Apoiar a criação e a calibração de judges, modelos de IA que avaliam respostas, e a definição dos critérios de qualidade.

• Fazer análises estruturadas em volume, encontrar padrões e transformar isso em aprendizado para o produto.

• Questionar premissas, apontar inconsistências e levar propostas para produto e engenharia.

• Usar IA para ganhar escala no seu trabalho, sem terceirizar a sua análise.

Requisitos obrigatórios

Hard Skills

• Formação em Direito

• Uso frequente de IA no trabalho, de forma crítica: você valida, discorda e sabe dizer onde ela erra.

• Capacidade analítica: você enxerga padrões em volume e transforma isso em aprendizado.

Soft Skills

• Senso crítico: você questiona premissas e aponta inconsistências, em vez de executar no automático.

• Autonomia: já tocou frentes sozinha a partir de um direcional geral.

• Disposição real para trabalho operacional e repetitivo.

• Curiosidade e comunicação ativa: você vai atrás, pergunta e avisa quando algo não ficou claro.

Diferenciais (não eliminatórios)

• Experiência redigindo, revisando ou analisando peças processuais.

• Contato com produto, tecnologia ou IA, como anotação de dados ou avaliação de IA jurídica.

• Pesquisa empírica em Direito.

Etapas do processo

• Conversa com People Etapa técnica com a liderança: inclui um desafio prático de uso de IA no trabalho jurídico. Conversa final com o time.

jobs.title: Afterschool & Summer Food Service Specialist
jobs.description:
Career Opportunity: Afterschool & Summer Food Service Specialist with Children’s Hunger Alliance in Cincinnati, OH

Frequent local and regional daily travel to partner sites is required.

Are you passionate about helping children access nutritious meals through afterschool and summer programs? Do you enjoy working in the community, supporting partner sites, and ensuring programs operate effectively and in compliance? If so, this is the opportunity for you.

Children’s Hunger Alliance (CHA) is seeking an Afterschool & Summer Food Service Specialist to coordinate the application, onboarding, training, and ongoing compliance monitoring for partner sites participating in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) Afterschool At-Risk (ASAR) and Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) across Southwest Ohio. This role also supports local outreach initiatives to expand program reach and establish new community partnerships.

As the Afterschool & Summer Food Service Specialist, you will:

• Coordinate the annual site application process and food order launches for regional afterschool and summer program partners.

• Conduct daily field visits to monitor site operations and ensure compliance with USDA, state, and agency regulations for ASAR and SFSP.

• Provide hands-on support, retraining, corrective action management, and review resolutions for sites facing compliance challenges.

• Facilitate annual regulatory and operational training for partner site staff, including program rules, administrative procedures, and required software platforms.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for participating sites, providing responsive customer service, guidance, and daily administrative support.

• Review and adjust daily food orders based on student attendance and participation trends to help minimize waste.

• Build and sustain strategic partnerships with local community organizations, faith-based groups, and program stakeholders.

• Research, identify, and recruit prospective partner sites, guiding them through the onboarding process for ASAR and SFSP.

• Partner with the Claims Services Team and internal departments to support accurate recordkeeping, efficient food delivery workflows, and seamless service execution.

• Participate in team, regional, and statewide meetings; assist with statewide meal donation requests and distribution logistics; and complete other duties as assigned.

Requirements:

• Associate’s Degree in Nutrition, Public Health, Youth Development, Early Childhood Education, Communications, Social Work, or a related field; equivalent practical experience may also be considered.

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, with advanced working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.

• Demonstrated ability to interpret, apply, and maintain compliance with federal, state, and organizational guidelines.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including confidence speaking and presenting to groups.

• Excellent time management, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Collaborative, self-motivated, and committed to the agency’s mission.

• Hybrid office environment paired with extensive field work.

• Must have Valid Driver’s License and Auto Insurance

• Required travel up to 60% of the time

We Offer:

• Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance options

• Pre-tax savings options including FSA and HSA (with employer contributions)

• Employer-provided life insurance and long-term disability coverage

• 401(k) with Safe Harbor contribution and employer match

• Generous PTO starting at 19 days, plus 11 paid holidays

• Paid parental leave and additional leave options (bereavement, jury duty, etc.)

• Tuition and continuing education reimbursement

• Employee Assistance Program and wellness initiatives

• Mileage reimbursement and free parking

• Eligibility for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF)

• Optional benefits including supplemental life, disability, legal, and identity protection plans

• Flexible schedule

Founded in 1970, Children’s Hunger Alliance is a statewide nonprofit dedicated to ending childhood hunger. CHA partners with childcare providers, afterschool and summer programs, and schools across Ohio to increase access to healthy meals and nutrition education, supporting the long-term health of children.

Learn More:

https://childrenshungeralliance.org/

If you are ready for a new challenge, apply online today!

jobs.title: Customer Experience Coordinator (Relief) - San Jose, CA
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Customer Experience Coordinator, your job is to define the customer’s experience through service, focus, and participation—so, you are passionate about perfecting the experience before, during, and after their time at VEG. Outgoing and personable, with each customer, you conduct yourself professionally in both demeanor and presence. You find ways to say yes and put patient and customer experience above all else. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to grow where you want to go, building valuable experience and paving the way for your career to take unexpected and rewarding directions.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Greet every customer with warmth and urgency, whether in person, over the phone, or online

• Oversee all customer communications (calls, emails, texts), record details accurately, and route urgent medical calls to a doctor quickly

• Deliver personalized, memorable experiences—always looking for creative ways to say “yes” to customer needs

• Listen with empathy, resolve concerns quickly, and anticipate issues before they escalate

• Keep nursing team and doctors updated on customer needs for a seamless care experience.

• Provide confidential, compassionate guidance on financial options and end-of-life decisions

• Process payments accurately while protecting personal and financial information

• Follow up with customers after visits to check on their pet’s care and strengthen relationships

• Celebrate and capture special moments (with permission), creating lasting connections between customers, their pets, and the hospital

WHAT YOU NEED

• 2+ years of experience in a customer service role

• Advanced knowledge in computer programs and practice management software

• Highly organized, with strong attention to detail

• A strong communicator; able to interact positively with anyone and everyone

• A strong multitasker, able to thrive amid chaos

• High emotional intelligence, able to read a room and plan and act accordingly

• Adaptable and amenable in high stakes environments

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation: pay range is $20-$30 and based on experience, including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling

• Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave, up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

jobs.title: Army Readiness and Environmental Solutions (ARES) Support Specialist
jobs.description:
Seneca Global Services, LLC is part of the Seneca Nation Group (SNG) portfolio of companies. SNG is Seneca Holdings’ federal government contracting business that meets mission-critical needs of federal civilian, defense, and intelligence community customers. Our portfolio comprises multiple subsidiaries that participate in the Small Business Administration 8(a) program. To learn more about SNG, visit the website and follow us on LinkedIn.

At Seneca, our team of talented individuals is what makes us successful. To support our team, we provide a balanced mix of benefits and programs. Your total rewards package includes competitive pay, benefits, and perks, flexible work-life balance, professional development opportunities, and performance and recognition programs.  We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability, voluntary benefit programs (critical illness, hospital, and accident), health savings and flexible spending accounts, and retirement 401K plan. One of our fundamental principles at Seneca Holdings is to offer competitive health and welfare benefits to our team members, providing coverage and care for you and your family. Full-time employees working at least 30 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in our benefits and paid leave programs.  We pride ourselves on our collaborative work environment and culture, which embraces our mission of providing financial and non-financial benefits back to the members of the Seneca Nation.

Seneca Global Services, LLC is seeking a full-time ARES Support Specialist to provide program management, requirements coordination, project tracking, technology-transition support, and strategic communications for the Army Readiness and Environmental Solutions (ARES) Program within the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army for Environment, Safety and Occupational Health (ODASA(ESOH)). ARES identifies, demonstrates, validates, and transitions cost-effective technology solutions to mitigate Army ESOH risks across energy resilience, emerging contaminants, infrastructure sustainability, and personnel safety while preserving lethality and operational readiness.
This position provides advisory, program-management, data-coordination, and communications support across the ARES lifecycle, from prioritized requirements intake and solution assessment through project execution, demonstration, validation, and transition to Army acquisition programs, installations, and other end users. The specialist works with Government leads and technical subject matter experts (SMEs) to evaluate alternatives, track RDT&E Budget Activity 4 (6.4) projects, and prepare decision-support and outreach products. Government Resource Management (RM) personnel retain responsibility for official financial processing and certifications; Government officials retain selection decisions and public-release approval. This is not a laboratory research position or an official public spokesperson role.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Maintain the centralized Army ESOH requirements intake process and prioritized 1–N list; coordinate validation, rankings, and investment themes with commands, installations, PAEs, and T2COM.

• Manage project tracking across cost, schedule, technical performance, key performance parameters, and risk; analyze status reports, prepare portfolio dashboards and quad charts, and coordinate reviews, reporting schedules, and action-item closure.

• Conduct literature and market assessments, prioritizing COTS, modified COTS, then RDT&E solutions; review proposals, test plans, and results with SMEs for evidence, operational relevance, maturity, and risk.

• Support calls for proposals, solicitation packages, and SBIR/SERDP/ESTCP/STED coordination; screen submissions, verify Army transition co-leads, facilitate validation and selection boards, consolidate SME evaluations, and document Government decisions.

• Support technology maturation and transition through applicable TRL 3–9 phases; draft MOAs, TTAs, CRADAs, and transition packages under AR 70-57, coordinating commitments and final reviews with acquisition programs, installations, EQTTP, SAFR, and R&D partners.

• Coordinate DOTMLPF-P assessments, lifecycle costs, training, and sustainment inputs; support project closeout, final reports, ROI analyses, and six- and twelve-month follow-up on adoption and benefits.

• Consolidate BA4 (6.4) spend plans and execution data, monitor benchmarks, and coordinate discrepancies and closeout with Government RM; prepare funding packages, financial records, and PPBE/POM inputs for Government processing without accounting transactions or funds certification.

• Develop program charters, SOPs, governance guidance, and policy support; prepare executive briefings and responses to leadership and congressional inquiries, ensuring technical accuracy, regulatory compliance, and AR 25-50 standards.

• Develop technical articles, success stories, fact sheets, website content, and conference materials; coordinate outreach and messaging with OCPA, command PAOs, the ESOH communications lead, and project SMEs.

• Prepare and track public-release review packages, including DD Form 1910 or Army equivalents, under DoDI 5230.09 and AR 360-1; coordinate OPSEC and technical reviews before authorized Government release.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, environmental science, engineering, business administration, public policy, or a related scientific, technical, or communications discipline.

• 5–8 years of progressive experience supporting DoD or Army RDT&E, S&T portfolio management, defense acquisition, enterprise ESOH programs, or defense-related technical communications.

• Working knowledge of research and technology-development processes; ability to review proposals, test plans, and results with SMEs and relate findings to mission needs.

• Familiarity with BA4 (6.4), PPBE/POM processes, spend plans, and funding execution tracking; ability to identify discrepancies and coordinate financial data with Government RM personnel.

• Working knowledge of DoD 5000-series acquisition, TRLs/TRAs, DOTMLPF-P frameworks, and technology transition to acquisition programs or military installations.

• Experience coordinating requirements, project status, technical specialists, Government stakeholders, and end users; ability to manage competing priorities and exercise sound judgment.

• Exceptional written and oral communication skills, including HQDA-level briefings, staff packages, policy drafts, analytical reports, and defense technical articles or digital content; familiarity with AR 25-50.

• Familiarity with DoD Security and Policy Review processes under DoDI 5230.09 and Army public affairs requirements under AR 360-1.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

• Active Secret clearance or ability to obtain and maintain a Secret clearance.

Desired Skills:

• Experience supporting Army or DoD ESOH research, demonstration, or technology-transition programs, including NDCEE, SERDP, ESTCP, STED, SBIR, SAFR, or EQTTP.

• Experience developing and staffing TTAs, MOAs, or CRADAs under AR 70-57 and working with Army Program Executive Offices (PEOs), program managers, and Army laboratories and centers (e.g., DEVCOM, USACE ERDC, and AFC/T2COM), academia, and industry partners.

• Experience conducting TRL assessments and supporting demonstration-to-fielding transitions, DOTMLPF-P assessments, lifecycle-cost analysis, and projected-versus-actual ROI.

• Experience evaluating research methods, test results, technical feasibility, or alternative technologies, including COTS and modified COTS solutions.

• Experience standing up a new program office (charters, governance boards, SOPs).

• Experience drafting Broad Agency Announcements, requests for information, or similar science and technology calls.

• Experience reviewing project funding packages and spend plans and coordinating financial closeout or post-project transition follow-up.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 collaboration and analytics tools, including Teams, SharePoint, Power BI, and Microsoft Approvals.

• DAWIA / Back-to-Basics certification in Program Management, Engineering and Technical Management, or Science and Technology Management, and/or Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

• Master’s degree in communications, technical writing, engineering, environmental management, systems management, business administration, or a related discipline.

Equal Opportunity Statement:
Seneca Holdings provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex/gender, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, marital status, genetic information and/or predisposing genetic characteristics, victim of domestic violence status, veteran status, or other protected class status. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including, but not limited to, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leave of absence, compensation and training. The Company also prohibits retaliation against any employee who exercises his or her rights under applicable anti-discrimination laws. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company does give hiring preference to Seneca or Native individuals. Veterans with expertise in these areas are highly encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Security Field Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:
AI NEEDS A NEW INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER. WE'RE BUILDING IT AT MODAL.

Every era of computing brought new workloads that previous infrastructure couldn't support: mainframes, databases, and the cloud. Each time, the company that rebuilt the layer underneath defined the decade. AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now.


Our customers include category-defining companies like Ramp https://modal.com/blog/how-ramp-built-a-full-context-background-coding-agent-on-modal, Cognition, DoorDash, and Suno. They rely on Modal for instant GPU access, sub-second container starts, and native storage, so it's simple to serve low-latency inference, fine-tune models, and access production-ready sandboxes at scale.


We've passed $1B in annualized run rate, up 15x from a year ago. In October 2026 we raised a $750M Series D led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation.


Our team includes creators of popular open-source projects (e.g., Seaborn https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn, Luigi https://github.com/spotify/luigi), academic researchers, international olympiad medalists, and experienced engineering and product leaders with decades of experience.




THE ROLE:

We’re looking for a Security Field Engineer to own how we represent and defend our security posture externally. This role sits at the intersection of security, engineering, and go-to-market, and is critical to building customer trust and accelerating deals.

You will work directly with customer security teams, translate our architecture and controls into clear, credible narratives, and ensure that what we present externally reflects how our systems actually operate.

This is a hands-on, technical role, not just documentation. You will identify patterns in customer requirements and drive improvements in both our product and security posture.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON:

Customer security engagement

 - Lead technical security conversations with customers and prospects

 - Respond to security reviews, deep-dive calls, and architecture discussions

 - Clearly explain our systems, controls, and tradeoffs to sophisticated security teams

Deal enablement and trust

 - Partner with Sales and GTM to unblock deals and accelerate security approvals

 - Own responses to complex security questionnaires and RFPs

 - Build credibility with customer security stakeholders through clear, consistent communication

Security representation

 - Own and evolve customer-facing security materials (trust center, whitepapers, architecture docs)

 - Ensure external messaging accurately reflects internal systems and controls

 - Continuously improve how we communicate security to reduce friction and ambiguity

Engineering partnership

 - Identify recurring customer requirements and gaps in our security posture

 - Work with engineering to prioritize and implement meaningful improvements

 - Translate customer expectations into concrete, actionable technical changes

Tooling and process

 - Improve how we handle inbound security reviews (automation, knowledge base, workflows)

 - Evaluate and implement tools to scale customer security interactions




YOU MAY BE A FIT IF:

 - You have experience in security engineering, security GRC, or solutions engineering in a technical product company.

jobs.title: Principal Instrumentation & Controls Engineer – Reactor
jobs.description:
The Team

You will be joining Valar Atomics' Instrumentation, Control & Electrical (IC&E) organization, working on the Reactor side of the program. Nuclear I&C Hardware Engineers own the instruments that measure the reactor itself neutron flux across startup, intermediate, and power ranges, core and primary loop temperatures and pressures, and radiation levels throughout the plant along with the signal chains that carry those measurements to the protection and control systems. You will work alongside I&C, electrical, reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, and nuclear safety engineers in a hands-on environment where measurement quality directly supports reactor safety. As a principal engineer, you will be among the discipline's most senior technical voices: an architect of its measurement systems, a final checker of its highest-consequence work, and a standard-setter for the engineers who will build their careers here. The team values technical depth, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking Principal I&C Engineers to own the technical direction of nuclear instrumentation plant design for our high temperature gas-cooled reactor program. The role spans the full domain neutron flux detection, radiation monitoring, reactor protection system sensors and signal chains, and process instrumentation in nuclear service, but at the level of measurement architecture, application and qualification strategy, and design authority rather than routine design execution. The focus is the application of vendor-supplied instrumentation in plant design, not instrument or detector development. This is a principal position: you will define the reactor measurement architecture and instrumentation application strategy for a first-of-a-kind reactor, hold final technical approval within assigned domains for safety-significant instrumentation designs and qualification bases, direct the resolution of the hardest measurement application problems in the program, represent the discipline in licensing and regulatory engagements, and build the engineering capability of the organization around you. Where a Staff Engineer owns the discipline's design bases and quality, the Principal Engineer owns where the discipline is going.

Key Responsibilities

Measurement Architecture and Technical Strategy

• Define and own the reactor measurement architecture across the program: the neutron flux measurement strategy across startup, intermediate, and power ranges, the reactor protection system sensor architecture, radiation monitoring architecture, and the measurement strategy for primary-loop process variables in high-temperature helium service.

• Author and own the discipline's philosophy and basis documents: instrumentation design basis, signal chain design philosophy, setpoint and uncertainty methodology basis, and the environmental and radiation qualification program basis that constrain and guide all downstream instrumentation engineering.

• Own the instrumentation application strategy for first-of-a-kind reactor conditions: technology and vendor selection across available detector and sensor platforms, application-specific qualification strategy, standardization across the plant and future units, and supply continuity and obsolescence strategy for critical instruments.

• Own the discipline's standards program within assigned domains: set the framework and priorities for design bases and standards, delegate authorship to staff and senior engineers, and approve them for release; drive convergence across the program.

• Evaluate emerging, commercially maturing measurement technology, advanced detectors, distributed and optical sensing, digital signal processing platforms, and decide what is adopted into plant design, what is piloted, and what is excluded, balancing capability against qualification burden, licensing risk, and long-term supportability.

Design Authority and Technical Governance

• Serve as a discipline design authority: hold final technical approval, within assigned domains, for safety-significant instrumentation designs, qualification bases and dispositions, deviations from design bases, and concessions; adjudicate technical disputes within the discipline and represent it in cross-discipline conflicts at program level.

• Own the technical integrity of reactor protection instrumentation within assigned domains: channel architecture, independence and separation (IEEE 603, IEEE 384 principles), qualification pedigree, and approval of safety-significant design changes.

• Lead the discipline's engagement in the highest-consequence program reviews: preliminary and critical design reviews, safety analysis and licensing reviews, qualification program reviews, and instrumentation readiness reviews for fuel load, startup testing, and power ascension milestones.

• Direct investigations of the most significant instrumentation problems and anomalies, spurious protection actuations, channel failures, qualification anomalies, and approve corrective action strategy, ensuring findings are institutionalized in design bases, standards, and training.

• Personally execute or lead engineering on the small set of measurement problems where the consequence of error or the degree of novelty warrants the discipline's most senior engineers and know which problems those are.

External Representation and Licensing

• Serve as a senior instrumentation voice in the nuclear licensing effort: contribute to and defend the instrumentation content of the safety analysis and licensing basis measurement capability claims, protection system instrumentation design bases, setpoint and uncertainty methodology, and qualification arguments, and support regulatory interactions and audits.

• Represent Valar Atomics to strategic detector and instrumentation vendors at a senior technical level; own long-term vendor technical relationships, qualification expectations, supply continuity for critical detectors, and escalation of systemic vendor issues.

• Represent the company in industry and standards forums as appropriate (IEEE Nuclear Power Engineering Committee working groups, IEC SC45A, advanced reactor industry groups); bring emerging standards and regulatory developments back into program strategy before they become constraints.

Organizational Capability

• Build the discipline's engineering capability: define the technical competencies the nuclear instrumentation organization needs, shape role definitions and the technical career ladder with the Director, set the hiring bar, and lead technical interviews for senior positions.

• Mentor staff and senior engineers toward independent technical authority; sponsor their development through delegation of ownership with oversight rather than retention of scope.

• Advise IC&E leadership on technical risk, resourcing, and sequencing for the instrumentation program; provide independent technical judgment on schedule and cost pressure where it intersects measurement integrity and reactor safety.

• Maintain disciplined engineering records consistent with nuclear quality requirements, ensuring traceability of design decisions, analyses, and test results, and setting the example for the discipline's documentation culture.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Nuclear, Electrical, Computer, or Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related discipline.

• 10+ years of experience in nuclear instrumentation, radiation detection systems, or reactor I&C, including substantial nuclear application.

• Demonstrated ownership of nuclear instrumentation or detection system scope across multiple significant programs, including at least one taken from concept or requirements through qualification, deployment, and initial operation.

• Track record of architecture-level technical leadership: defining measurement strategy, instrumentation architecture, or design bases that were adopted across a program or organization, not just a single system.

• Recognized technical authority in at least one deep area of the domain (for example: neutron flux instrumentation, detector physics and signal chains, environmental/radiation qualification, or protection system instrumentation), evidenced by design authority roles, published work, standards participation, or a verifiable reputation as the final technical reference.

• Deep, hands-on command of the full domain: detector physics and operating regimes, wide-range channel design across pulse, fluctuation, and current modes, analog signal chain engineering, qualification methodology (IEEE 323/344), and nuclear I&C standards (IEEE 603, IEEE 497, IEC 61513).

• Experience with formal approval or independent-review authority over safety-related or safety-significant instrumentation designs, analyses, or qualification bases.

• Experience directing and developing other engineers, including senior-level engineers, and reviewing and approving their work as a formal checker or design authority.

• Experience representing an engineering discipline to external parties — regulators, licensing bodies, standards organizations, major vendors, or client design authorities.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Professional Engineer (PE) license.

• Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in nuclear engineering, physics, or a related field.

• Direct experience with NRC licensing interactions, safety analysis instrumentation content, or defense of instrumentation design bases before a regulator.

• Experience defining instrumentation strategy for first-of-a-kind, advanced, or test reactors, particularly high-temperature gas-cooled or other non-LWR designs.

• Experience applying instrumentation in advanced, test, or first-of-a-kind reactor plant designs, including harsh-environment installations, MI cable systems, and vessel or containment penetration interfaces.

• Setpoint and uncertainty methodology expertise (ISA-67.04 or equivalent) at a methodology-ownership level.

• Participation in IEEE NPEC, IEC SC45A, or equivalent standards development.

• Working experience under NQA-1 / 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programs at a program-governance level.

What We Offer

• Competitive base salary

• Equity ownership in a rapidly growing advanced energy company

• Comprehensive medical benefits

• Unlimited PTO

• Free daily lunch and dinner provided onsite

• Generous PPE stipend

• High-impact startup environment with significant ownership and autonomy

• Opportunities for rapid career growth and internal advancement

• Direct collaboration with experienced operators, engineers, and industry leaders

• The opportunity to help build and scale transformative energy technology from the ground up

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Valar Atomics is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law.

We are committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination and harassment and will provide reasonable accommodation as required by law.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States as a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (green card holder).

Salary

$196,000—$240,000 USD

Imprint is taking on our opportunity with a small team of exceptional people, with the best AI and technology dramatically amplifying what each person can accomplish. That means you’ll learn faster here than you could anywhere else. You’ll be one of the few people building an entirely new technology with the ownership and trust to shape what Imprint becomes. You’ll work alongside people who make you sharper everyday, armed with tools that turn your best ideas into reality faster than you thought possible. This is a rare chance to do the most important work of your career and to help prove that a small team can build what’s never been done before, inside industries that haven’t changed in decades.




ROLE SUMMARY

As Partner Marketing Manager, you will own marketing for Imprint's launch partners, taking each new co-brand program from pre-launch through its first couple months in market. This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will set the strategy and you will also do the work: write the briefs, build the assets, ship the launches, and report on results.

You are the marketing point of contact for your partners. You will build each partner's marketing plan, run every launch workstream, design acquisition journeys, and make sure every piece of work clears brand, legal, bank, and network review. You will work closely with Partner Success, Lifecycle, Data Science, Creative, and Compliance to get programs to market fast and grow them once they're live.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Partner strategy and planning

 - Own the marketing strategy and quarterly plan for each launch partner

 - Build and share a marketing strategy and quarterly plan for each assigned launch partner, including full marketing workstream: assets, landing pages, and launch comms

 - Plan and run joint campaigns with partner marketing teams

 - Write partner-facing marketing comms and keep partners informed on plans and results

 - Run the flighting calendar, quarterly planning, and intake process as the single source of truth for partner marketing work

Launch marketing

 - Own the marketing workstream for every program and campaign launch, including assets, landing pages, launch comms, and PR

 - Build an asset bank for launch and sustain phases, aligned with the partner playbook and toolkit

Acquisition

 - Set top-of-funnel strategy and offers for each partner

 - Build and optimize ITA and prescreen journeys

 - Drive acquisition through in-store and partner-owned channels

Lifecycle

 - Brief Lifecycle Managers on key moments in each partner's retail and marketing calendar

Creative and brand

 - Manage design and copy, working within Imprint brand, partner guidelines, and the design system

 - Manage translations for multilingual programs

Measurement

 - Partner with Data Science to set marketing KPIs, including LTV/CAC and spend per active

 - Design tests, report on results, and use what you learn to shape the next plan

Compliance

 - Route all marketing through the required legal, bank, and network reviews and keep launches on schedule

Budget

 - Provide input on spend priorities
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - 8+ years of partner, product, or growth marketing experience, ideally in financial services or fintech

 - Hands-on experience launching new products, programs, or partnerships end to end

 - Experience running acquisition journeys, including prescreen or ITA direct mail and partner or in-store channels

 - Strong project management: you can run a calendar, an intake process, and multiple launches at once without dropping details

 - Experience managing creative production with designers and copywriters, including brand and partner guidelines

 - Comfort working with data teams to define KPIs, design tests, and report results

 - Experience moving work through legal and regulatory review in a regulated industry

 - Clear writer and communicator who can present plans and results to partners

Nice to have

 - Co-brand credit card or loyalty program experience

 - Experience with prescreen data providers (TransUnion, Acxiom) and direct mail vendors

 - Familiarity with Braze or similar lifecycle tools

 - Experience at a high-growth startup where you built the playbook while shipping




PERKS & BENEFITS

 - Mental health support through Spring Health, plus a confidential Employee Assistance Program

 - Healthcare navigation through Rightway, plus HSA, FSA and commuter benefits

 - Flexible paid time off

 - 20 weeks of paid parental leave for primary caregivers and 8 weeks for all new parents

 - The latest tools and technology, including AI, so you can do your best work
