jobs.title: Mid Level Optical Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Overview 

Red 6 is an innovative Augmented Reality (AR) technology startup leading the way in synthetic air combat training. Our primary technology, supporting our ATARS product, enables pilots to simulate the cognitive challenges of flying while accessing realistic, scalable training in dynamic outdoor environments.

Red 6 is seeking a hands-on Optical Engineer to help design, prototype, characterize, and validate current and next-generation augmented reality systems. This role is for an engineer who enjoys turning challenging optical requirements into practical hardware, models, test plans, and well-documented engineering results.

The Optical Engineer contributes to optical performance across the ATARS platform and future architectures. The role works closely with experienced technical leaders and cross-functional partners in Product, R&D, Manufacturing, Software, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain, and external suppliers to move optical systems from concept through prototype, validation, production transition, customer integration, and field support.

The ideal candidate combines sound optical fundamentals with curiosity and execution discipline. They can build and validate an optical model, run a careful lab experiment, analyze performance data, and communicate clear findings and recommendations to the team.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


OPTICAL ARCHITECTURE & DESIGN EXECUTION

 - Support detailed optical design for ultra-wide field-of-view AR headset optics, freeform combiners, waveguides, HOE/PVH elements, display and illumination integration, eye-tracking optical paths, and future optical architectures.

 - Develop, maintain, and validate optical models, tolerancing analyses, performance budgets, and design documentation using tools such as Code V, Zemax OpticStudio, Python, MATLAB, FRED, LightTools, JMP, or equivalent workflows.

 - Contribute to trade studies across field of view, brightness, contrast, eyebox, MTF, distortion, pupil swim, color uniformity, stray light, environmental stability, manufacturability, cost, and schedule risk.

 - Convert system and product requirements into measurable optical requirements, acceptance criteria, verification plans, and design margins.

 - Produce and review technical packages for optical components and subassemblies, including drawings, specifications, tolerances, coatings, illumination requirements, and test methods.


PROTOTYPE, METROLOGY & VALIDATION

 - Plan and execute optical prototype characterization, including interferometry, MTF measurement, distortion mapping, radiometry, photometry, color measurement, image quality evaluation, and headset-level optical metrology.

 - Support calibration and characterization methods that produce repeatable, traceable optical performance across prototypes and production-intent systems.

 - Participate in root-cause investigations for optical defects, performance variation, field issues, and integration failures; translate findings into corrective design, process, or supplier actions.

 - Establish practical golden-sample, acceptance, and correlation methods that connect component-level measurements to system-level visual performance.

 - Partner with software and systems teams to define calibration algorithms, measurement data products, and validation workflows needed for reliable customer experience.


PRODUCT INTEGRATION & SUPPLIER COLLABORATION

 - Work directly with Product, R&D, Manufacturing, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software, Supply Chain, and Program Management to integrate optical requirements at the system level.

 - Support technical engagement with optical suppliers by reviewing data packages, first articles, test results, manufacturability concerns, and corrective-action plans.

 - Guide DFM and yield-improvement activities for optical manufacturing processes including diamond turning, injection molding, thin-film coatings, holographic recording, assembly, and inspection.

 - Participate in design reviews and program risk reviews; clearly communicate optical trade-offs, technical risk, recommended decisions, and validation status to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Support customer integration activities, demonstrations, and field troubleshooting where deep optical judgment is required.


ENGINEERING GROWTH & TEAM CONTRIBUTION

 - Bring rigor to optical documentation, experimental discipline, and evidence-based engineering decisions.

 - Learn from design reviews, lab work, analysis methods, and root-cause investigations while sharing useful tools, data, and lessons learned with the team.

 - Contribute observations and technical evidence that inform optical technology roadmaps and risk-retirement plans.

 - Help improve reusable analysis, metrology, and design-review practices that increase execution speed, repeatability, and technical confidence.

SUCCESS IN THE ROLE

 - Optical architectures are well modeled, thoroughly characterized, and connected to clear product requirements and validation evidence.

 - Critical optical risks are discovered early, quantified rigorously, and reduced through focused prototypes, trade studies, or supplier actions.

 - Calibration, metrology, and acceptance methods are repeatable and support confident prototype-to-production transition.

 - Optical supplier relationships are technically strong, issues are resolved quickly, and delivered hardware meets performance expectations.

 - The engineer is a reliable cross-functional partner who advances technical work with sound analysis, well-run experiments, and clear documentation.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - B.S. or M.S. in Optical Engineering, Physics, Applied Physics, or a closely related technical field.

 - 3+ years of experience developing or characterizing optical systems, preferably including near-eye displays, AR/VR, HMDs, imaging systems, projection systems, aerospace/defense optics, or other high-performance optical hardware.

 - Demonstrated ownership of optical systems from concept through modeling, prototype build, characterization, validation, production transition, and field support.

 - Hands-on capability in optical design or characterization, including some combination of tolerancing, image quality, MTF, distortion, stray light, radiometry, photometry, display performance, color science, calibration, and headset characterization.

 - Working proficiency in one or more optical design, analysis, or metrology toolchains, such as Code V, Zemax OpticStudio, Python, MATLAB, FRED, LightTools, JMP, or equivalent tools.

 - Experience working directly with optical suppliers and cross-functional Product, Manufacturing, Software, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain, and Program Management partners.

 - U.S. citizenship required; must be eligible for and willing to obtain a security clearance.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with ultra-wide-FOV AR systems, freeform combiners, waveguides, holographic optical elements, polarization volume holograms, holographic backlights, or laser/display illumination architectures.

 - Experience with LCoS, MicroLED, DMD, laser backlights, polarization optics, display color calibration, color uniformity, or human visual system modeling.

 - Experience with optical manufacturing methods, eye-tracking optics, or defense, aerospace, military training systems, SBIR/STTR environments, or venture-backed hardware companies.


WHO THRIVES HERE

You are a builder and a problem solver who wants to stay close to the physics, the model, and the hardware. You enjoy turning a measurement, model, or prototype into a clear next step - whether the question is field of view, waveguide efficiency, stray light, color uniformity, calibration repeatability, or brightness in direct sunlight. You are motivated by building optical systems that military pilots depend on, and bring the curiosity, rigor, and persistence needed to make demanding AR hardware perform reliably in the real world.

Estimated Base Salary upon skills and experience: $120,000 to $140,000 range 

Full-Time Employee Benefits

 - Healthcare, Dental, and Vision (100% coverage for Employees)

 - Paid time off, including vacation, sick, paid holidays, and parental leave

 - Short and Long-Term Disability

 - Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

 - 401(k) Retirement Plan

 - Voluntary Worksite Benefits (Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity)

 - May be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus based on individual and company performance, subject to plan terms.
   

Note

Red 6 reserves the right to change its current benefits program at any time, in a manner that is consistent with applicable federal and state regulations.

This job description is not a contract and confers no contractual rights, privileges, or benefits on any applicant or potential applicant. Red 6 has the right to change any and all terms of this job description, including, but not limited to, job responsibilities, qualifications, and benefits. Nothing in this job description constitutes an offer or guarantee of employment. 

Red Six Aerospace, Inc, is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Staff Workday HRIS Technical Analyst
jobs.description:
About Checkr
Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About the team/role

We are seeking a highly experienced Workday specialist to own and advance our Workday platform end to end. This role sits at the center of our people systems landscape and is responsible for deep Workday configuration, business process design, integrations, reporting, and the adoption of Workday's AI and automation capabilities. The ideal candidate has deep, hands-on Workday expertise: they know its modules, security model, and release cadence intimately, and they can translate complex HR and business requirements into clean, scalable Workday solutions. We are looking for a proactive self-starter who can independently drive work forward without needing explicit direction.

What you’ll do

• Platform Ownership & Roadmap - Serve as the Workday subject matter expert across HR, IT, and Finance; own the platform roadmap, module adoption strategy, and alignment with Workday's twice-yearly release cycle.

• Configuration & Optimization - Lead configuration, testing, and deployment across HCM Core, Compensation, Benefits, Absence, Time Tracking, Talent, Performance, Recruiting, Workday Adaptive Planning - including business processes, security models, calculated fields, and custom reporting.

• Release Management & Health - Conduct regression testing for each Workday release, perform regular audits, and drive performance tuning and configuration health checks to ensure platform stability.

• Integrations & Automation - Build and maintain integrations using Workday Studio, Core Connectors, EIB, and APIs to connect Workday with adjacent systems (Greenhouse, CultureAmp, Pave, payroll, finance, provisioning); identify and eliminate manual workflows through system-driven automation.

• Self-Service & Employee Experience - Optimize business processes, notifications, navigation, and the user interface to reduce administrative burden, increase adoption, and improve the employee and manager self-service experience.

• AI & Analytics - Evaluate and implement Workday AI, machine learning, skills intelligence, and Analytics capabilities; partner with data and IT teams to ensure scalability, data privacy, and ethical deployment.

• Cross-Functional Partnership - Translate stakeholder requirements into technical specifications, manage the Workday vendor and implementation partner relationships, and lead project delivery and adoption across the organization.

What you bring

• Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field.

• 6+ years of progressive HR technology experience, with deep, hands-on expertise configuring and optimizing Workday.

• Demonstrated expertise across multiple Workday modules, such as HCM Core, Compensation, Benefits, Absence, Time Tracking, Talent, or Recruiting. Workday certification (Pro or equivalent) is a strong plus.

• Hands-on experience building Workday integrations using Studio, Core Connectors, EIB, and Workday APIs.

• Strong command of the Workday security model, business process framework, calculated fields, and advanced reporting.

• Experience with Workday Adaptive Planning is a strong plus.

• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills. Self-starter with a proactive approach, capable of driving work independently and identifying opportunities for improvement without explicit direction.

• Proven experience with process automation and workflow design inside Workday.

• Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex Workday concepts for non-technical audiences.

• An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Pay Transparency Disclosure

We use geographic cost of labor as an input to develop ranges for our roles and as such, each location where we hire may have a different range. If this role is remote, we have listed the top to the bottom of the possible range, but we will specify the target range for an exact location when you are selected for a recruiting discussion. For more information on our compensation philosophy, see our website.

On-target Earnings OR Base Salary range (San Francisco, CA)

$161,000—$189,000 USD

What We Offer

• A fast-paced and collaborative environment

• Learning and development allowance

• Competitive cash and equity compensation, and opportunity for advancement

• 100% medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Up to $25K reimbursement for fertility, adoption, and parental planning services

• Flexible PTO policy

• Monthly wellness stipend

At Checkr, we believe an in office work environment strengthens collaboration, drives innovation, and encourages connection. Our hub locations are Denver, CO; San Francisco, CA; Nashville, TN; and Santiago, Chile. Individuals are expected to work from the office 3+ days a week. In-office perks are provided, such as lunch five times a week, a commuter stipend, and an abundance of snacks and beverages. A relocation stipend may be available for those willing to relocate to a Checkr hub location.

Equal Employment Opportunities at Checkr
Checkr is committed to building the best product and company, which requires hiring talented and qualified individuals with a diverse set of perspectives and lived experiences. Checkr believes in hiring people of all backgrounds, including those whose histories are impacted by the justice system in accordance with local, state, and/or federal laws, including the San Francisco’s Fair Chance Ordinance.

Applicant Privacy Policy
If you are a California resident or are located in Alberta or British Columbia, our Applicant Privacy Policy applies to our collection and processing of your personal information when you apply for a role with us or otherwise participate in our recruitment process.

For applicants in Massachusetts: It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

*Legitimate Checkr emails will always include our official domain name after the @ symbol (e.g., name@checkr.com or name@ext.checkr.com).

jobs.title: Production Supervisor
jobs.description:
Nestled in San Francisco's Excelsior neighborhood on a nine-acre campus, the San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living (SFCJL) is the leading senior services organization in Northern California. Our continuum of care includes: the Frank Residences assisted living and memory care; the Jewish Home and Rehabilitation Center, offering long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, an acute geriatric psychiatric unit for adults over the age of 65; and our Foundation.

Founded in 1871 and formerly known as the Jewish Home, our legacy grounds us as our vision propels us forward. Today, we've evolved to support more than 2,500 older adults each year through innovative, comprehensive programs rooted in the Jewish values of compassion, community, and excellence. We are equally proud of our inclusive culture, where 950 team members of diverse faiths and backgrounds work together in shared purpose.

WHY WORK WITH US

• Mission-driven nonprofit organization

• Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

• Meaningful work that positively impacts the lives of older adults every day

• Inclusive community, welcoming to all (you do not need to be Jewish to live or work here)

• Supportive, team-oriented environment

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

• Collaborative leadership focused on enhancing the employee experience

POSITION SUMMARY

As a Production Supervisor, you will oversee daily meal preparation for residents and the preparation of special meals for community events and gatherings. In addition to culinary responsibilities, you will be accountable for daily point-of-sale (POS) operations, the generation and review of daily sales reports, menu-system accuracy, and inventory monitoring and reporting. You will collaborate closely with Dining Services management, maintaining effective communication and promptly reporting discrepancies and operational concerns.

This is a non-union, supervisory position with authority to assign and direct work, train and evaluate employees, and effectively recommend discipline. You will supervise staff on assigned shifts, exercise independent judgment regarding production volume, menu execution, and service standards, and serve as the person in charge of the venue in the absence of the Dining Services management team.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Culinary Operations

• Prepare and cook food items and meals according to standardized recipes and planned menus, ensuring high-quality, palatable, and appetizing meals.
• Use professional cooking techniques to prepare center-of-the-plate proteins, sauces, and visually appealing plate presentations with appropriate side dishes.
• Plan food production to align with meal service hours, maintaining food quality, temperature, and appearance while minimizing overproduction.
• Read customer meal tickets and prepare selected menu items to order using small-batch cooking techniques on the hotline, managing multiple tickets simultaneously during peak periods.
• Demonstrate expertise on sauté and grill stations.
• Assist with food preparation for special meals, parties, and events.
• Prepare soups, appetizers, entrées, vegetables, side dishes, and desserts for regular and special dietary needs.
• Prepare and maintain display and grab-and-go items according to presentation standards, ensuring accurate labeling, pricing, and date marking on packaged items.
• Provide authorized substitute foods to residents who decline the served meal and consult with the Executive Chef regarding menu changes.
• Review special diet requests and orders to ensure accurate meal service.
• Follow sanitary regulations, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) standards, and established policies and procedures when preparing, holding, displaying, and serving food.
• Maintain temperature logs, cooling logs, and food safety documentation, and immediately report deviations.
• Maintain clean and organized production, service, and food storage areas.
• Complete assigned cleaning tasks according to daily and weekly checklists and maintain a sanitary work environment in compliance with local codes and organizational policies.
• Dispose of food and waste in accordance with established procedures.

Point-of-Sale, Sales Reporting & Menu Systems

• Independently operate the POS system, including opening and closing the register or terminal, processing guest transactions, and accurately processing payment tenders.
• Apply resident charges, discounts, comps, and voids in accordance with established policies.
• Generate, print, and review daily sales reports at the close of each operating day, including transaction counts, item-level sales mix, voids, discounts, comps, and tender totals.
• Reconcile daily sales against receipts and tender totals, identify variances, and document them on the daily close record.
• Report any sales, transaction, cash, or POS discrepancy to management immediately upon discovery, on the same business day without exception.
• Ensure discrepancies are not held, corrected unilaterally, or carried forward to the following day.
• Audit the menu system regularly to verify that item names, prices, modifiers, portion descriptions, tax settings, and category assignments match approved menus and current pricing.
• Identify discontinued, seasonal, mispriced, duplicated, or incorrectly configured menu items; submit correction requests to management and verify corrections after implementation.
• Monitor daily transaction and sales-mix data for production-planning trends, including slow-moving items, high-waste items, and overproduction or underproduction.
• Communicate sales and production observations to the Executive Chef and Dining Services Director.
• Maintain the integrity and confidentiality of POS credentials, register access, and transaction records, and follow cash-handling and register-accountability procedures.

Supervision & Staff Leadership

• Assign, direct, and prioritize staff work on assigned shifts, including station assignments, production tasks, side work, and cleaning duties.
• Hold staff accountable for the quality and completion of their work.
• Train new and existing staff on recipes, production standards, food safety, HACCP, sanitation, equipment use, and POS procedures, and verify and document competency.
• Monitor staff performance, attendance, and punctuality; provide daily coaching and feedback and contribute written input to performance evaluations.
• Evaluate employees and effectively recommend discipline.
• Address and resolve employee concerns and work-related complaints at the first level, escalating unresolved matters to management.
• Enforce organizational policies, safety rules, food safety standards, and uniform and hygiene requirements, correcting noncompliance promptly.
• Serve as the person in charge of the venue in the absence of the Dining Services management team.

Communication & Reporting

• Maintain effective communication with management regarding kitchen operations and operational needs.
• Provide daily updates to the Executive Chef and Dining Services Director regarding sales, discrepancies, inventory status, equipment issues, and guest feedback.
• Monitor and report inventory status and concerns to management.
• Work closely with management to address concerns related to food preparation, service, and kitchen operations.
• Interact courteously and professionally with residents, families, staff, and visitors, responding accurately to questions about menu items, ingredients, allergens, and pricing.
• Promptly report incidents, infractions, injuries, and policy violations to the Executive Chef.
• Attend required in-service training and education sessions.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

JOB DETAILS

• Pay Rate: $33.50 per hour
• Hours: Full-Time, 40 hours per week
• Shift Schedule: AM
• Days Off: Friday & Saturday
• Working Days: Monday through Thursday

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• High school diploma or equivalent.
• Minimum of ten (10) years of experience as a cook in a hotel, restaurant, club, or similar establishment.
• Minimum of five (5) years of experience in a food service operation with personal responsibility for operating a POS system and handling guest transactions.
• Minimum of two (2) years of experience in a lead, supervisory, or person-in-charge role in a commercial kitchen.
• Demonstrated proficiency with POS systems, including processing transactions, applying discounts and voids, completing end-of-day close procedures, and generating and reviewing sales reports.
• Demonstrated ability to audit a menu system against an approved printed menu and identify pricing, item, and configuration errors.

jobs.title: Specialist, Wastewater Treatment
jobs.description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

Overview

The Specialist, Wastewater Treatment is responsible for the compliant operation of Scout’s pretreatment and reverse osmosis systems in support of Scout’s launch and production activities in South Carolina. The role is responsible for the generation of procedures and standards and requires working in industrial and laboratory environments.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, EHS- Production, this position will establish positive working relationships with internal stakeholders, third party support and regulatory officials.

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

• Support the design, construction, and commissioning of the Wastewater Treatment System

• Develop and Implement Wastewater Operating Procedures

• Develop and Implement Wastewater Preventative Maintenance Plans

• Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local water regulations, including discharge permits.

• Operate and maintain wastewater system including servicing of pumps, motors, valves, and equipment.

• Analyze and track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to wastewater, identifying trends, and recommend improvements.

• Assess lab data and make appropriate operational adjustments to maintain operation below permitted levels

• Maintain records, perform data entry, and provide detailed reporting

• Ensure completion of work assignments within specified deadlines and in compliance with safety regulations and procedures

• Analyze and evaluate equipment, trouble-shooting malfunctions, and monitoring of water operations

• Performs preventative maintenance, minor repairs, and cleaning of equipment

• Ensures Lab Equipment is calibrated and in working order

• Work Proactively with production team members to manage flow and treatment of wastes

• Perform necessary testing and management of Reverse Osmosis (RO) System

• Performs other duties as assigned by Senior Manager, EHS

Location & Travel Expectations:

• This role will be based out of the Scout Motors location in Blythewood, South Carolina.

• The responsibilities of this role require 5 days attendance in office with in-person meetings and events regularly. Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

• High school diploma or GED

• Must possess or be able to obtain an active B-level South Carolina Physical/Chemical Wastewater License and become Operator of Record

• 4+ years of experience operating wastewater treatment systems

• Ability to work independently

• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

• Requires the ability to read, write, compile, and analyze data and reports daily Ability to monitor control panels, gauges, and meters to ensure proper plant operation

• Ability to operate and maintain standard wastewater lab equipment.

• Must be available to work weekends, overtime and ‘on-call’ as needed

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up.  This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation.  In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

• Competitive insurance including: Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans

• 401(k) program with: An employer match and immediate vesting

• Generous Paid Time Off including: 20 days planned PTO, as accrued 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $100,000.00 - $125,000.00

Internal leveling code: IC9

• Residing in Los Angeles: Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

• Residing in New York City: This role is not eligible for remote work in New York City.

Equal Opportunity

Scout Motors is committed to employing a diverse workforce and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, disability, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected by law. Scout Motors is committed to compliance with all applicable fair employment practice laws. If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please contact ScoutAccommodations@scoutmotors.com.

jobs.title: Clinic Director (Bellevue, WA)
jobs.description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is bringing our intensive outpatient (IOP), partial hospitalization (PHP) and interventional psychiatry services, starting with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), into local communities. As Clinic Director, you will lead day-to-day operations of one clinic and be accountable for the quality of care, the team and the clinic's growth.

You are a licensed clinician (LCSW or PMHNP) who has led clinical operations at a multi-provider practice and wants to build something new. You will supervise a team of clinicians and non-clinical staff, see a reduced caseload of your own (more while the clinic ramps up), and be the on-site lead for crises and escalations. You will partner closely with our clinical, operations, outreach and admissions teams to grow the clinic and shape how Charlie Health delivers in-person care. As we add clinics in your region, this role can grow into oversight of multiple sites.

We're a team of passionate, forward-thinking professionals eager to take on the challenge of the mental health crisis and play a formative role in providing life-saving solutions. If you're inspired by our mission and energized by the opportunity to increase access to mental healthcare and impact millions of lives in a profound way, apply today.

Responsibilities

• Lead day-to-day operations of a single in-person clinic offering IOP, PHP and TMS, including scheduling, staffing coverage, patient flow and facilities

• Supervise and develop junior clinicians and non-clinical staff, including therapists, group facilitators, social workers, TMS technicians and front-desk staff

• Carry a reduced clinical caseload (therapy or medication management, depending on licensure), with more direct patient care while the clinic ramps

• Serve as the on-site lead for patient crises, safety events and escalations, following Charlie Health protocols

• Coordinate care across therapy and psychiatry so each client gets the right level and mix of care

• Own clinic performance against targets for census, utilization, admissions and quality, and report on it regularly

• Partner with outreach and admissions teams to build local referral relationships and grow clinic census

• Maintain compliance with state licensing, payor, documentation and safety requirements, and support site and provider credentialing

• Help hire and onboard clinic staff, and contribute to the playbook for opening future clinics

Requirements

• Master's degree in social work with an active, unrestricted LCSW, or an active, unrestricted PMHNP license, in the state where the clinic is located (or eligibility to obtain one before start)

• Experience leading clinical operations at a practice of roughly 5–10 providers

• Experience in a multi-specialty practice that delivers both therapy and psychiatry required

• Experience with IOP or PHP, or with interventional psychiatry (TMS, ketamine / Spravato), preferred

• Experience supervising clinical and non-clinical staff; eligibility to provide clinical supervision for licensure in your state preferred

• Willingness to carry a reduced caseload and to work on-site full time, with flexibility for crises and clinic needs

• Strong judgment in crisis management and risk assessment

• Work authorized in the United States and native or bilingual English proficiency

• Familiarity with and willingness to use cloud-based communication software—Google Suite, Slack, Zoom, Dropbox, Salesforce—in addition to EMR and survey software on a daily basis

Benefits

Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Our Values

• Connection: Care deeply & inspire hope.

• Congruence: Stay curious & heed the evidence.

• Commitment: Act with urgency & don’t give up.

Please do not call our public clinical admissions line in regard to this or any other job posting.

Please be cautious of potential recruitment fraud. If you are interested in exploring opportunities at Charlie Health, please go directly to our Careers Page: https://www.charliehealth.com/careers/current-openings. Charlie Health will never ask you to pay a fee or download software as part of the interview process with our company. In addition, Charlie Health will not ask for your personal banking information until you have signed an offer of employment and completed onboarding paperwork that is provided by our People Operations team. All communications with Charlie Health Talent and People Operations professionals will only be sent from @charliehealth.com email addresses. Legitimate emails will never originate from gmail.com, yahoo.com, or other commercial email services.

Recruiting agencies, please do not submit unsolicited referrals for this or any open role. We have a roster of agencies with whom we partner, and we will not pay any fee associated with unsolicited referrals.

At Charlie Health, we value being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We strive to cultivate an environment where individuals can be their authentic selves. Being an Equal Opportunity Employer means every member of our team feels as though they are supported and belong. We value diverse perspectives to help us provide essential mental health and substance use disorder treatments to all young people.

Charlie Health applicants are assessed solely on their qualifications for the role, without regard to disability or need for accommodation.

jobs.title: Industrial Technician - Minneapolis, MN
jobs.description:
JOB POSITION:  Industrial Technician

Are you interested in becoming an experienced Overhead Crane Service Technician? Join Konecranes, one of the world’s largest material handling companies. We're seeking skilled individuals with electrical and mechanical expertise, comfortable working at extreme heights. Our service technicians, the heart of our industry, thrive in a safety-first environment. You'll troubleshoot 480 3-phase motors, address crane issues, and collaborate with clients and facility directors to meet service needs across the United States.

Principal Responsibilities:

• Conduct inspections, maintenance, and repairs on electric overhead traveling cranes and hoists at customer locations.
• Provide on-call service as part of a rotation, including after-hours support.
• Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, structural, and electronic issues on-site.
• Perform post-repair audits to ensure safety features are functional.
• Document findings and recommend corrective actions, including safety notifications to customers.
• Consult with customers on repair and safety issues, offering recommendations for material handling improvement.
• Produce electronic documentation using company tools, obtaining customer signatures.
• Stay updated on industry codes and regulations (OSHA, ANSI, CMAA, HMI).
• Complete service reports and other required documents accurately and promptly.
• Communicate with the Field Operations Manager and Service Coordinator following established practices
• Maintain company-issued equipment, vehicles, and assets in proper working order.
• Operate tools, equipment, and vehicles, reporting deficiencies to the supervisor.
• Follow established safety rules and procedures, including customer guidelines.
• Participate in monthly safety meetings.
• Perform other responsibilities as assigned by the supervisor.

Education: High School Diploma required. Associate degree in Industrial Electrical and/or Mechanical Technology or related field preferred or equivalent vocational/technical training and experience.

Experience: Minimum one (1) year experience involving electrical troubleshooting and mechanical repair. Some electronic experience but not necessary. Prior experience with cranes is a benefit, but not required.

Other Requirements: Must have and maintain a good driving record, including a valid driver's license. Must be willing to work off the ground. Can work varied overtime, as needed by customer, be available for "on call" as part of the service office rotation and be able to travel and work out of town, on occasion.

Must be able to frequently lift to 25 lbs. Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. on a daily basis. Must be able to lift to 75 lbs. although not on a daily basis. Must be able to lift 100 lbs. on a rare basis. This position requires frequent climbing, balancing, stooping/crouching, and overhead reaching. This position requires occasional pushing, pulling, kneeling, and crawling. This position will be inside approximately 90% of the time and outside approximately 10% of the time. This position will be frequently exposed to heat, cold, noise and heights.

• This is a safety sensitive position.
• *KCN

What we offer:

Salary: $22 - $48 an hour - Pay is determined based on skills, geographic location, internal equity, market/data analysis, number of years of prior relevant experience, degrees and/or certifications, technical assessment score, etc.

Company Vehicle: Our Service Technicians get a work truck and a gas card to be used for business purposes. Candidates must pass a Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) check.

Benefits: Medical Plan, Dental, Vision, 401k plan with a match from day one, identity theft protection, accident insurance, travel insurance and so much more!

Vacation: 2 weeks of vacation per year (pro-rated for the first year depending on start date). 5-12 years of service, 3 weeks. 13+ years of service, 4 weeks.

Sick Leave: 5 days of Sick Leave per year. Pro-rated the first year after 90 days of service

Holidays: 10 paid holidays per year

That's why, with 16 000+ professionals in over 50 countries, we are trusted every day to lift, handle and move what the world needs.

jobs.title: Clinic Director (Tempe, AZ)
jobs.description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is bringing our intensive outpatient (IOP), partial hospitalization (PHP) and interventional psychiatry services, starting with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), into local communities. As Clinic Director, you will lead day-to-day operations of one clinic and be accountable for the quality of care, the team and the clinic's growth.

You are a licensed clinician (LCSW or PMHNP) who has led clinical operations at a multi-provider practice and wants to build something new. You will supervise a team of clinicians and non-clinical staff, see a reduced caseload of your own (more while the clinic ramps up), and be the on-site lead for crises and escalations. You will partner closely with our clinical, operations, outreach and admissions teams to grow the clinic and shape how Charlie Health delivers in-person care. As we add clinics in your region, this role can grow into oversight of multiple sites.

We're a team of passionate, forward-thinking professionals eager to take on the challenge of the mental health crisis and play a formative role in providing life-saving solutions. If you're inspired by our mission and energized by the opportunity to increase access to mental healthcare and impact millions of lives in a profound way, apply today.

Responsibilities

• Lead day-to-day operations of a single in-person clinic offering IOP, PHP and TMS, including scheduling, staffing coverage, patient flow and facilities

• Supervise and develop junior clinicians and non-clinical staff, including therapists, group facilitators, social workers, TMS technicians and front-desk staff

• Carry a reduced clinical caseload (therapy or medication management, depending on licensure), with more direct patient care while the clinic ramps

• Serve as the on-site lead for patient crises, safety events and escalations, following Charlie Health protocols

• Coordinate care across therapy and psychiatry so each client gets the right level and mix of care

• Own clinic performance against targets for census, utilization, admissions and quality, and report on it regularly

• Partner with outreach and admissions teams to build local referral relationships and grow clinic census

• Maintain compliance with state licensing, payor, documentation and safety requirements, and support site and provider credentialing

• Help hire and onboard clinic staff, and contribute to the playbook for opening future clinics

Requirements

• Master's degree in social work with an active, unrestricted LCSW, or an active, unrestricted PMHNP license, in the state where the clinic is located (or eligibility to obtain one before start)

• Experience leading clinical operations at a practice of roughly 5–10 providers

• Experience in a multi-specialty practice that delivers both therapy and psychiatry required

• Experience with IOP or PHP, or with interventional psychiatry (TMS, ketamine / Spravato), preferred

• Experience supervising clinical and non-clinical staff; eligibility to provide clinical supervision for licensure in your state preferred

• Willingness to carry a reduced caseload and to work on-site full time, with flexibility for crises and clinic needs

• Strong judgment in crisis management and risk assessment

• Work authorized in the United States and native or bilingual English proficiency

• Familiarity with and willingness to use cloud-based communication software—Google Suite, Slack, Zoom, Dropbox, Salesforce—in addition to EMR and survey software on a daily basis

Benefits

Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Our Values

• Connection: Care deeply & inspire hope.

• Congruence: Stay curious & heed the evidence.

• Commitment: Act with urgency & don’t give up.

Please do not call our public clinical admissions line in regard to this or any other job posting.

Please be cautious of potential recruitment fraud. If you are interested in exploring opportunities at Charlie Health, please go directly to our Careers Page: https://www.charliehealth.com/careers/current-openings. Charlie Health will never ask you to pay a fee or download software as part of the interview process with our company. jobs.title: Business Development Specialist - Offshore & Marine
jobs.description:
PURPOSE: The Offshore and Marine Specialist is a direct-sales position responsible for developing and closing business across offshore oil and gas, marine transportation, shipbuilding, government marine, and related markets. The position owns assigned strategic accounts and opportunities, creates demand with end users and specification influencers, and coordinates VEGA resources to convert projects, standards, and installed-base opportunities into orders and sustainable revenue growth.  This position has frequent travel of >50% domestically, and occasionally internationally.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Other duties as assigned by management.

Direct Sales and Business Development

• Own the direct-sales process for assigned offshore and marine accounts and opportunities, from account planning and prospecting through quotation, negotiation, order conversion, and post-sale follow-up.

• Identify, vet, and develop new buying customers and project opportunities in offshore oil and gas, floating production, drilling, marine transportation, shipbuilding, government marine, and related segments.

• Establish and grow relationships with offshore operators, FPSO organizations, drilling contractors, vessel owners, shipyards, EPCs, marine engineering firms, OEMs, package suppliers, integrators, and classification organizations.

• Develop strategic account plans that map customer organizations, decision makers, installed base, competitive position, approved vendor status, current projects, and future potential.

• Prioritize a defined group of high-potential focus accounts and spend the majority of selling time advancing these accounts and opportunities.

• Create demand for VEGA level, pressure, point-level, guided wave radar, and radiometric technologies by connecting customer operating problems to measurable business value.

• Identify and pursue capital projects, brownfield upgrades, fleet standardization opportunities, replacement business, and repeat vessel or platform programs.

• Influence product selection during FEED, detailed engineering, vessel design, and project specification; increase VEGA inclusion on approved vendor lists and written specifications.

• Prepare and deliver compelling technical-commercial presentations, proposals, demonstrations, quotations, and negotiations that clearly differentiate VEGA.

• Coordinate Product Management, Technical Sales, Inside Sales, Field Service, Global Projects, Marketing, and leadership resources required to win strategic business.

• Maintain a prioritized opportunity pipeline with estimated value, competitive position, next actions, influence status, timing, and probability of conversion.

• Consistently use CRM to document customer activity, contacts, quotes, opportunities, project intelligence, specifications, and account strategy.

• Achieve agreed direct-sales metrics, including visits, quotes, orders, units, sales, buying customers, strategic-account penetration, and project/specification wins.

Target Applications

• Three-phase separators, oil/water interface, electrostatic treaters, scrubbers, and other production-separation equipment.

• Produced-water systems, wastewater sumps, open drains, slop tanks, and environmental-compliance applications.

• Flare knockout drums, slug catchers, surge vessels, and other safety-critical process vessels.

• Mud tanks, trip tanks, active mud systems, chemical tanks, cement systems, and drilling-fluid applications.

• Ballast tanks, bilge tanks, fuel tanks, LNG fuel systems, freshwater, greywater, and marine utility systems.

• High-pressure/high-temperature, foam, buildup, emulsion, changing-density, or externally measured applications where radiometric technology can differentiate VEGA.

Geographic and Account Focus

• Primary center of influence: Houston, Texas, including offshore operators, EPCs, drilling contractors, FPSO organizations, service companies, and classification influence.

• Gulf Coast coverage: Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Florida, including vessel owners, service contractors, fabrication yards, shipbuilders, and marine operators.

• National strategic coverage as assigned, including government and commercial shipbuilding centers and offshore or marine accounts with multi-territory impact.

• Travel frequently (>50%) within the United States and occasionally internationally based on customer, project, conference, training, and business-development requirements.

Performance Expectations

• Grow offshore and marine sales, orders, units, buying customers, and qualified opportunity pipeline.

• Generate new buying customers and expand share of wallet within assigned strategic accounts.

• Secure approved vendor additions, written specification wins, and measurable project influence.

• Develop relationships at multiple levels within operator, EPC, shipbuilder, vessel-owner, and engineering organizations.

• Convert large-project, brownfield, fleet, and replacement opportunities into profitable orders.

• Maintain disciplined account plans, opportunity follow-up, forecasting, and CRM documentation.

• Demonstrate effective collaboration with territory sellers and internal resources while retaining clear commercial ownership of assigned accounts and opportunities.

QUALITY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Focus on customer satisfaction through continuous improvement.

• Understand, implement, and maintain the Quality Policy of VEGA Americas.

• Identify and implement corrections to problems and opportunities for improvement, both individually and through teams.

• Follow procedures and work instructions in compliance with ISO 9001.

• As applicable, assure that the product meets drawings and customer requirements.

• Identify and prevent further processing of non-conforming parts or processes.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor's Degree in related field.

• AND five (5) or more years of relevant experience in direct industrial sales, process instrumentation, offshore oil and gas, marine engineering, shipbuilding, EPC/project sales, or a related industrial marketplace

• OR an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Preferred experience includes strategic-account ownership, specification selling, project pursuit, offshore or marine applications, and established relationships in the Houston/Gulf Coast offshore ecosystem.

REQUIRED SKILLS / ABILITIES

• Strong direct-sales, commercial, and technical aptitude with the ability to convert customer problems into orders and long-term account growth.

• Ability to prospect, gain access, qualify opportunities, overcome objections, negotiate, close business, and maintain executive and technical relationships.

• Demonstrated strategic-account planning, project management, presentation, communication, and forecasting skills.

• Ability to lead through influence and coordinate cross-functional resources without direct authority.

• Working knowledge of radar, guided wave radar, pressure, point-level, and radiometric measurement technologies is preferred.

• Ability to work independently, prioritize high-value selling activity, travel extensively, and maintain consistent communication with sales leadership.

COMPUTER SKILLS

• Microsoft Office Products

• Proficient in CRM

• Other company-approved collaboration and business systems.

VEGA Americas manufactures, distributes, and services process instrumentation to measure level, density, weight, and pressure. Our products have been making industrial processes safer and more efficient for over 60 years.

As an employee, you’ll find VEGA Americas commits itself to the highest quality standards and respect for the individual needs of employees, customers, vendors, and shareholders. Don’t take it from us alone, VEGA has been awarded a Cincinnati Enquirer’s Top Workplace Award for 10 years running!

Our Mission: With innovative technologies and services, we develop solutions that inspire. Through our sense of simplicity and our focus on people, we are looking to the future with curiosity. Locally grounded and globally connected, together we give values a home.

Our Values: Curiosity, Humanity, Simplicity, Connectivity

jobs.title: Automation & Controls Specialist (Starship)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

AUTOMATION & CONTROLS SPECIALIST (STARSHIP)

SpaceX's Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket (collectively referred to as Starship) represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Starship will be the world's most powerful launch vehicle ever developed, with the ability to carry in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth orbit.

The Launch Hardware Automation & Controls Specialist role will be hands-on in designing and activating the systems that build and launch Starship. The successful applicant will work as part of a team of elite engineers designing and improving the electrical and control systems across our rocket launch facility at Cape Canaveral Space Force Base.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide innovative solutions to special requirements and challenges faced by the team, which can range from integrating specialized equipment to challenging operating environment, packaging or loading.

• Execute the integration and activation testing of new equipment.

• Manage electrical cabinet builds, field wiring, pneumatic, and fluid plumbing.

• Experience with authoring detailed manufacturing planning work orders.

• Provide hands-on troubleshooting support for a variety of active and critical ground support equipment tooling.

• Write robust and scalable procedures to activate technicians to quickly and reliably build and commission control systems.

• Lay out new industrial electrical control panels that are NFPA79/NEC/UL508A compliant and create electrical, pneumatic, and fluid schematics.

• Participate in the design and development of new and existing control systems critical to the launch organization.

• Architect, write, and debug PLC code, emphasizing generating organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable code for manufacturing applications.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

• 3+ years of experience in a controls technician, controls specialist, or engineering role.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering or technology field.

• Occupational trade school qualification in an instrumentation or electrical-based field

• Knowledge of NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 70E (Standard for Electrical Safety), NFPA 79 & UL508A codes.

• Excellent communication skills—both written and verbal.

• Ability to thrive in ambiguity, independently drive project progress, and manage multiple priorities.

• Proven ability to author detailed manufacturing planning work orders in strict compliance with guidelines and procedures.

• Fundamental understanding of engineering principles behind electronic equipment, instrumentation, and commonly used industrial equipment.

• Experience designing and installing instrumentation and control systems in hazardous areas (NFPA 70 Section 500 installations); Class 1, Division 1 and Division 2 environments or IEC equivalence.

• Electrical schematic CAD experience using EPlan.

• PLC programming experience, preferably Siemens TIA Portal.

• First-hand experience with programming and software development.

• Experience with industrial bus protocols such as Modbus, Profinet and EtherNet/IP.

• Exposure to C/C++, Python, and JavaScript.

• Process integration and electromechanical/mechatronic systems experience.

• Able to collaborate with a wide range of people and effectively work in a team in a high-pressure, dynamic environment.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to work weekends and night shifts as needed.

• Must be willing to travel to other launch sites in support of operational activities and launches; travel requirement is up to 15%.

• Ability to pass Air Force background check for Cape Canaveral.

• Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

jobs.title: Territory Manager (MI, Grand Rapids)
jobs.description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is one of the fastest-growing startups in the healthcare industry, working tirelessly to connect people everywhere to life-saving mental health treatment. Our Outreach team members are the lifeblood of our business; they know our product, partners, and patients better than anyone. In this role, you’ll be joining a team of passionate professionals who are dedicated wholeheartedly to our mission.

You’ll build relationships with clinical partners in your local community and provide much-needed resources to thousands of people struggling with their mental health. You'll be a champion of Charlie Health and ensure that every possible patient, parent, and provider can access our programs. While this work can be challenging, we set the bar high knowing that every decision we make directly impacts our communities.

In your role, you’ll have unparalleled responsibility while collaborating with sharp, spirited, and ambitious coworkers, with room for everyone to excel and grow in their careers. You’ll also receive competitive benefits, ensuring you have the resources to thrive both personally and professionally.

At Charlie Health, we believe in leading with our “why” and connecting with our purpose every day. Join us to find not only a career but a calling.

Responsibilities

• Develop and operationalize GTM strategy for efficient new market penetration

• Create, build, and manage relationships with referral sources across priority markets

• Go in the field 4 - 5 days/week to lead meetings with patients, parents, and providers to uncover needs, address barriers to treatment, and cement community partnerships

• Design strategies to better support and engage referral partners across different channels

• Deepen Charlie Health’s penetration across existing partnerships

• Attend and lead various educational meetings, marketing presentations, and networking events both in person and via conference call

• Synthesize and share market feedback from partners, patients, and stakeholders to inform go-forward marketing and product strategies

• Work closely with internal partners including marketing, product, client success, and legal to deliver on GTM goals

Requirements

• Must be based in Grand Rapids, MI

• Must be fluent in English

• You have 1-4 years proven sales experience - owning & overachieving KPIs is a plus

• Experience working with or selling to healthcare organizations a plus

• Ability to travel locally with reliable transportation & valid drivers license (within ~1 hour driving distance) 4-5 days/week for meetings with potential referral partners

• Ability to energize, advise & persuade senior corporate personnel

• Strong interpersonal, relationship-building and listening skills, with a natural, consultative style

• Strong project management skills, with a demonstrable ability to corral and manage details in a fast-paced, fluid environment

• Experience with Microsoft Office, Salesforce & Zoom is a plus

Benefits

Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Additional Information

The total target base compensation for this role will be between $65,000 and $80,000 per year at the commencement of employment. In addition to base compensation, this role offers an uncapped performance-based bonus. Please note, pay will be determined on an individualized basis and will be impacted by location, experience, expertise, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations. #LI-HYBRID

Our Values

• Connection: Care deeply & inspire hope.

• Congruence: Stay curious & heed the evidence.

• Commitment: Act with urgency & don’t give up.

jobs.title: Director of Field Marketing
jobs.description:
About Us

AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.

The bottleneck now has moved from code generation to security and safety - AI agents write code faster than any team can review it, and over 65% of the lines of code produced by them are insecure. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.

AURI by Endor Labs closes that gap. It runs inside the harness where coding agents work, through hooks, skills and MCP, so the controls sit outside the model and every agent action is visible. Underneath is our patented code context graph, which maps code, open source, containers and infrastructure. It shows which vulnerabilities can actually be reached and exploited, then delivers fixes that won’t break the application. Security teams get evidence instead of noise, and developers get fixes instead of tickets.

The companies building AI trust us to secure it - our customers include OpenAI, SpaceX, DoorDash, Dropbox, Atlassian, MongoDB, Snowflake, Robinhood and Peloton to name a few.

Endor Labs is the third company from Founder & CEO Varun Badhwar, who built Prisma Cloud, the platform that helped define cloud security, from $0 to $300M ARR at Palo Alto Networks. We’ve raised $163M from Lightspeed, Coatue, DFJ Growth, Salesforce Ventures and Dell Technologies Capital.

Software runs everything around our lives today - banking, hospitals, airports and power grids. AI now writes more of it every day, and our mission is to make sure the world can trust that software. Come build that future with us.

The role

The Director of Field Marketing owns how Endor Labs shows up in person, from flagship industry conferences to small, invite-only executive experiences. You will set the field marketing strategy, run the programs that create and accelerate pipeline in every region, and build the team that scales it.

Our buyers are CISOs, AppSec leaders, engineering leaders, and practitioners who are technical, busy, and allergic to marketing. Booth swag and badge scans don't move them. Experiences that respect their time and teach them something do. This role reports to the VP of Marketing and partners closely with Sales leadership, SDRs, Product Marketing, Demand Generation, and Partners.

How You'll Make an Impact

Create experiences that decision makers remember

• Design and run Endor Labs experiences that security and engineering leaders want to attend, from strategic industry events to executive experiences, our customer summit, and partner events.

• Bring our personality into every room: practitioner content, real technical conversations, and a bit of fun.

• Use experiences to build relationships with target accounts, accelerate deals, and turn customers into advocates.

Run a balanced event portfolio

• Strategic events: the major industry conferences where our buyers gather, where Endor Labs shows up with a clear point of view and a full calendar of executive meetings.

• Partner events: co-hosted programs with resellers and technology partners that put us in front of shared customers and prospects.

• Regional events: local programs built with regional sales leaders to reach target accounts and build pipeline in each territory.

• Vertical events: focused programs for industries such as financial services, software and tech, and connected products, with content that speaks to their security and compliance needs.

Drive pipeline

• Own field marketing's contribution to pipeline, with regional programs built alongside sales leadership and partners.

• Plan every program around a clear pipeline goal, and make sure follow-up turns conversations into opportunities.

• Measure what matters, report results to marketing and sales leadership, and invest where programs perform.

Set the strategy and build the team

• Write the field marketing strategy and budget, tied to company pipeline targets.

• Hire and lead a team of field and event marketers, with the playbooks to scale into new regions.

What You Bring to the Table

• 10+ years in B2B marketing, with 6+ years in field or event marketing at a venture-backed or high-growth enterprise software company.

• Experience selling into security or developer audiences. You know the difference between an AppSec leader and a CISO, and how to get each in a room.

• A track record of field programs tied to pipeline, with numbers you can walk us through.

• Experience running flagship conferences (RSAC, Black Hat, re:Invent, or similar) and intimate executive programs alike.

• 3+ years managing people, including hiring and building a team from early stage.

• Strong partnership with sales leadership. Reps should see you as part of their team.

• Fluency with Salesforce, marketing automation, and event platforms, plus comfort owning a seven-figure budget.

• Willingness to travel roughly 20 to 30%.

Why Endor Labs

We're building at the intersection of developer productivity and security — one of the fastest-growing spaces in software. Our dev-loved platform has real ROI, strong momentum, and customers who care about doing things right.

At Endor Labs, we think big, start small, and learn fast. We take ownership, move with purpose, and always start with the customer's success. We debate with data, make the complex simple, and challenge each other with kindness and candor. We celebrate wins, learn from misses, and have fun along the way — because when our customers win, we all win.

Endor Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Even if you don't fit every requirement above, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives and experiences, so we encourage all talented individuals to apply—there's no one-size-fits-all here.

This may include incentives/variable compensations such as commissions, stock options and/or bonuses, depending on the position. Final compensation will vary based on seniority and relevance of experience, location, and position requirements.

jobs.title: Automation & Controls Specialist (Starship) - Night Shift
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

AUTOMATION & CONTROLS SPECIALIST (STARSHIP) - NIGHT SHIFT

SpaceX's Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket (collectively referred to as Starship) represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Starship will be the world's most powerful launch vehicle ever developed, with the ability to carry in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth orbit.

The Launch Hardware Automation & Controls Specialist role will be hands-on in designing and activating the systems that build and launch Starship. The successful applicant will work as part of a team of elite engineers designing and improving the electrical and control systems across our rocket launch facility at Cape Canaveral Space Force Base.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide innovative solutions to special requirements and challenges faced by the team, which can range from integrating specialized equipment to challenging operating environment, packaging or loading.

• Execute the integration and activation testing of new equipment.

• Manage electrical cabinet builds, field wiring, pneumatic, and fluid plumbing.

• Experience with authoring detailed manufacturing planning work orders.

• Provide hands-on troubleshooting support for a variety of active and critical ground support equipment tooling.

• Write robust and scalable procedures to activate technicians to quickly and reliably build and commission control systems.

• Lay out new industrial electrical control panels that are NFPA79/NEC/UL508A compliant and create electrical, pneumatic, and fluid schematics.

• Participate in the design and development of new and existing control systems critical to the launch organization.

• Architect, write, and debug PLC code, emphasizing generating organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable code for manufacturing applications.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

• 3+ years of experience in a controls technician, controls specialist, or engineering role.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering or technology field.

• Occupational trade school qualification in an instrumentation or electrical-based field

• Knowledge of NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 70E (Standard for Electrical Safety), NFPA 79 & UL508A codes.

• Excellent communication skills—both written and verbal.

• Ability to thrive in ambiguity, independently drive project progress, and manage multiple priorities.

• Proven ability to author detailed manufacturing planning work orders in strict compliance with guidelines and procedures.

• Fundamental understanding of engineering principles behind electronic equipment, instrumentation, and commonly used industrial equipment.

• Experience designing and installing instrumentation and control systems in hazardous areas (NFPA 70 Section 500 installations); Class 1, Division 1 and Division 2 environments or IEC equivalence.

• Electrical schematic CAD experience using EPlan.

• PLC programming experience, preferably Siemens TIA Portal.

• First-hand experience with programming and software development.

• Experience with industrial bus protocols such as Modbus, Profinet and EtherNet/IP.

• Exposure to C/C++, Python, and JavaScript.

• Process integration and electromechanical/mechatronic systems experience.

• Able to collaborate with a wide range of people and effectively work in a team in a high-pressure, dynamic environment.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to work weekends and night shifts as needed. Night shift: 6pm-6am, 4 days a week

• Must be willing to travel to other launch sites in support of operational activities and launches; travel requirement is up to 15%.

• Ability to pass Air Force background check for Cape Canaveral.

• Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:
